added.summary: Apply online through the ND DOCR Crime Victim's Compensation Application portal linked from the program page.
added.quote: Clicking the link below will take you to the online application for Crime Victim
added.pinpoint: Program page, Crime Victims Compensation Application and Forms
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Allow 2 to 4 weeks for the program to process an application or a reimbursement request.
added.quote: Please allow 2-4 weeks for processing CVC application or claim reimbursement requests.
added.source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

added.summary: Submit a completed application on the program's form, signed by the claimant or a parent, guardian, or legal representative; an employer, provider, or insurer cannot apply for you.
added.quote: A claimant for benefits shall submit a completed application for compensation signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative on an application form prescribed by the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement in time, explain the reason for the late report in the application.
added.quote: There may be a justifiable reason for the late report. Please explain.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application Tips, Section 3 (Incident Information, continued)
added.source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

added.summary: For medical costs, include a billing statement showing the provider's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for medical services must include a billing statement containing the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For dental costs, include a billing statement showing the dentist's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
added.quote: A request for compensation for dental services must include a billing statement containing the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider's billing statement must list itemized transactions with the provider's name, business address, and phone number.
added.quote: A billing statement of itemized transactions containing the provider's name, business address, and telephone number.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), Verification Requirements
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For counseling, the provider returns the CVC Provider Verification Form with the billing invoice.
added.quote: The Provider Verification Form portion is to be returned with the billing invoice for reimbursement of services to the CVC program.
added.pinpoint: CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025), introduction
added.source_title: ND CVC Mental Health Treatment Policy and Provider Verification Form (Rev. 6/2025)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider and from your employer.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for work loss must include written documentation from a medical or mental health provider, the claimant's employer, and information the division may request that supports payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer you worked for at the time of the crime completes the CVC Employer's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY EMPLOYER YOU WERE WORKING FOR AT THE TIME OF THE CRIME INCIDENT.
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a copy of your federal income tax return for the prior year.
added.quote: Self-employed victims shall provide a copy of federal income tax return for one year prior and other substantial verification of work loss or profits the division determines is necessary to support payment for work loss.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, a medical provider who treated your crime injuries completes the CVC Physician's Report.
added.quote: FORM MUST BE COMPLETED BY A MEDICAL PROVIDER WHO TREATED YOU FOR YOUR CRIME INJURIES.
added.source_title: ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)

added.summary: For travel and lodging, include your receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit receipts for travel and lodging expenses to the division.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For funeral and burial costs, include itemized receipts.
added.quote: The claimant shall submit itemized receipts for reimbursement under this section.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For replacement services, include receipts showing the billed amount and the type of service.
added.quote: A claim for reimbursement for replacement services loss must include receipts for the billed amount, type of service provided, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: For loss of support, include proof of the support the victim gave dependents before the crime, such as tax forms, a certified death certificate, or birth certificates.
added.quote: A claim for loss of support must include verification of the amount of support the victim provided to dependents prior to the criminally injurious conduct.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: Before the program pays, you or the provider must show what insurance or another collateral source paid, or that it did not cover the service.
added.quote: Before payment is made from the division, either the provider or the claimant shall provide documentation that: a. Verifies the amount paid by the collateral source; or b. Verifies the applicant or service was not covered by the collateral source.
added.source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

added.summary: The program may ask you to sign its Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information form so it can get records it needs to decide the claim.
added.quote: The DOCR may, however, require that you authorize disclosure of your health information if needed to make a determination about your claim.
added.pinpoint: Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information, SFN 61353, Privacy Statement
added.source_title: ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

added.title: ND CVC Work Loss - Employer's Report (SFN 12437, Rev. 06-2018)
ND CVC Work Loss - Physician's Report (SFN 60497, Rev. 06-2018)
ND CVC Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information (SFN 61353)

added.summary: Mail the completed, signed application and documentation to the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program, PO Box 94946, Lincoln, NE 68509-4946.
added.quote: Return the completed/signed application and documentation to the below address: Nebraska Crime Victim’s Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Email the claim application and the supporting documentation requested to ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov.
added.quote: Submit, along with supporting documentation requested, by email or mailing to: CVR Claim → ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Reparations program page, Apply
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

added.summary: The application's return-to block also lists the program's fax number, 402.471.2837.
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Include itemized copies of all medical bills related to the incident.
added.quote: Submit itemized copies of all medical bills relating to the incident.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, What must I do to apply for compensation?
added.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

added.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills and any receipts for bills you already paid.
added.quote: Attach copies of crime related bills and any paid receipts.
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Sign and date the Authorization to Release Information; no action is taken on the claim until it is signed.
added.quote: This authorization is an integral part of your application and must be signed and dated by the victim or claimant before any action will be taken on your claim.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Authorization to Release Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Complete the citizenship attestation; if you attest as a qualified alien, you agree to provide a copy of your USCIS documentation.
added.quote: I am a qualified alien under the federal Immigration and Nationality Act and I agree to provide a copy of my USCIS documentation.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), United States Citizenship Attestation
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay periods of work missed because of the incident.
added.quote: Copy of pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay period(s) for missed work as a result of the incident.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages when self-employed, include your most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C and copies of estimates, bids, or contracts.
added.quote: If Self-Employed: submit the most recent federal tax returns including the schedule C form, Copies of Estimates, Bids, and/or Contracts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include a doctor's release back to work.
added.quote: A Doctor’s release back to work.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, a copy of the death certificate is needed.
added.quote: Funeral or Burial Expenses (A copy of the death certificate will need to be provided.)
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: By statute, a hearing officer rules on an application within 180 days after receiving all required information; the clock does not start until the file is complete.
added.quote: A hearing officer shall consider and rule upon any application made under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act within one hundred eighty days after receipt of all required information related to the crime.
added.pinpoint: Claims Process, quoting Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1809(1)
added.source_title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: The program says claims are typically fully processed within 6 to 9 months.
added.quote: CVR program applications take time, typically claims are fully processed within 6-9 months.
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program pamphlet (English)

added.title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
added.quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
added.quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
added.pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
added.quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
added.quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
added.quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
added.quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
added.quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
added.quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
added.quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
added.quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
added.quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
added.quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.
added.quote: Once the program receives your application, you will be contacted by mail or email within 2 weeks.
added.pinpoint: Program page FAQ, How Long Will It Take?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
added.quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.source_title: NJ VCCO Contact page

added.summary: Attach a copy of the police incident report if you have one; otherwise the VCCO requests it.

Attach a copy
of the incident report. If you don't have one, the

prosecutor.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions, Section 4

Include
copies of as much related information (i.e. copies of itemized receipts,

added.summary: Include copies of insurance statements with the application.

Include

added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: For lost wages, supply pay stubs from before the crime and from your return to work.
added.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.

added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: For lost wages, supply a doctor's letter stating the period of disability.
added.quote:
If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: Self-employed applicants claiming lost wages must supply income and business tax returns for the 2 years before the crime.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, you must supply copies of your income tax returns and business tax returns for the last 2 years before the crime.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: The HIPAA release in the application must be completed, signed and dated before the claim can be processed.

This authorization is necessary to obtain information
from your health care providers under federal law.

for the VCCO to process your claim.

added.summary: The VCCO decides on an application within 90 days after it acknowledges receiving the completed application and all supporting information; this can be extended for good cause.

The Office will make its determination regarding the application within 90 days of acknowledgment by the

the turn around time for processing a claim is 3 months of receipt of

added.summary: You can file online through the CVRC application portal, where you sign in or create an account and submit the application.
added.quote: To begin Please choose one of the following options: Sign In OR Create an Account
added.pinpoint: CVRC online application portal, home page
added.source_title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

added.summary: A paper application goes to the Crime Victims Reparation Commission office in Albuquerque; the rules count it as filed on the postmark date.
added.quote: Crime Victims Reparation Commission 6200 Uptown Blvd., Suite 210 Albuquerque, NM 87110
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: A paper application can be faxed to the commission's office.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: The application asks for a copy of the police report if one is available.
added.quote: CRIME INFORMATION (Provide copy of police report if available)
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: The commission reviews the application with a complete offense report or a provider incident verification form, which its office requests.
added.quote: The application and related documentation received, including a complete offense report or provider incident verification form (which this office requests), will then be reviewed to determine if the victim and/or claimant are eligible for compensation.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: Expenses must be documented with invoices, receipts or canceled checks that show who was paid, who paid, the amount, the date and the service.
added.quote: This documentation must provide the name of payee, the name of payer, the amount paid, date of services, and indicate what service was provided. This documentation may include invoices, receipts and canceled checks. Affidavits and letters shall not be considered proper documentation.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer must give a statement of the work dates missed, hourly wage and average weekly hours.
added.quote: a statement from the employer providing: (a) the dates of work missed due to the incident; (b) hourly wage; (c) the average number of hours worked weekly; and (d) any type of compensation received, such as sick leave, annual leave, unemployment, etc.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: For lost wages, a doctor's statement or medical documentation must show the victim is unable to work.
added.quote: a copy of a doctor's statement certifying that the victim is unable to work; or a doctor's statement included in a medical document, or medical documentation showing the inability of the victim to work.
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: Counselors must give commission staff a detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization.
added.quote: All counselors shall provide the commission staff with the following: (a) detailed patient evaluation describing the effect of the victimization
added.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

added.summary: If the victim is deceased, the application asks for a copy of the death certificate.
added.quote: DECEASED (Submit copy of death certificate)
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: If the victim is incapacitated, the application asks for a power of attorney.
added.quote: INCAPACITATED (Submit a power of attorney)
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: The signed Acknowledgement and Authorization page is required for the application to be processed.
added.quote: This authorization is part of your application and must be completed and signed in order to process this application.
added.source_title: NM Crime Victims Reparation Commission Application (English, reviewed 02/2025)

added.summary: An eligibility decision is usually made within 120 days.
added.quote: A decision about whether the victim/claimant is eligible is usually made within 120 days.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, What happens after I send my application?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

added.summary: Mail the completed, signed application to the VOCP office in Las Vegas.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation (English, revised 7/30/2026)

added.summary: If the victim has life, medical, dental, or vision insurance, attach the insurance card.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation (English, revised 7/30/2026)

added.summary: Sign the authorization and release forms that come with the application; all of them are needed to process it.

added.summary: The program needs some document showing the crime occurred, such as a police report, an advocate statement, medical or counseling records, or court papers.

added.source_title: Nevada VOCP Application for Victim of Crime Compensation Instructions and form (2026)

added.summary: Unless the claim is denied at first review, the compensation officer must decide it within 60 days after receiving the application.

added.summary: Include all bills and receipts for the expenses described in the application.

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Include the bills for the crime-related goods and services claimed.

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: Include one completed HIPAA authorization for each medical and mental health provider seen for crime-related care.

added.summary: A police or other criminal justice agency report can be submitted as the crime verification document, but it is a choice.

added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fax the printed and signed claim form to 405/264-5097.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), page 1 header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: The claim form says it can be emailed once printed and signed; the program email is victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us.
added.quote: Website: www.okvictimscomp.com E-mail: victimsservices@dac.state.ok.us
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), instructions header
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Fill out every section of the paper form and sign all three signature areas on page four.
added.quote: Please thoroughly complete ALL sections and sign all three areas of page four.
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: List the injuries from the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.quote: List the injuries suffered as a result of the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section I
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: Send all the bills you have received with the application; bills that arrive later can be added.
added.quote: Please submit all the bills that you have received. If more come in, they can always be added later.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, Do I need to submit all bills with the application?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Out-of-pocket medical, dental, and counseling costs are reimbursed at 100% only with documentation of payment.
added.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: The DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator requests the police report while documenting the claim.
added.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Lost income must be verified by both your employer and your attending physician.
added.quote: Work loss must be verified by the employer and the attending physician.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Income Loss / Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For lost wages, a physician or mental health professional and your employer must verify the disability time.
added.quote: provided the crime prevented the person from working and the disability can be verified by a physician or mental health professional and by the victim’s employer.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section G
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: If you are self-employed, tax returns for the last 3 years are required for lost wages.
added.quote: IF SELF-EMPLOYED, TAX RETURNS FOR THE LAST THREE YEARS WILL BE REQUIRED.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Section G heading
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For mileage to medical or counseling appointments, include documentation from the provider verifying the dates of service.
added.quote: Documentation from the provider verifying the dates of services is required.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Travel
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: To ask for future costs, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect and an explanation.
added.quote: To submit a request for future economic loss, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect to incur, along with an explanation regarding the expense.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For future dental work or surgery, ask the attending physician for a written estimate of the work and the cost.
added.quote: For future dental work or surgery necessary to repair damage from the criminal incident, ask the attending physician to write an accurate estimate which clearly states the work to be performed and the cost.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For traditional American Indian healing or burial services, receipts must note each item's purpose.
added.quote: In order for reimbursement of these expenses, receipts must be provided with the item’s purpose clearly noted on the receipt.
added.pinpoint: Eligible Expenses, Traditional American Indian Services
added.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

added.summary: If you paid the forensic exam bill yourself, the program needs your Social Security number to reimburse you.
added.quote: If the victim/guardian paid the bill out of their own pocket, we will need a Social Security number in order to reimburse them.
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Processing can take anywhere from 4 to 12 months depending on where the crime occurred.
added.quote: Depending on the area in which the crime occurred, the processing time could vary anywhere from 4-12 months
added.pinpoint: FAQ, How Long is the Process?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Once the Victim-Witness Coordinator sends all documentation, claims are generally docketed for decision within 30 days.
added.quote: Claims are generally placed on a docket for decision within 30 days of receipt of all documentation from the Victim-Witness Coordinator.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Payments are generally made within 3 weeks of approval.
added.quote: PAYMENTS are generally made within three weeks of approval.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Sexual Assault Examination Fund payments are usually made within 30 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: Payment is usually made within 30 days of the receipt of the application by the Compensation Program.
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions
DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)
OCVC VCP Online Access claim portal

added.summary: Apply online through the CVC Portal, which also lets you upload documents and check claim status.
added.quote:
You can apply electronically through the Crime Victims’ Compensation Portal at
doj.state.or.us/cvcportal.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Email the completed, signed application to the program.
added.quote: You can also submit your application by email: cvssd@doj.oregon.gov
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Mail the signed paper application to the DOJ Crime Victims' Compensation Program in Salem.
added.quote:
You can mail a paper application to:
Oregon Department of Justice
Crime Victims’ Compensation Program
1162 Court Street NE
Salem, OR 97301–4096
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, How do I apply?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: You can also apply in person through a county District Attorney's victim assistance program or a community-based victim services agency.
added.quote: Apply at your local District Attorney’s Office Victim Assistance Program or local community-based victim services agency.
added.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), How Do I Submit an Application?
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

added.summary: Sign the release in the application so CVC can verify your information; unsigned applications are returned.
added.quote: You must sign this form to allow CVC to verify the information in your application. We will return any unsigned applications.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page 4, Required Release to Process Your Application
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: For lost earnings, provide employer documentation of employment and time lost and your last paystub before the crime.
added.quote: The following information must be provided to CVC: Documentation from your employer to verify employment and time loss. Your paystub just prior to the crime.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you are self-employed and claim lost earnings, submit the previous year's tax records.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, please submit the previous year tax records.
added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you missed more than 2 weeks of work, a work release from your doctor is required.
added.quote: A work release from a doctor is required beyond 2 weeks of missed work.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, Answers to Commonly Asked Questions
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Payment requests must be itemized billing statements listing the services, the provider's name, and the date of service.
added.quote: Requests for payment of crime related expenses shall be submitted in the form of an itemized billing statement detailing the services provided, the provider’s name, the date of service
added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: Insurance EOBs, chart notes, and bills can be combined into one upload in the CVC Portal.
added.quote: EOB’s, chart notes, and bills can all be combined to one document and select bill as the category.
added.pinpoint: Applying for CVC, Crime Victims Portal FAQs, How do I upload documents?
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Applying for Crime Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If CVC pays for a car rental or bus, train, or air fare instead of mileage, it needs a valid receipt.
added.quote: the Department may, at its discretion, reimburse reasonable and necessary round-trip car rental or bus, train, or air fare, upon submission of a valid receipt.
added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: CVC confirms receipt by mail or email and issues a claim number within 2 business days.
added.quote:
We will notify you by mail or email when we receive your application. You will receive a
claim number within 2 business days.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: CVC says it will contact you in 60 to 90 days to tell you whether the application was accepted.
added.quote:
We will contact you again in 60 to 90 days to tell you if we have accepted your
application.
added.pinpoint: CVC Application (2026), page i, What happens next?
added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Mail the completed claim form to VCAP's mailing address, PO Box 1167, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167.
added.quote: Mailing Address PO Box 1167 Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: File the claim online through the DAVE portal (the Crime Victims App also files online).
added.quote: File online at https://www.dave.pa.gov
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Email the completed claim form to VCAP at ra-davesupport@pa.gov.
added.quote: Email ra-davesupport@pa.gov
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized medical bills related to the crime, in the victim's name.
added.quote: Provide all itemized medical bills related to the crime. Medical bills must be in the name of the victim.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.quote: Provide all itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include copies of cancelled checks or receipts for any bills the victim or claimant already paid.
added.quote: Provide copies of cancelled checks and/or receipts for any bills paid by the victim/claimant.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: If insured, submit bills to insurance first and include the insurance statements showing payments or rejections.
added.quote: Provide insurance statements of all payments and/or rejections for corresponding bills.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include two pay stubs from right before the crime, W-2 statements, or the most recent tax return with all schedules.
added.quote: Provide two pay stubs immediately prior to the crime incident, W-2 statements, or most recently filed IRS tax returns including all schedules.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages from crime injuries, a doctor, psychologist, or other listed provider must certify the disability.
added.quote: If filing for loss of earnings due to crime-related injuries a physician verification certifying disability is needed.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include proof of any sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay or other benefits received.
added.quote: Provide documentation of any reimbursements received, such as sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For relocation, include a letter from a human service agency, law enforcement, or a medical provider saying the move is needed for safety and health.
added.quote: Please provide a verification letter explaining that the immediate need for relocation is necessary to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the same household
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Sign the Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information (and the HIPAA release for medical or counseling expenses) before the claim can be processed.
added.quote: The Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information must be signed before a claim can be verified and processed for payment.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Acknowledgement & Reimbursement Agreements section
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: The program says most claims are processed in 12 weeks or less, though each claim differs.
added.quote: Most organizations process claims in 12 weeks or less.
added.pinpoint: PA.gov apply page, FAQ: How long does it take the Program to make a decision?
added.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

added.summary: Once approved, payments owed to the victim or claimant of $5,000 or less are released within 2 business days.
added.quote: Payments owed to the victim/claimant that total $5,000.00 or less are released within 2 business days of being approved.
added.source_title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

added.title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Crime Victim Compensation Program at the Office of the General Treasurer in Warwick.

added.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

added.summary: A printed application can be faxed to the program.
added.quote: You can also print out an application below, either in English or Spanish, and fax it to 401-462-7694
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Program page, how to apply
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

added.summary: Applications can be filed online through the Treasury's CVCP portal; registration is required.
added.quote: Applications can be submitted online here . (registration required)
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Compensation Program page, how to apply (link target http://cvcapp.treasury.ri.gov/)
added.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

added.summary: Include a copy of a valid photo ID with the application.
added.quote: MUST SUBMIT A COPY OF A VALID PHOTO ID
added.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

added.summary: Include copies of the bills for the expenses being claimed.
added.quote: PLEASE SUBMIT COPIES OF BILLS
added.source_title: CVCP Application (English)

added.summary: The application must be signed under penalty of perjury and include a release of information.
added.quote: The application must be signed by the Applicant under the pains and penalties of perjury;
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Where they apply, the applicant must provide lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, and tax returns.
added.quote: Such documentation shall include, where appropriate, all expenses, lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, tax returns, death and birth certificates, and the incident report from the appropriate law enforcement authorities.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Where appropriate, the applicant provides the incident report from law enforcement.
added.quote: Such documentation shall include, where appropriate, all expenses, lost wage verifications, W-2 forms, tax returns, death and birth certificates, and the incident report from the appropriate law enforcement authorities.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: A sexual assault survivor may submit evidence of a Sexual Assault Nurse Examination or other qualifying medical forensic exam.
added.quote: Victims of sexual assault may submit documentary evidence of their Sexual Assault Nurse Examination or other qualifying Medical Forensic Examination consistent with the requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: If the office asks, a victim claiming lost earnings must send a disability letter from a treating physician or mental health provider.
added.quote: Upon request by the office, the victim must submit a disability letter from a treating physician or mental health provider demonstrating that the victim is disabled from working as a direct result of the crime
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

SECTION IX. Other Expenses or Losses as a result of the Crime

added.summary: By statute, information in victims' compensation claim files and records that is covered by a confidentiality privilege under Wyoming law stays confidential and is not open to public inspection. It is also shielded from legal process and cannot be used as evidence in any proceeding without the consent of the person who gave it.
added.quote: Information contained in the claim files and records of victims, which are subject to any privilege of confidentiality under Wyoming law, shall remain confidential and shall not be open to public inspection. rule.summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
rule.quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

rule.summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
rule.quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
rule.quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

rule.summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
rule.quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
rule.quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
rule.quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
rule.quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
rule.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
rule.quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with law enforcement and prosecutors; the commission may deny or reduce an award if they do not.
rule.quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rule.quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
rule.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
rule.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
rule.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
rule.quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

rule.summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.
rule.quote: means actual bodily harm or disfigurement and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy, venereal disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Crimes committed in Idaho qualify. An Idaho resident hurt in another state qualifies only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for.
rule.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs outside the state of Idaho against a resident of the state of Idaho and which occurred in a state which does not have a crime victims compensation program for which the victim is eligible
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rule.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
rule.quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

Idaho Code 19-5703 (Address confidentiality program, application, certification)

params.condition: if you are 16 or older

rule.summary: Police, a hospital, or anyone else may not make a sexual assault survivor age 16 or older pay for the evidence exam, directly or through their health insurance.
rule.quote: A law enforcement agency, health care facility, or other entity may not require a victim of sexual assault under AS 11.41.410 — 11.41.425 who is 16 years of age or older to pay, directly or indirectly, through health insurance or any other means, for the costs of examination of the victim necessary for (1) collecting evidence using the sexual assault examination kit under AS 18.68.010 or otherwise; or (2) determining whether a sexual assault has occurred.
rule.source_title: AS 18.68.010 to 18.68.040, Sexual Assault Examinations (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The Alaska Department of Law tells survivors that sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to them. This page does not address insurance billing; AK-EXAM-1 (the statute) does.

after.summary: The Alaska Department of Law's victims' rights handbook says sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to victims, and cites AS 18.68.040.

rule.summary: The Alaska Department of Law's victims' rights handbook says sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to victims, and cites AS 18.68.040.
rule.quote: Victims of sexual assaults should obtain sexual assault examinations as soon as possible after the crime has occurred. These exams are provided at no cost to victims [AS 18.68.040].
rule.pinpoint: Alaska Department of Law, Victims' Rights Handbook, Crimes of Sexual Assault
rule.source_title: Alaska Department of Law, Victims' Rights Handbook

rule.summary: The most the board can award is $40,000 per victim per incident.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under this chapter in an amount in excess of $40,000 per victim per incident.
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days, or within five days of when a report could reasonably have been made. The statute lists no alternative to a police report for sexual assault.

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

after.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days. If it could not reasonably be reported that soon, it must be reported within five days of when it reasonably could be.

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days. If it could not reasonably be reported that soon, it must be reported within five days of when it reasonably could be.
rule.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense listed in AS 18.67.101 that had been reported to the police within five days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The board may also look at whether the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors where appropriate.

after.summary: The board can pay only if it finds that the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors when that was appropriate.

rule.summary: The board can pay only if it finds that the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors when that was appropriate.
rule.quote: in the discretion of the board, the applicant has cooperated with law enforcement and prosecution officials to further prosecution of the offender if appropriate
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

params.scope: prosecution or conviction, not the police report

rule.summary: An award can be made even if no one is prosecuted or convicted.
rule.quote: An order may be made under this section whether or not a person is prosecuted or convicted of an offense arising out of the act that caused the injury or death involved in the application.
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

rule.summary: A direct victim's initial counseling award covers up to 24 sessions. The first evaluation and intake session is paid in full, and later sessions with a licensed mental health provider are paid up to $200 each. More sessions can be requested with a treatment plan.
rule.quote: Counseling – Direct Victims: Initial maximum award is 24 sessions. Secondary Victims: initial maximum 12 sessions VCCB will pay first evaluation and intake session in full. Payment after first session: $200/session for services provided by a licensed mental health provider
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Benefits at a Glance, Mental Health Therapy, Payment Maximums
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Benefits at a Glance (last revised July 2026)

before.summary: Relocation is covered when the survivor's health or safety is at risk because of the crime.

after.summary: Moving costs can be paid only in some cases, for example when the crime may put your health or safety at risk.

rule.summary: Moving costs can be paid only in some cases, for example when the crime may put your health or safety at risk.
rule.quote: Relocation may only be eligible specific instances, such as when an individuals health or safety may be at risk as a direct result of the crime.
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

params.scope: a cell phone that was damaged or taken as evidence

rule.summary: A cell phone that was damaged or taken as evidence can be covered.

rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application, Claim Application and Instructions, covered expenses
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

rule.summary: The paper application can be mailed to the VCCB office in Anchorage.
rule.quote: You may fill out and send in the application by mail. 4300 Boniface Pkwy Anchorage, AK 99504
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply, Mail
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

rule.summary: The paper application can be faxed to the VCCB.
rule.quote: You may fill out and fax in the application. fax: (907) 465-2379
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, How to Apply, Fax
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

rule.summary: Alaska's new Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Administration, gives an enrolled person a post office box to use as a substitute mailing address and forwards their mail, and state and municipal agencies must accept that address. rule.summary: A sexual assault claim cannot be denied only because no police report was made; medical records, mental health records, or a sexual assault exam can show the crime happened.
rule.quote: An application for a claim based on a sexual assault shall not be denied solely because a police report was not made by the victim. The board shall adopt guidelines that allow it to consider and approve applications for assistance based on a sexual assault relying upon evidence other than a police report to establish that a sexual assault crime has occurred. Factors evidencing that a sexual assault crime has occurred may include, but are not limited to, medical records documenting injuries consistent with allegations of sexual assault, mental health records, or that the victim received a sexual assault examination.

added.summary: Delaware's victim compensation law applies to victims of crimes committed in Delaware, including people who do not live there. That law includes the free forensic exam rule.
added.quote: This chapter shall apply to: (1) All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: You do not need a lawyer before the Appeals Board, but if you have one, the Board may award an amount for the lawyer's services.
added.quote: A claimant need not be represented by an attorney before the Appeals Board, but if such person is represented the Appeals Board may award an amount for services rendered.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: The program may not turn away a claim from sexual assault or abuse of a child because it was filed late.
added.quote: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the Agency may not limit acceptance or consideration of any applications arising from sexual assault or abuse of a child which may have otherwise been barred from consideration by a statute of limitations.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: If the crime happened before your eighteenth birthday, the program may pay for mental health counseling. This holds even if you applied late, did not report to police in time, or did not cooperate with police. The crime must be properly documented, and you must apply before your twentieth birthday.
added.quote: Notwithstanding the provision of paragraph (10) of this section and § 9010(a)(3), (4), and (5) of this title to the contrary, the Agency may make an award for the payment of mental health counseling services under this chapter on a claim made by the victim of a crime that occurred before the victim’s eighteenth birthday so long as the occurrence of the crime is appropriately documented, and the claim is filed before the victim’s twentieth birthday.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: For sexual assault or abuse, that twentieth-birthday limit does not apply.
added.quote: However, the foregoing limitations in this paragraph (11) regarding the victim’s twentieth birthday do not apply in cases of crimes involving sexual assault or abuse.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: If you were a child when the sexual assault or abuse happened, the program cannot deny your claim just because you waited to report or to apply.
added.quote: In no event may the Agency deny any claim solely because the victim was a child victim of sexual assault or abuse, and the victim either delayed reporting the abuse or assault to authorities or the victim delayed an application for services to mitigate the effects of the impact of sexual assault or abuse.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

before.summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must give sexual offense forensic medical exams free of charge, and the survivor pays no out-of-pocket cost and does not have to file a compensation application for the exam. The provider bills the patient's insurance first.

after.summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.

rule.summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.
rule.quote: The victim of the sexual offense shall not pay any out-of-pocket costs associated with the forensic medical examination and shall not be required to file an application with the Agency.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must provide forensic medical exams free of charge to sexual offense victims.
rule.quote: Hospitals and health-care professionals shall provide forensic medical examinations free of charge to the victims of sexual offenses.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

before.summary: The provider must bill the patient's insurance (including Medicaid and Medicare) first; whatever insurance does not cover can be billed to the Victims' Compensation Fund, not the survivor.

after.summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.

rule.summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rule.quote: Any hospital or health-care professional performing a forensic medical examination shall seek reimbursement for the examination from the patient's insurance carrier, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If insurance is unavailable, or does not cover the full costs of the forensic medical examination, the service provider may seek reimbursement from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.exception: or up to $50,000 if you are left fully and permanently disabled

rule.summary: Total compensation is capped at $25,000, or up to $50,000 for victims who are permanently and totally disabled.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under the chapter to a claimant in a total amount in excess of $25,000; provided, however, that the Agency may award compensation to victims who are permanently and totally disabled in an amount not to exceed $50,000.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: replacing items seized as evidence

rule.summary: Replacing items seized as evidence is covered; this is separate from the general bar on property loss.
rule.quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: the deposit plus up to 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider

rule.summary: Child care is covered, limited to the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed provider.
rule.quote: l. Child care not to exceed the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.extension: Agency may grant an extension or waive the deadline when the circumstances make it unreasonable; claims from child sexual assault or abuse may not be barred by a statute of limitations (§ 9009(12))
unless the program gives you more time

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the injury, unless the Agency grants an extension or finds the deadline unreasonable in the circumstances.
rule.quote: Where the claim has not been filed within 1 year after the personal injury on which the claim in based, unless an extension is granted by the Agency or the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances render this requirement unreasonable.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, but this is waived if it was reported to protective services or Family Court, the victim has a protection from abuse order, the victim cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in a sexual assault case, or the Agency finds the requirement unreasonable.
rule.quote: Where the victim has failed to report the crime to a law-enforcement agency within 72 hours of its occurrence. This requirement is waived in any of the following circumstances: a. The crime has been reported to an appropriate governmental agency, such as child or adult protective services or the Family Court. b. The victim can provide a protection from abuse order. c. The victim has cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in cases of crimes involving domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. d. Where the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances of the crime or the victim render this requirement unreasonable.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: A Delaware domiciliary hurt by a crime in another state may apply if the crime would be compensable in Delaware and that state has no eligible program with equal benefits.
rule.quote: A person whose domicile is in Delaware and who is the victim or secondary victim of a crime that occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States may make an application for compensation if both of the following are true: a. The crimes would be compensable had they occurred in Delaware. b. The placement of the crime occurred in states, possessions, or territories of the United States not having eligible crime victim compensation programs that provide benefits equal to the benefits provided under this chapter.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: If VCAP asks for more documentation while investigating, it must be sent within 45 days of the request.
rule.quote: If VCAP, in its investigation of a claim, requires further documentation from the claimant, such documentation must be submitted to VCAP no later than 45 days of the date of VCAP's request.
rule.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

before.summary: Florida's Address Confidentiality Program gives a substitute mailing address to relocated victims of domestic violence (and, by statute, dating violence and stalking), with the Attorney General's office accepting mail and service of process for them. Survivors of sexual assault qualify only when it was domestic or dating violence; there is no general sexual assault eligibility.

after.summary: Florida's Address Confidentiality Program gives relocated victims of domestic violence a substitute mailing address, and the Attorney General's office accepts their mail and legal papers. To ask about it, call (850) 414-3300 and ask for the program.

rule.summary: Florida's Address Confidentiality Program gives relocated victims of domestic violence a substitute mailing address, and the Attorney General's office accepts their mail and legal papers. To ask about it, call (850) 414-3300 and ask for the program.
rule.quote: the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) provides a substitute mailing address for relocated victims of domestic violence, with this office serving as legal agent for receipt of mail and service of process. If you require information regarding the Address Confidentiality Program, please contact the switchboard at (850) 414-3300. Once you call, please request to be connected to the Address Confidentiality Program, and you will be transferred to the appropriate personnel who can assist you further.
