added.summary: Counseling is paid only when a professional licensed or certified by the state provides it.
added.quote: Compensable counseling services are those services rendered by professionals duly licensed or certified by the appropriate state authorities.

rule.summary: A survivor cannot be made to pay, directly or indirectly, for a forensic medical exam; the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund pays, whether or not the survivor reports or cooperates with police.
rule.quote: A victim shall have the right to have a forensic medical examination regardless of whether the victim participates in the criminal justice system or cooperates with law enforcement in pursuing prosecution of the underlying crime. A victim shall not be required to pay, directly or indirectly, for the cost of a forensic medical examination. The cost of a forensic medical examination shall be paid for by the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund, as provided for in Chapter 15 of this title.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-5-72 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.applies_to: exam costs above the $1,000 limit

rule.summary: The program says providers may not bill law enforcement or the patient's insurance for exam costs above the $1,000 limit.
rule.quote: If FME expenses are over $1,000.00, can we bill law enforcement or the patient’s insurance for the difference? No. The maximum allowable amount is $1,000.00 for the collection of evidence for a FME.
rule.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2002, the total award to a claimant cannot exceed $25,000.
rule.quote: with respect to any claim filed with the board as a result of a crime occurring on or after July 1, 2002, no award made under the provisions of this chapter payable to a claimant sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of a victim shall exceed $25,000.00 in the aggregate
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Medical and dental bills, including prescriptions and copays, are covered up to $15,000.
rule.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Dental expenses are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.
rule.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Prescriptions and copays are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.

rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Mental health counseling is covered up to $3,000; itemized counseling bills must be submitted.
rule.quote: Mental Health Counseling Up to $3,000 Submit copies of any itemized counseling bills related to the victimization.

rule.summary: Crime scene sanitization by a trained company is covered up to $1,500.
rule.quote: Crime Scene Sanitization Up to $1,500 Submit an itemized bill from a company trained in crime scene and biohazard clean-up.
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: No award is made for loss of property, so items like a damaged or taken phone are not reimbursed.
rule.quote: No award of any kind shall be made under this chapter to a victim of a crime for loss of property.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-7 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.extension: The board may extend the time for good cause shown.
or later if the board extends it for good cause

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the crime, and the board may extend that for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim shall be filed by a victim not later than three years after the occurrence of the crime upon which such claim is based or not later than three years after the death of the victim; provided, however, that if such victim was a minor at the time of the commission of the crime, he or she shall have until three years after his or her eighteenth birthday to file such claim; and provided, further, that upon good cause shown, the board may extend the time for filing a claim.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-5 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: By statute, no award is made if records show the crime was reported more than 72 hours after it happened, unless the board finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: In no case may an award be made where the police records, records of an investigating agency, or records created pursuant to a mandatory reporting requirement show that such report was made more than 72 hours after the occurrence of such crime unless the board, for good cause shown, finds the delay to have been justified
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

before.summary: An award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources such as workers' compensation; gifts from family or charitable donations do not count.

after.summary: By statute, an award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources, such as workers' compensation, but gifts from family members or charitable donations do not count.

rule.summary: By statute, an award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources, such as workers' compensation, but gifts from family members or charitable donations do not count.
rule.quote: Any award made pursuant to this chapter may be reduced by or set off by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury, serious mental or emotional trauma: (1) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; and (2) From any other private or public source, including an award of workers’ compensation pursuant to the laws of this state, provided that private sources shall not include contributions received from family members or persons or private organizations making charitable donations to a claimant.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

before.summary: A sexual assault victim who is not the primary policyholder may opt out of giving insurance information by checking the opt-out box on the application.

after.summary: The application's instructions say that if you are a victim of sexual assault and are not the main policyholder, you may opt out of giving insurance information for this incident.

rule.summary: The application's instructions say that if you are a victim of sexual assault and are not the main policyholder, you may opt out of giving insurance information for this incident.
rule.quote: If you are not the primary policyholder and are a victim of sexual assault or family violence, you may opt out of providing insurance information for this incident by checking the opt-out box in Section 6 of the application.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rule.summary: The program lists sexual offenses among its most common compensable crimes.
rule.quote: Most Common Compensable Crimes Child Molestation Cruelty to Children Child Abuse Human Trafficking Sexual Offenses
rule.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation program page

rule.summary: A covered crime includes an act in Georgia, or for a Georgia resident, an act in a state with no compensation program or a state that paid less than Georgia would.
rule.quote: An act which is committed in this state; in a state which does not have a victims’ compensation program, if the claimant is a resident of this state; or in a state which has compensated the claimant in an amount less than the claimant would be entitled to pursuant to this chapter, if the claimant is a resident of this state
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-2 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

before.summary: Georgia's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other eligible people a designated substitute address for public records, forwards their mail, and seals their address on voter rolls.

after.summary: Georgia's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, helps survivors of sexual assault and others whose safety may be at risk if their home address is made public.

rule.summary: Georgia's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, helps survivors of sexual assault and others whose safety may be at risk if their home address is made public.
rule.quote: The Georgia Safe at Home Program is an address confidentiality program that helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other eligible individuals whose safety may be compromised by public disclosure of their residential address.
rule.source_title: Georgia Secretary of State: Safe At Home

added.summary: When a licensed professional gives a child victim emergency or short-term medical care under the state's child victim services law, the professional files the claim. That claim does not need a police report.
added.quote: When immediate or short-term medical services to a victim are provided pursuant to section 915.35 by a professional licensed or certified by the state to provide such services, the professional shall file the claim for compensation, unless the department of health and human services is required to file the claim under this section. The requirement to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department under subsection 3 does not apply to this subsection.
added.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

added.summary: A child or dependent adult who was sexually abused by a caregiver does not need a police report. The abuse must have been reported to the state health and human services department, and the department must verify the report.
added.quote: a victim under the age of eighteen or dependent adult as defined in section 235B.2 who has been sexually abused or subjected to any other unlawful sexual conduct under chapter 709 or 726 or who has been the subject of a forcible felony is not required to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department to be eligible for compensation if the crime was allegedly committed upon a child by a person responsible for the care of a child, as defined in section 232.68, subsection 8, or upon a dependent adult by a caretaker as defined in section 235B.2, and was reported to an employee
added.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

added.summary: The victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation or prosecution of the crime.
added.quote: The victim shall cooperate with reasonable requests by the appropriate law enforcement agencies in the investigation or prosecution of the crime.
added.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: After the exam program pays, the provider may not send the survivor a bill for any leftover balance.
rule.quote: A medical provider must not submit any remaining balance to the sexual abuse victim after the sexual abuse examination program has determined payment.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: Glasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetics, wheelchairs, and medication taken, lost, or destroyed in the crime can be replaced.
rule.quote: Compensation may be paid for the replacement of a medical device including but not limited to a sight or hearing device, dentures, a prosthetic device, a wheelchair, and medication that was taken, lost or destroyed during the crime.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: Lost wages are figured from gross pay for scheduled hours missed, then reduced by 25 percent.
rule.quote: Lost wages are computed as the gross rate of pay multiplied by the number of scheduled hours of work missed, decreased by 25 percent
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: To count as emergency relocation, the move must happen within 30 days of the crime, its discovery, or when it could reasonably be reported, or within 30 days before or after the offender's release from incarceration.
rule.quote: "Emergency relocation" means a relocation that takes place within thirty days of the date of a crime or the discovery of a crime, or within thirty days after a crime could reasonably be reported. "Emergency relocation" also includes a relocation that takes place within the thirty days before or after an offender related to the crime is released from incarceration.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.scope: clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement

rule.summary: Clothing and bedding held as evidence by police can be paid for.
rule.quote: Compensation may be paid for clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

before.summary: Lost or damaged property (for example a phone or other belongings) is not paid, nor are legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.

after.summary: The program does not pay for property loss or repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for property loss or repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rule.quote: The program cannot pay for property loss, property repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rule.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rule.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

before.summary: Pregnancy care for the victim is covered, but care for a newborn child is not.

after.summary: The program does not pay for the care of a newborn child.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for the care of a newborn child.
rule.quote: Expenses incurred for the care of a newborn child are not compensable.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.extension: Two years may run from discovery of the crime; the department may waive the limit for good cause (61 IAC 9.28(2) lists age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, and health or safety reasons).
or later if the crime was discovered later or you show good cause

rule.summary: Apply within two years of the crime or its discovery. The program can waive the deadline for good cause.
rule.quote: file the application with the department within two years after the date of the crime, the discovery of the crime, or the date of death of the victim. The department may waive the time limitation if good cause is shown.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.exception: or within 72 hours of when you reasonably could, and the program may waive this for good cause

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police or the sheriff within 72 hours, or within 72 hours of when a report could reasonably be made. The program may waive this for good cause.
rule.quote: A person is not eligible for compensation unless the crime was reported to the local police department or county sheriff department within seventy-two hours of its occurrence. If the crime cannot reasonably be reported within that time period, the crime shall have been reported within seventy-two hours of the time a report can reasonably be made. The department may waive this requirement if good cause is shown.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: For sexual abuse, the 72-hour police report rule may be waived for good cause if a forensic exam was done within 72 hours or the survivor told a medical provider, mental health professional, or victim service provider.
rule.quote: For a victim of sexual abuse, the 72-hour reporting requirement may be waived for good cause if a sexual abuse evidentiary examination was completed within 72 hours of the crime or if the crime was disclosed to another provider including but not limited to a licensed medical provider, a licensed mental health professional, or a designated victim service provider.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

before.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further (see the next residency rule).

after.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if the act would be covered had it happened in Iowa and that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further.

rule.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if the act would be covered had it happened in Iowa and that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further.
rule.quote: To a victim of an act committed outside this state who is a resident of this state, if the act would be compensable had it occurred within this state and the act occurred in a state that does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: Send the paper application and signed forms to the Victim Assistance Section at the Hoover Building in Des Moines.
rule.quote: Office of the Attorney General of Iowa Victim Assistance Section Hoover Building, First Floor 1305 E Walnut Street Des Moines, Iowa 50319
rule.source_title: Iowa Crime Victim Compensation Application portal home page (ccvcia.org)

before.summary: Iowa's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, trafficking, stalking, and assault a substitute address and mail forwarding so their real address stays off public records. It also offers confidential voter registration and absentee voting.

after.summary: Iowa's Safe at Home program gives participants a substitute address. Its page lists survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, and assault.

rule.summary: Iowa's Safe at Home program gives participants a substitute address. Its page lists survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, and assault.
rule.quote: Safe at Home is an address confidentiality program that provides participants with a substitute address. Who Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, trafficking, stalking, and assault.

before.summary: Confidential information the compensation program collects to process a claim, such as medical and counseling records that are confidential under Iowa's public records law, stays confidential in the program's hands. after.summary: Records that Iowa's public records law already keeps confidential, and information taken from them, stay confidential when the program gets them.

rule.summary: Records that Iowa's public records law already keeps confidential, and information taken from them, stay confidential when the program gets them.
rule.quote: Information and records which are confidential under section 22.7 and information or records received from the confidential information or records remain confidential under this section.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. params.exception: or later if the commission finds good cause for the delay

before.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with law enforcement and prosecutors; the commission may deny or reduce an award if they do not.

rule.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).

rule.summary: A hospital or other provider giving a sexual assault survivor a medical forensic exam, medical care and treatment, transportation, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of those costs, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, or denied claims.
rule.quote: shall not: (1) charge or submit a bill for any portion of the costs of the services, transportation, or medications to the sexual assault survivor, including any insurance deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim by an insurer, spenddown, or any other out-of-pocket expense

after.summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances.

before.summary: Kentucky's Safe at Home Program, run by the Secretary of State, protects victims of sexual assault, rape, other sexual crimes, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking by letting them use a designated address instead of their real one. It also covers their minor children and anyone living with them, and it is free for Kentucky residents who are U.S. citizens.

after.quote: The Safe at Home Program is hereby established within the Office of the Secretary of State. The Safe at Home Program shall be operated with the intent to protect victims of: (a) Domestic violence; (b) Human trafficking; (c) Stalking; (d) Sexual assault; (e) Rape; and (f) Other sexual crimes as defined by KRS 17.500. The Safe at Home Program shall authorize the use of designated addresses for victims, their minor children, and all other individuals residing with the victim. The Safe at Home Program shall be open to victims of a specified offense who are United States citizens and residents of Kentucky, without any cost to the program participant.

added.summary: If the victim was a minor and a criminal complaint or indictment came after the victim turned 18, the time to file starts on the date it was issued.
added.quote: If the victim was a minor when the crime was committed and the crime results in the issuance of a criminal complaint or indictment after the victim's 18th birthday, the filing period shall not commence until the date of issuance of the criminal complaint or indictment provided, however, that this exception shall not apply to claims based on the death of a minor victim.

added.summary: To get compensation, the claimant must cooperate with law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. This does not apply if the claimant shows a reasonable excuse for not cooperating.
added.quote: A claimant shall be eligible for compensation only if such claimant cooperates with law enforcement authorities in the investigation and prosecution of the crime in which the victim was injured or killed unless the claimant demonstrates that he possesses or possessed a reasonable excuse for failing to cooperate.

added.summary: The program may accept the physical or psychological effects of the crime as a reasonable excuse for not cooperating. A reasonable fear for the safety of the claimant or others can count too.

before.summary: If the claimant did not discover the crime until more than three years after it happened, the period starts at discovery, but only if there was a criminal complaint, indictment or other probable cause finding.

rule.summary: The Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of the Commonwealth, protects survivors of sexual assault, rape, domestic violence and stalking who move to get away from the person who hurt them. rule.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) protects survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, rape, and stalking as well as some legally protected healthcare providers. The ACP is a mail forwarding service that gives you a protected address to use with state and municipal agencies.

rule.summary: A police report is one kind of evidence the Board must accept. It is not the only one. The Board must also accept medical records showing an injury that fits the crime. It must accept a sworn statement from a qualified third party, and a peace order or protective order. It must also accept any other evidence it thinks helps prove what happened.

params.scope: what counts as good cause for a late report

rule.summary: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking can apply to New Hampshire's Address Confidentiality Program if they meet its eligibility guidelines.

rule.summary: A health care provider may not charge the survivor, directly or indirectly, for the costs of collecting a sexual assault examination kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.

rule.summary: Under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, the state administrator must provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes, arrange free exams, or reimburse victims for the exam cost.

rule.summary: If the victim is reimbursed for the exam instead of getting it free, reimbursement covers the full cost with no deductible or limit, and the victim can apply for reimbursement for one year from the exam date.
rule.quote: the reimbursement covers the full cost of the forensic medical exam, without any deductible requirement or limit on the amount of the reimbursement; (2) the victim of a sexual crime is entitled to apply for reimbursement for a period of one year from the date of the forensic medical exam

params.exception: or up to $30,000 more if an injury leaves you fully disabled for life

rule.summary: The maximum award is $20,000 per victim. The commission may add up to $30,000 more for extraordinary losses when the injury is catastrophic and causes permanent total disability.
rule.quote: No award of reparation shall be in excess of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per victim, except that the commission may award up to an additional thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for extraordinary pecuniary losses, if the personal injury to a victim is catastrophic and results in a permanent total disability.
rule.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

params.item: eyeglasses or contact lenses

params.item: Native American medicine man treatment

rule.summary: Native American medicine man treatment fees can be considered, up to $3,000 per application unless the board approves more in advance.
rule.quote: In all cases of medicine man care, the commission board shall only approve up to $3,000.00 per application unless prior approval has been granted by the commission board for additional treatment.
rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.summary: The program lists medical and dental care and mental health counseling (30 session maximum) as types of reparation.

rule.summary: Lost wages can be paid for a recovery period of up to 14 calendar days after the crime without a physician's certification. The person must have been employed at the time of the incident.
rule.quote: Loss of wages may be paid to the victim, claimant, and/or, in the case of a minor victim, guardian, for up to fourteen calendar days after the crime for a recovery period.
rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.scope: gas for trips over 30 miles one way to a health provider

rule.summary: Gas to get to a health provider can be reimbursed at 20 cents per mile when the trip is over 30 miles one way from home.
rule.quote: Gas expenses to transport the victim to a health provider may be considered if the travel is over thirty miles one way from the victim's residence. This travel shall be verified by the health provider's billing and reports for the travel requested. The gas will be reimbursed at the rate of twenty cents per mile.
rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.summary: The program lists medical and dental care among the expenses it can pay.

params.scope: gas for trips over 30 miles one way from home, at 20 cents a mile

rule.quote: The distance traveled shall be more than thirty miles one way from the victim's residence and the gas will be reimbursed at the rate of twenty cents per mile.
rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.summary: The program does not pay for property loss, pain and suffering, or attorney's fees.

rule.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

rule.quote: The following expenses shall not be considered for reimbursement: (1) phone bills; (2) copying fees; (3) postage costs.
rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

before.summary: Nevada's Confidential Address Program, run by the Division of Child and Family Services, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking a fictitious address to use instead of their home, work, or school address, and forwards their mail for free. after.summary: Nevada's Confidential Address Program, run by the Division of Child and Family Services, helps victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, or stalking keep the person who hurt them from finding them through public records. If your application is approved, you get a fictitious address to use instead of your home, work, or school address, and the program forwards your mail at no cost. To apply, you need specific evidence that you were a victim, and you apply in person through a CAP Certified Advocate, not directly with the program.

rule.summary: Nevada's Confidential Address Program, run by the Division of Child and Family Services, helps victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, or stalking keep the person who hurt them from finding them through public records. If your application is approved, you get a fictitious address to use instead of your home, work, or school address, and the program forwards your mail at no cost. rule.quote: The Nevada Confidential Address Program (CAP) is a program that helps victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking and/or stalking from being located by the perpetrator through public records. rule.quote: In the case of medically necessary life-sustaining equipment which was lost or damaged as the direct result of a crime, the award shall be limited to the amount of ten thousand dollars.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

outerwear, suits and footwear

clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear

bedding other than mattress and box spring

params.extension: Runs from the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend for good cause, and must extend if the claimant got no notice of the program and did not know they were eligible.
or of when the crime was discovered, or later if OVS finds good cause

rule.summary: File within 3 years of the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence or discovery of the crime upon which such claim is based, three years after a court finds a lawsuit to be frivolous, or not later than three years after the death of the victim, provided, however, that upon good cause shown, the office may extend the time for filing.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 625 (Filing of claims)

before.summary: A police report is not required: the crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime (such as a forensic exam facility or protective services agency) can show this instead of police records. No fixed reporting window appears in the statute.

after.summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.

rule.summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.
rule.quote: the records of a support agency for survivors of crime or the records of a criminal justice agency show that such crime was reported.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: A medical facility that provides forensic exams for rape and sexual assault counts as a support agency, so its records can stand in for a police report.
rule.quote: any medical facility established under the laws of the state that provides a forensic physical examination for victims of rape and sexual assault
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, mandated insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, and any emergency award.
rule.quote: Any award made pursuant to this article shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) under insurance programs mandated by law, (c) from public funds, (d) under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary, (e) as an emergency award pursuant to section six hundred thirty of this article.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

before.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam is an exception (see the exam rules).

after.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.

rule.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.
rule.quote: OVS is the payer of last resort and can only consider your out-of-pocket loss. OVS can only process payments for crime-related expenses. You must bill your insurance company or benefits plan before OVS can pay.
rule.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

rule.summary: OVS considers whether the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury and can reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rule.quote: the office shall determine whether, because of such victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of such victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Acts committed in New York count as crimes for compensation whether or not anyone was arrested, charged, or prosecuted, and whether or not the claimant dealt with police.
rule.quote: an act committed in New York state which would, if committed by a mentally competent criminally responsible adult, who has no legal exemption or defense, constitute a crime as defined in and proscribed by law, regardless of whether any suspect was arrested, charged, apprehended or prosecuted for the commission of the act or whether the claimant has interacted with a criminal justice agency investigating such act
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

rule.summary: OVS records and proceedings on a victim's or claimant's compensation claim are confidential and are not shared with government or private entities, except for listed purposes such as criminal justice requests, judicial subpoenas, the claimant's own requests, and program administration.
rule.quote: Records maintained by the office and proceedings by the office based thereon regarding a claim submitted by a victim or a claimant shall be deemed confidential and shall not be shared with any government or private entity, with the following exceptions:
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 633 (Confidentiality of records)

added.quote: There are cases in which evidence should be collected beyond 96 hours. Examples include where the patient was unconscious or sedentary or where an exam may corroborate chronic injury or excessive force related to the sexual assault. Documentation must clearly justify the reasoning for the forensic collection as it relates to the sexual assault. Documentation does not guarantee payment by the SAFE Program.

added.summary: The Attorney General's billing instructions say Ohio law has health care providers report a sexual assault to police even when the patient does not want to talk to police. If an adult patient stays unnamed, the provider gives police the date, time, and general location of the assault, but not the patient's name or other identifying details.
added.quote: Law enforcement reporting – Ohio Revised Code (ORC) 2921.22 (A) & (B) (see page 7) requires health care providers report a sexual assault to law enforcement whether a patient chooses to speak with law enforcement or not. If the adult patient chooses to remain unnamed, the provider is mandated to provide the date, time, and general location the assault took place, but not the patient’s name or other identifiers.

added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

rule.summary: An award can be reduced or denied for contributory misconduct, which the statute defines narrowly as unlawful or intentionally tortious conduct at the time of the crime that caused or threatened serious harm and provoked the crime.

rule.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours after the assault is found to have fully cooperated.
rule.quote: Victims of sexual assault who undergo a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after the sexual assault shall be found to have fully cooperated.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

added.summary: The SAVE Fund law counts you as a victim only if the sexual assault happened in Oregon.
added.quote: “Victim” means a person who has experienced an incident of sexual assault as defined in ORS 181A.323 that occurred in this state.
added.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rule.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund for a sexual assault medical assessment may not bill the survivor for it, unless the Fund lacks money or declines to pay. The statute does not address billing the survivor's insurance; the SAVE Fund rule does, and it bars billing insurance too.
rule.quote: A provider who submits a bill under this subsection may not bill the victim for the medical assessment except to the extent that the department is unable to pay the bill due to lack of funds or declines to pay the bill.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rule.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurance for the exam, evidence collection, or other services given with the exam (exceptions: the Fund lacks money or declines to pay for reasons other than a late or incomplete bill).
rule.quote: An eligible medical services provider (including subcontractor or other designee) who submits a bill to the Fund under these rules may not bill the victim or the victim's insurance carrier for a medical examination, collection of forensic evidence using the Oregon State Police SAFE Kit, or other services provided in conjunction with the sexual assault exam
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: The Oregon Department of Justice pays for a sexual assault medical assessment through the SAVE Fund, subject to available funds and the time frame set by rule.
rule.quote: Subject to the availability of funds from gifts, grants and donations in the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund, the Department of Justice shall pay the costs of a medical assessment obtained by a victim if the victim obtains the medical assessment within the time frame established in rules adopted by the department.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: A survivor can get a SAVE Fund paid medical assessment without reporting the assault to police.

after.summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.

rule.summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.
rule.quote: A victim may obtain a medical assessment and complete and submit a form under this section regardless of whether the victim reports the sexual assault to a law enforcement agency.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Medical and hospital expenses, including counseling and medications, are covered up to $20,000 combined.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: The victim's counseling counts toward the same $20,000 limit as medical and hospital expenses.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are paid at up to $600 per week.
rule.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are capped at $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are figured at 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the crime.
rule.quote: Compensation for lost earnings under ORS 147.035(2)(b) shall be computed on the basis of 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the compensable crime.
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rule.summary: A parent or guardian who misses work to care for a minor victim can get up to $5,000 in lost earnings.
rule.quote: Loss of earnings for the parent or guardian are compensable up to a maximum of $5,000.00 under the child victim's claim under ORS 147.035 (2)(f).
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rule.summary: Travel for the victim's covered medical care or counseling is paid up to $3,000, only when the care is more than 30 miles from home and adequate care is not available closer.
rule.quote: Expenses related to transportation for the victim's medical care or counseling, at a rate determined by the Department of Justice, up to a maximum amount of $3,000, when: (A) The medical care or counseling is compensable under this section; (B) The medical care or counseling is provided more than 30 miles away from the victim's residence; and (C) Adequate medical care or counseling is not available in closer proximity to the victim's residence.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.scope: mileage to medical and mental health treatment

rule.summary: Mileage to medical and mental health treatment is reimbursed at 50 cents per mile, up to $3,000.
rule.quote: Reimbursement of mileage (50¢ per mile) for travel to medical and mental health treatment, up to $3,000.
rule.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), What Does CVC Pay For?
rule.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rule.summary: Rehabilitation expenses, such as physical therapy, are covered up to $4,000.
rule.quote: The victim's rehabilitation expenses, up to a maximum amount of $4,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.extension: good cause shown, at the department's discretion
or later if the department gives you more time for good cause

rule.summary: The application must be filed within one year of the injury, or later if the department allows an extension for good cause.
rule.quote: Within one year of the date of the injury to the victim; or (B) Within such further extension of time as the department, for good cause shown, allows.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Good cause for filing after one year includes not knowing about the program, police not giving the required information, or trauma that got in the way of filing on time.
rule.quote: "Good cause" for failure to file an application for compensation within one year of the date of the crime as required by ORS 147.015(1)(e) includes but is not limited to the victim's lack of knowledge of the Crime Victims' Compensation Program, failure of a law enforcement official to provide information to the victim as required by ORS 147.365(1), or emotional or physical trauma sustained by the victim that was a barrier to timely filing the application for compensation.
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

before.summary: The reporting requirement is also met by a sexual assault medical assessment or other forensic exam, or a health or mental health provider certifying the victim reported to them, or other documentation the department accepts.

after.summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.

rule.summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.
rule.quote: (E) A medical assessment, as defined in ORS 147.395, for sexual assault, or any other forensic exam or medical assessment; (b) A health provider, tribal health provider, student health provider or community mental health provider certifies that the victim reported the crime to the provider; or (c) The victim provides to the department documentation that qualifies as law enforcement notification under the rules of the department.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source the victim received or is entitled to.

after.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.

rule.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.
rule.quote: shall deduct the amount of benefits, payments or awards that are payable under the Workers' Compensation Law, from local governmental, state or federal funds or from any source, and that the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim have received or to which the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim are entitled as a result of the death or injury of the victim
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Eligibility depends on the department finding the victim acted reasonably given the victim's specific situation. Shown for information only.
rule.quote: The department determines that the victim acted reasonably with respect to the incident causing the death or injury to the victim, taking into account the specific situation of the victim and what a reasonable action would be for a person in the victim's circumstances
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Injury includes mental or emotional harm and pregnancy, not only physical harm.
rule.quote: "Injury" means abuse of a corpse, actual bodily harm, mental or emotional harm and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy and mental or nervous shock.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state can apply in Oregon only if that state has no reciprocal compensation program; otherwise the state where the crime happened pays.

after.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state that has no reciprocal crime victims' compensation program can apply in Oregon.

rule.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state that has no reciprocal crime victims' compensation program can apply in Oregon.
rule.quote: Who is an Oregon resident killed or injured as a result of a compensable crime perpetrated or attempted against the person in a state, within the United States, without a reciprocal crime victims' compensation program
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

added.summary: For the program to pay for the exam, the hospital must notify the local police where the assault happened within 12 hours of collecting the evidence.
added.quote: In order for payments to be considered, hospitals or licensed health care providers requesting reimbursement of costs associated with a forensic rape examination are required to notify the local law enforcement agency where the reported sexual assault occurred within 12 hours of collection of the sexual assault evidence as per the Sexual Assault Testing and Evidence Collection Act (Act 165 of 2006).
added.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
added.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

added.summary: Adults 18 or older can choose an anonymous report when evidence is collected, if they are worried about the kit going to police. A minor's exam cannot be done anonymously.
added.quote: Adult victims (age 18 or older) have the option of anonymous reporting and gathering of evidence and may consider this option if they have concerns about the kit being provided to police. An exam cannot be completed anonymously for a minor.
added.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

added.summary: A helper who is not a family member is paid at most $8 an hour. A family member who does the work is paid their own lost earnings, up to the average weekly wage.
added.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation. (i) Members of the family of the direct victim or intervenor engaged to perform the services will be paid their net loss of earnings not to exceed the average weekly wage and if not otherwise reimbursed for the loss of earnings. (ii) Individuals engaged to perform services who are not family members will be paid a maximum hourly rate of $8.
added.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: The program's page says the 5-year limit is for crimes on or after 9/8/2022. For an older crime, it asks you to contact the program to find out the filing rules.
added.quote: For crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, the claim must be filed within 5 years of the crime. For crimes occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the Program to determine filing requirements.
added.pinpoint: PA.gov Apply for Victims' Compensation page, Who is eligible?
added.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

added.summary: Claims for counseling related to sexual abuse are an exception to the filing deadline.
added.quote: (2) Exceptions shall be as follows: (i) ((i) deleted by amendment). (i.1) Claims for counseling services related to sexual abuse under section 701.1.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the abuser was a parent, a caretaker, someone living in the same home, or a parent's partner, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21. It then runs until the later of the criminal time limit for the crime or the usual deadline.
added.quote: If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the alleged offender is the direct victim's parent or a person responsible for the direct victim's welfare, an individual residing in the same home as the direct victim or a paramour of the direct victim's parent, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age. (B) The limitation period shall run until the later of: (I) the end of the limitation period for the offense as set forth in 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 55 Subch. C (relating to criminal proceedings); or (II) the end of the limitation period under paragraph (1).
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the claim is only for counseling, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21.
added.quote: (ii.1) If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the direct victim is seeking reimbursement for counseling services only, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The Office of Victims' Services may accept a late claim for good cause, such as when the victim was incapacitated or a minor, feared retaliation, or the crime was not readily apparent.
added.quote: (iii.1) The Office of Victims' Services may find good cause to accept a claim beyond the limitation period under paragraph (1) if one of the following circumstances existed at the time of the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the occurrence of the crime: (A) The direct victim, intervenor or claimant was mentally or physically incapacitated. (B) The victim was a minor. (C) There was a fear of retaliation. (D) The occurrence of the crime was not readily apparent. (E) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The program's manual says the filing, reporting, and minimum loss rules are different for a crime before 9/8/2022, and asks you to contact the program about them.
added.quote: For eligibility requirements for crime occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the program as there are different filing requirement, reporting requirement, and minimum loss requirements.
added.pinpoint: VCAP Manual for Compensation Assistance, Eligibility
added.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

added.summary: If you start a protection order case to meet the report rule and then drop it, you cannot get an award unless the program finds you had good reason to drop it.
added.quote: An award may not be made if the record shows that the petition was withdrawn, except if the Office of Victims' Services finds the withdrawal to have been justified, consistent with regulations of the Office of Victims' Services.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: For a standard claim, the survivor must also have fully cooperated with law enforcement and the program, unless the program finds there was a good reason not to.
added.quote: The direct victim, intervenor or claimant has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and the Office of Victims' Services, unless the Office of Victims' Services finds the noncompliance to have been justified consistent with the Office of Victims' Services regulations.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The program may excuse not cooperating if the survivor was incapacitated, feared retaliation, was a minor, or shows other good cause.
added.quote: OVS may consider a failure to cooperate with law enforcement and OVS to be justified when one of the following circumstances exist: (1) The direct victim, intervenor or the claimant is mentally or physically incapacitated. (2) There is a fear of retaliation. (3) The victim is a minor. (4) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
added.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

before.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor. Insurance is billed first unless the survivor asks that it not be.

after.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.

rule.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.
rule.quote: The cost of a forensic rape examination and the cost of medications prescribed to the direct victim shall not be charged to the victim.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rule.summary: If the program pays the maximum and a balance remains, the provider still may not bill the survivor; the program payment is payment in full.
rule.quote: No. A health care provider must accept the payment in full for the costs of the forensic rape examination.
rule.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

rule.summary: The provider must file the exam claim within one year of the crime or its discovery; if the provider misses that deadline, the survivor still cannot be billed.
rule.quote: The claim must be filed by a hospital or other licensed health care provider, within one year of the date of the crime or discovery of the crime. Failure to file within the prescribed time frame will result in non-payment of the claim and the victim cannot be billed for those costs.
rule.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.4
rule.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params.exception: not counting some costs that are paid on top

rule.summary: The total award is capped at $35,000, except that counseling, forensic rape exam costs, and crime scene cleanup are paid on top of that cap.
rule.quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rule.summary: Lost earnings caused by the injury are covered, up to the state average weekly wage for each week, if not otherwise reimbursed.
rule.quote: OVS may make an award within the monetary limitations of the act to compensate a direct victim, intervenor or claimant for loss of earnings attributable to the injury not to exceed the average weekly wage if the claimant was not otherwise reimbursed for the loss.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rule.summary: Temporary or permanent relocation is covered when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and household, verified by a medical provider, human services provider, or law enforcement.
rule.quote: expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a direct victim and individuals residing in the household of the direct victim due to the incident forming the basis of the victim's claim when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the household, as verified by a medical provider, human services provider or law enforcement
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

rule.summary: The move must happen within 120 days of the crime, or within 120 days of a new threat or sign of danger.
rule.quote: Relocation must occur within 120 days from the date of crime, or 120 days from the date the victim is threatened by any change of circumstance or indicator of danger.
rule.source_title: VCAP flyer: Relocation Expenses (11/2023)

params.item: replacing medical devices, eyeglasses, and prescription medicine

rule.summary: Replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dental devices, prescription medications and similar health items stolen or damaged in the crime is capped at $1,000, with eyeglass frames limited to $200. This is not a cap on ordinary medical bills.
rule.quote: OVS will reimburse a claimant for costs for the replacement of each prosthetic device, wheelchair, cane, walker, hearing aid, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, dental device or prescription medications. Reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 and will be subject to the following limitations: (1)  Two hundred dollars for eyeglass frames.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.scope: services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, or laundry

rule.summary: Services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, laundry, and meal preparation, can be reimbursed.
rule.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.extension: Good cause can excuse a late filing (incapacity, victim was a minor, fear of retaliation, crime not readily apparent, other good cause; 18 P.S. 11.702(b)(2)(iii.1)). For a victim under 18 abused by a parent, caretaker, household member or parent's paramour, the period is tolled until age 21 and runs to the later of the criminal limitation period or the standard period. Sexual abuse counseling claims under 18 P.S. 11.701.1 are excepted from this deadline.

before.summary: A claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered, under the current law; the program may accept a late claim for good cause. Older crimes had a shorter deadline, so those survivors should call the program.

params.extension: or later in some cases, such as sexual abuse counseling claims, some survivors who were children, or when the program finds good cause

after.summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.

rule.summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.
rule.quote: a claim must be filed not later than five years after the discovery of the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: The crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities; the statute sets no fixed number of hours. A protection order filing (statute) or a forensic rape exam (program policy) also counts.

after.summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.

rule.summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.
rule.quote: The crime was promptly reported to the proper authorities.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: Filing for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order satisfies the reporting requirement, even without a police report.

after.summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.

rule.summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.
rule.quote: may satisfy the eligibility requirement under subsection (a)(3) for reporting a crime to the proper authorities by commencing an action brought in accordance with 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 62A (relating to protection of victims of sexual violence or intimidation)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: Having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without going to police.

params.exam_condition: for a crime on or after September 8, 2022

after.summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.

rule.summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.
rule.quote: Effective for crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, a forensic rape exam is considered acceptable for reporting to proper authorities. This change allows victims who have the FRE completed to be eligible for a standard claim without having to report the crime to law enforcement.
rule.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rule.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

before.summary: An emergency award of up to $5,000 per claim is available for urgent financial need.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.
rule.quote: The total amount of an emergency award will not exceed $5,000 per claim.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

before.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records.

after.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, can give survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records, once the office approves their application.

rule.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, can give survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records, once the office approves their application.
rule.quote: The ACP can provide you with an alternate mailing address to keep your address out of public records if you are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction.
rule.pinpoint: OVA Address Confidentiality Program page; statute: 23 Pa.C.S. 6703(a), 6704(2)
rule.source_title: PA Office of Victim Advocate: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)
