added.summary: The Attorney General's bill of rights page also warns that choosing not to take part in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for compensation benefits.
added.quote: However, your decision not to participate in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for benefits under the crime victim compensation program.
added.pinpoint: Attorney General's Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights page, Your right to choose whether to report
added.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

added.summary: If you found out about the crime more than 1 year after it happened, the time to apply starts when you found out, or should have. This applies only if the crime led to a criminal complaint, an indictment or criminal information, or another court finding of probable cause.
added.quote: If the Applicant did not discover the act which constitutes a crime until more than one year after the crime was committed, the filing period shall not commence until the Applicant discovered or, in exercise of reasonable diligence, should have discovered, the act which constitutes a crime, provided, however, that in such cases, the crime for which the Applicant seeks compensation must have resulted in the issuance of a criminal complaint, indictment or criminal information, or other judicial determination of probable cause that an act constituting a crime occurred
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Not knowing the filing rules does not count as good cause for a late application.
added.quote: Delay resulting from the lack of knowledge of the filing requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-25-1, et seq. shall not constitute good cause.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Believing police will not investigate, or not knowing that an award depends on reporting the crime, is not good cause for a late report. The program's rule also says good cause excuses only the delay, not the reporting requirement itself.
added.quote: Delay resulting from a belief that law enforcement authorities will not investigate the crime, or delay resulting from lack of knowledge that an award under R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-1 et. seq. is contingent upon reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities, does not constitute good cause for delay. d. A finding of good cause for delay does not excuse the reporting requirement which must be satisfied as a condition of receiving compensation.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: The program's rule says a victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. It says this includes reporting the crime, helping identify the suspect, and following reasonable requests for information and help.
added.quote: A victim must cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. a. Victim’s obligations: Cooperation with law enforcement agencies and personnel includes reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities; assisting in identifying the suspect; and complying with all reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel for information and assistance.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Emergency relocation is capped at $5,000. Any relocation award is deducted from the final award.
added.quote: Compensation awarded for emergency relocation expenses shall not exceed the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). Any award for emergency relocation expenses shall be deducted from the final award.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: To be paid for a move, the crime must have happened in your home. If it did not, you must show the crime makes you reasonably afraid to stay there. You must also need to move right away, reasonably fear living as you did before the crime, or be unable to afford your documented housing costs right after the crime.
added.quote: The crime must have occurred in the victim’s primary place of residence or the Applicant must demonstrate that, as a result of the crime, he or she reasonably fears for his or her continued safety in his or her primary place of residence. (2) An Applicant must have an immediate need to relocate, a reasonable fear to continue to live within the arrangements as established prior to the crime, or, alternatively, immediately following the crime, the Applicant must be unable to afford the documented housing costs.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

rule.summary: The total award to a victim cannot exceed $25,000 (plus any attorney fees awarded on appeal).
rule.quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter to the victim, or in the case of death to dependent relatives or to the legal representative, in a total amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)
rule.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

params.extension: Minors: the period starts at age 18 (120-RICR-00-00-2.7(A)(1)(a)); if the crime was not discovered until more than a year later, the period starts at discovery, but only if the crime led to a criminal complaint, indictment, criminal information, or other probable cause finding (2.7(A)(1)(b)); late filing may be allowed for unsound mind or good cause (2.7(A)(1)(c)); lack of knowledge of the filing rules is not good cause.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 3 years of the injury.
rule.quote: Actions for compensation under this chapter shall be commenced within three (3) years after the date of the injury or death
rule.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 15 days, but the office may allow a claim without a police report when a sexual assault survivor had a medical forensic exam within 15 days of the crime.
rule.quote: no compensation shall be awarded for an injury or death resulting from a crime that was not reported to the appropriate law enforcement authority within fifteen (15) days of its occurrence; provided, that the office shall have the authority to allow a claim that was not reported pursuant to this section when a victim of a sexual assault receives a medical forensic examination within fifteen (15) days of the crime
rule.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

before.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.

after.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws 15-15-3 with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.

rule.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws 15-15-3 with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.
rule.quote: The reporting of a crime to a court through a citizen application for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-15-3 accompanied by an affidavit in support of the application for protection, or through a citizen application for a criminal complaint, shall constitute a report to law enforcement authorities.
rule.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

before.summary: A late police report can be excused for good cause, such as physical or psychological incapacity or reasonable fear of retaliation. Good cause excuses only the delay; a report is still required.

after.summary: A late police report can be excused for good cause, such as being physically or psychologically unable to make a report, or a reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.

rule.summary: A late police report can be excused for good cause, such as being physically or psychologically unable to make a report, or a reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
rule.quote: Good cause for delay shall include, but not be limited to, delay caused by physical or psychological incapacity which prevented the making of a report; or by reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
rule.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

before.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior contributed to the injury; the same subsection also lets it weigh cooperation with police and violent criminal history.

after.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.

rule.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.
rule.quote: The behavior of the victim, including past behavior, that directly or indirectly contributed to his or her injury or death, unless the injury or death resulted from the victim’s lawful attempt to prevent the commission of a crime or to apprehend an offender. The office may reduce or deny an award based on these circumstances.
rule.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

rule.summary: Lost earnings for injuries on or after January 1, 2022 are figured at 62% of gross earnings.
rule.quote: All net earnings for injuries occurring on or after January 1, 2022 are calculated based on 62% of the victim’s gross earnings.
rule.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

before.summary: A Rhode Island resident hurt in another state can apply only if that state's program offers no compensation.

after.summary: A Rhode Island resident hurt in another state can apply here only if they also lived in Rhode Island when it happened and are not entitled to any compensation from the state where it happened.

rule.summary: A Rhode Island resident hurt in another state can apply here only if they also lived in Rhode Island when it happened and are not entitled to any compensation from the state where it happened.
rule.quote: Outside the state of Rhode Island to any victim who has his or her residence in the state of Rhode Island and had the residence in the state at the time that the offense occurred, and is not entitled to compensation of any kind from the state, possession, or territory or district of the United States in which the offense occurred
rule.source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

before.summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State's Department of State, gives victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move a shared Providence PO Box to use as their address on state and local government records, with first-class mail and legal papers forwarded free to their real address. Applicants mail a sworn application to the Department, which can help fill it out.

after.summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of State, helps victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move. To qualify, you must live in Rhode Island, fear for your own or your children's safety, live or plan to live at an address the person who harmed you does not know, and agree not to give that person the address. You apply by mailing a sworn application to the Department, which can help you fill it out.

rule.summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of State, helps victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move. To qualify, you must live in Rhode Island, fear for your own or your children's safety, live or plan to live at an address the person who harmed you does not know, and agree not to give that person the address. You apply by mailing a sworn application to the Department, which can help you fill it out.
rule.quote: The goal of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP/Program) is to help victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, and trafficking and/or abuse as defined by RI Gen. Laws §42-164-2 who have relocated or are about to relocate
rule.source_title: Address Confidentiality Program page, Rhode Island Department of State

before.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days of the latest qualifying event (usually the crime). For good cause the deadline can be extended, but not past four years after the crime, diagnosed manifestation, or death.

params.extension: or of a later date in some cases, such as when police learned it was a crime. With good cause, the program can allow up to 4 years after the crime

after.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.
rule.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than one hundred eighty days after the latest of the following events: (1) the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; (2) the death of the victim; (3) the discovery by the law enforcement agency that the occurrence was the result of crime; or (4) the manifestation of a mental or physical injury is diagnosed as a result of a crime committed against a minor. (C) Upon good cause shown, the time for filing may be extended for a period not to exceed four years after the occurrence, diagnosed manifestation, or death.

added.summary: The exam cost the county pays includes the provider and facility services for the exam, forensic supplies, scope procedures, lab tests such as STI, HIV, and pregnancy screening, any medication given during the exam, and radiology tied to the exam.
added.quote: The cost of a forensic medical examination includes: (1) Provider, hospital, or clinic services directly related to the examination; (2) Necessary forensic supplies; (3) Scope procedures directly related to the examination, including anoscopy and colposcopy; (4) Laboratory testing directly related to the examination, including drug screening, urinalysis, pregnancy screening, syphilis screening, chlamydia culture, gonorrhea coverage culture, HIV screening, hepatitis B and C screening, herpes culture, and any other sexually transmitted disease testing directly related to the examination; (5) Any medication provided during the examination; and (6) Any radiology service directly related to the examination.

added.summary: Except for an emergency award, the commission may go above the limits on single costs when the claimant shows evidence of need. In no case can payments go above the program's overall limit.
added.quote: With the exception of an emergency award, the commission may deviate from the limits established in this chapter. The claimant must submit evidence to the commission that substantiates the need for the deviation. Based on the evidence submitted, the commission shall determine whether the deviation is warranted. added.quote: Expenses for security devices , including digital security cameras, are payable.

added.quote: monthly service cost , if any, of a security device installed for the benefit of a victim is the victim's responsibility.
added.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: The county where the sexual assault happened pays for the forensic medical exam, including related lab tests, medication given during the exam, and supplies.

after.summary: The county where the sexual assault happened pays for the forensic medical exam.

rule.summary: The county where the sexual assault happened pays for the forensic medical exam.
rule.quote: The county where an alleged rape or sexual offense occurred shall pay the cost of any forensic medical examination performed on the victim of the alleged rape or sexual offense.
rule.source_title: SDCL 22-22-26, Forensic medical examination, costs to county

before.summary: Hospitals and clinics must tell survivors the forensic exam is available at no cost to them, and a survivor does not have to take part in the criminal case or cooperate with police to get the exam. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.

params.condition: if the crime was in South Dakota

after.summary: For an exam under section 22-22-26, which has the county where the assault happened pay, hospitals and clinics must tell survivors the exam is available at no cost to them. A survivor does not have to take part in the criminal case or cooperate with police to get the exam. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.

rule.summary: For an exam under section 22-22-26, which has the county where the assault happened pay, hospitals and clinics must tell survivors the exam is available at no cost to them. A survivor does not have to take part in the criminal case or cooperate with police to get the exam. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
rule.quote: Each hospital and clinic that provides a forensic medical examination under § 22-22-26 shall coordinate with the county to establish a payment process by which the county shall pay for the cost of the examination, and to notify any victim of rape or sexual offense of the availability of an examination at no cost to the victim. A victim of rape or sexual offense is not required to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement to be provided with a forensic medical examination.
rule.source_title: SDCL 22-22-26.2, Forensic medical examinations, payment, notice to victim

rule.summary: The compensation program does not reimburse rape or sexual offense exams that are provided under the county-pay exam statute.
rule.quote: Reimbursement is not allowed for rape or sexual offense examinations provided under the provisions of SDCL
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Security devices, including digital security cameras, are covered up to $500 including materials and labor; monthly service fees are not. The commission can approve more than this limit on evidence of need, but never above the overall program limit.

after.summary: Security devices are covered up to $500, including materials and labor.

rule.summary: Security devices are covered up to $500, including materials and labor.
rule.quote: Payment for security devices may not exceed $500, including materials and labor.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Basic funeral and burial expenses are capped at $8,000. The commission can approve more than this limit on evidence of need, but never above the overall program limit.

after.summary: Basic funeral and burial expenses are capped at $8,000.

rule.summary: Basic funeral and burial expenses are capped at $8,000.
rule.quote: Payment for basic funeral and burial expenses may not exceed $8,000.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Homicide scene cleanup is capped at $1,500. The commission can approve more than this limit on evidence of need, but never above the overall program limit.

params.applies_to: homicide scene cleanup

after.summary: Homicide scene cleanup is capped at $1,500.

rule.summary: Homicide scene cleanup is capped at $1,500.
rule.quote: Payment for homicide scene cleanup may not exceed one thousand five hundred dollars.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

rule.summary: Lost earnings are paid based on the victim's average monthly earnings for the 6 months before the injury or the monthly minimum wage, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage is the federal hourly minimum wage times 173.2 hours.
rule.quote: Loss of earnings, loss of future earnings, and loss of support shall be determined on the basis of the victim's average monthly earnings for the six months immediately preceding the date of injury, or the monthly minimum wage as of the date of the crime underlying the claim, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage shall be based upon the federal hourly minimum wage in effect as of the date of the crime multiplied by 173.2 hours per month.
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

before.summary: When the victim is the claimant, lost earnings are limited to the 12 months right after the crime. The victim must have been employed at the time of the crime, and hours paid with sick or annual leave do not count.

after.summary: When the victim is the claimant, lost earnings are paid only for the 12 months right after the crime.

rule.summary: When the victim is the claimant, lost earnings are paid only for the 12 months right after the crime.
rule.quote: Payment for lost earnings or loss of future earnings is limited to the following: (1) If the claimant is the victim, the 12-month period immediately following the date of the crime;
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Apart from mental health care, medical services are paid only if provided in the 12 months after the crime, unless the department extends that for good cause.

after.summary: Payment for medical expenses is limited to medical services provided in the 12 months right after the crime. The department may extend this 12-month period for good cause.

rule.summary: Payment for medical expenses is limited to medical services provided in the 12 months right after the crime. The department may extend this 12-month period for good cause.
rule.quote: payment for medical expenses is limited to those medical services provided during the 12-month period immediately following the date the crime occurred. The department may extend this 12-month period if good cause is shown.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Mileage is covered for trips such as getting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam, treatment, court, and meetings with police.

params.scope: mileage to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam

after.summary: Mileage is covered for getting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam.

rule.summary: Mileage is covered for getting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault exam.
rule.quote: Mileage accrued for transporting the victim to a hospital or medical facility for a sexual assault examination
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: mileage in a private car, paid at the state employee rate

rule.summary: Mileage is reimbursed at the state employee rate for a privately owned car.
rule.quote: Mileage is reimbursed at the rate established for state employees in SDCL 3-9-1 , as applicable, for the use of a privately owned automobile.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

params.scope: replacing clothing, bedding, and other property used as evidence

rule.summary: The replacement value of property taken as evidence, including clothing and bedding, is covered if it is not returned.
rule.quote: "Personal property losses," the replacement value of property, including clothing and bedding, used for evidentiary purposes
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

rule.summary: Child care is covered when the parent cannot care for the child because of crime-related impairment, court, police meetings, or a medical appointment.
rule.quote: Child care expenses are payable if the parent is unable to care for the child because the parent has sustained physical or emotional impairment as a direct result of a crime, if the parent is required to attend court proceedings or meet with law enforcement, or the parent has a medical appointment.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: Only clothing and bedding kept as evidence is covered; property damaged in the incident is not.

after.summary: Property damaged in the incident is not covered.

rule.summary: Property damaged in the incident is not covered.
rule.quote: Only clothing and bedding that was collected as evidence, and will not be returned to the claimant, is compensable through the CVC Program. Property damaged in the incident is not eligible for compensation.
rule.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Primary Application Instructions

params.extension: The department may waive the one-year deadline for good cause shown.
or later if the department waives the deadline for good cause

rule.summary: The application must be filed within one year after the date of the injury, but the department may waive that for good cause.
rule.quote: Unless an application for compensation is filed with the department within one year after the date of the personal injury or death and the personal injury or death was the result of a crime which had been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within five days of its occurrence or, if the crime could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the date when a report could reasonably have been made. The department may waive the one year application requirement for good cause shown
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

before.summary: The crime must have been reported to law enforcement within 5 days, or within 5 days of when a report could reasonably have been made. No alternative to a police report for sexual assault was found in the statute.

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

after.summary: The crime must have been reported to law enforcement within 5 days. If that was not reasonably possible, it must have been reported within 5 days of when it could have been.

rule.summary: The crime must have been reported to law enforcement within 5 days. If that was not reasonably possible, it must have been reported within 5 days of when it could have been.
rule.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of a crime which had been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within five days of its occurrence or, if the crime could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the date when a report could reasonably have been made
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

before.summary: If the crime was not reported within 5 days, the application asks for a letter explaining the reason for the delay.

after.summary: If the crime was not reported within 5 days of when it happened, or the victim did not cooperate, the application asks for a letter explaining the late report or the decision not to cooperate.

rule.summary: If the crime was not reported within 5 days of when it happened, or the victim did not cooperate, the application asks for a letter explaining the late report or the decision not to cooperate.
rule.quote: If the crime was not reported within 5 days of the date that it occurred or if the victim did not cooperate, please submit a letter explaining the reason for the delay in reporting or decision not to cooperate.
rule.source_title: SD Crime Victims' Compensation Program Primary Application (DPS-VS-694 12/17)

before.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from collateral sources such as the offender, insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, workers compensation, or employer wage continuation.

after.summary: Any award is reduced by money the victim gets, or will get, because of the crime from the sources the law lists. These include the offender, insurance, Medicaid or Medicare, workers compensation, and an employer's wage continuation.

rule.summary: Any award is reduced by money the victim gets, or will get, because of the crime from the sources the law lists. These include the offender, insurance, Medicaid or Medicare, workers compensation, and an employer's wage continuation.
rule.quote: Any award of victims' compensation made pursuant to this chapter shall be reduced by the amount of any payment received, or to be received, by the victim from any collateral source as a result of the conduct giving rise to the application for compensation.
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

before.summary: Bills for rape exams and related expenses must go to insurance and other collateral sources before the program pays.

after.summary: Before the compensation program pays a bill for a rape exam or related care, the bill must first go to insurance and other sources, including health insurance.

rule.summary: Before the compensation program pays a bill for a rape exam or related care, the bill must first go to insurance and other sources, including health insurance.
rule.quote: Bills for rape exams and related expenses must be submitted to collateral sources, including health insurance, before payment may be made under the provisions of this article.
rule.source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

before.summary: The department may grant an emergency award of up to $1,000 for undue hardship; it is deducted from the final award.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.
rule.quote: The amount of an emergency award may not exceed one thousand dollars.
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

before.summary: Records and reports the compensation department or commission obtains stay confidential if another law or rule already makes them confidential (for example medical or counseling records). The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.

after.summary: Records and reports the department or commission obtains stay confidential if another law or rule already makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.

rule.summary: Records and reports the department or commission obtains stay confidential if another law or rule already makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
rule.quote: Any record or report obtained by the department or commission, the confidentiality of which is protected by any law or administrative rule, shall remain confidential.
rule.source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

added.summary: The program says it may consider paying for counseling the victim needs because of the injury. The most it can pay is the overall limit.
added.quote: Any counseling services must be necessary due to the injury and may be considered for the victim up to the maximum award.
added.pinpoint: Program page, Eligible (Covered) Expenses Explained: Medical Bills/Mental Health Counseling
added.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation program page (eligibility, Apply for Compensation, FAQ)

added.summary: The program covers reasonable costs to repair or replace property of the victim or a relative that was damaged when police processed the scene. This is for a sexual assault, homicide, or aggravated assault at the home of the victim or of the relative who owned the property.
added.quote: the reasonable costs of repairing or replacing personal property owned by the victim or a relative of the victim as defined in § 29-13-102 that was damaged or destroyed in processing the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault if the scene was the residence of the victim or the relative of the victim who owned the property.
added.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

added.summary: Some sex crimes against a minor allow more time. A claim can also be filed within 2 years after a mental or physical injury from the crime is diagnosed.
added.quote: two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses
added.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: A victim does not have to report to police or cooperate with prosecution for the forensic exam to be paid.
rule.quote: the victims shall not be required to report the incident to law enforcement officers or to cooperate in the prosecution of the crime in order to be eligible for payment of forensic medical examinations
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params.condition: for a crime on or after July 1, 2025

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2025, the Treasury lists an overall maximum of $34,100 for all expenses on claims from the crime. The cap depends on the crime date.
rule.quote: For crimes occurring on or after July 1, 2025: $34,100
rule.pinpoint: Treasury Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025); set under T.C.A. 29-13-106(h)
rule.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025)

params.item: pain and suffering
params.scope: for victims of rape, human trafficking, or another sexual crime

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid for most crimes, but it can be paid to victims of rape, human trafficking, and crimes involving sexual deviancy.
rule.quote: Compensation must not be awarded for any personal injury or loss alleged to have been incurred as a result of pain and suffering, except for victims of the crime of rape, victims of a human trafficking offense, and victims of a crime involving sexual deviancy
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: pain and suffering

rule.summary: A pain and suffering award for a victim of a sexually-oriented crime may not exceed $3,000.
rule.quote: Any award based on the pain and suffering experienced by a claimant victimized by a sexually-oriented crime is to be made in an amount deemed necessary and appropriate, not to exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: Lost wages caused by the crime are paid on the workers' compensation temporary total disability schedule, but at 85 percent of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rule.quote: Any award made for lost wages proximately caused by a violent crime is to be based upon those schedules of compensation for temporary total disability allowable by the workers' compensation statutes, found in § 50-6-207, in effect at the time of the commission of the crime giving rise to such claim; provided, however, that the sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) rate prescribed in the workers' compensation statutes shall not be used in determining the amount of any award hereunder. Instead, such rate shall be eighty-five percent (85%) of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: If the assault happened at the victim's home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and utility transfer fees are covered, for no more than 2 moves.

params.scope: moving costs, if the assault happened at your home, for up to 2 moves

after.summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.

rule.summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable moving expenses, storage fees and fees for transfer of utility service if the move is a direct result of an assault committed upon such victim at the victim's residence, provided that the victim shall not receive compensation for more than two (2) moves resulting from the assault
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: cleaning the scene, if it was your home or a relative's home

rule.summary: Reasonable costs to clean the scene of a sexual assault are covered when the scene was the home of the victim or a relative.
rule.quote: Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred for cleaning supplies, equipment rental and labor needed to clean the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault, if the scene was the residence of the victim or a relative of the victim
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial (and later appeals) is capped at a cumulative $1,250. This cap is only for court travel.

after.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.

rule.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.
rule.quote: Any award made under the preceding sentence to a claimant shall not exceed a cumulative total of one thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($1,250) for all such travel.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: eyeglasses and hearing aids; property damaged in processing a sexual assault scene at the residence

before.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, repair, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged by the crime are covered, as is property damaged while processing a sexual assault scene at the home of the victim or a relative.

params.item: eyeglasses and hearing aids; property damaged in processing a sexual assault scene at the residence
params.scope: cleaning, fixing, or replacing the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged by the crime or the crime scene work

after.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, fix, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids are covered when the crime or the crime scene work damaged them.

rule.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, fix, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids are covered when the crime or the crime scene work damaged them.
rule.quote: Reasonable costs of cleaning, repairing or replacing eyeglasses and hearing aids owned by the victim that were damaged or destroyed by the crime or the processing of the crime scene
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.extension: Good cause can extend the period, before or after it runs. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, the claim may also be filed within 2 years after a resulting mental or physical injury is diagnosed.
or later if the program extends it for good cause

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years after the crime. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, it can also be filed within 2 years after a resulting injury is diagnosed, and good cause can extend the time.
rule.quote: A claim for compensation must be filed not later than two (2) years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based, two (2) years after the death of the victim, or two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses; provided, that upon good cause shown, the time period for filing such claim may be extended either before or after the expiration of the filing period.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

params.exception: or later if there is good cause, which can include sexual assault

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authorities within 15 days, but a late report can be excused for good cause, and being a victim of sexual assault is a listed reason for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim cannot be filed until the crime upon which the claim is based has been reported by the victim, or a member of the victim's family, to the proper authorities within fifteen (15) days after the occurrence of such crime unless, for good cause shown, it is found that the delay was justified. Good cause for the failure of a victim or a member of the victim's family to report a crime may be found if the victim is: (1) Physically unable; (2) A victim of sexual assault;
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: To qualify, the claimant needs at least $100 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 2 continuous weeks of lost earnings or support, unless the limit would not serve the interest of justice.
rule.quote: no award shall be made unless the claimant has incurred a minimum out of pocket loss of one hundred dollars ($100) or has lost at least two (2) continuous weeks earnings or support, unless it is determined that the interest of justice would not be served by such a limitation
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: The claims commission may make an emergency award of up to $500 before a final decision when an award is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship. It is deducted from the final award.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.
rule.quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-114 (emergency award), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: If claiming lost wages, include wage documentation; the statute lists lost wage verifications and W-2 forms.
rule.quote: Lost wage verifications; (iii) W-2 forms
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-103 (burden of proof; documentation; proof of offense), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Tennessee Secretary of State, is free and open to survivors of rape, sexual battery, or any other sexual offense (plus domestic abuse, stalking, and human trafficking). An approved participant gets a substitute address to use as the official mailing address for state and local government purposes, with a few exceptions. Applying takes an application assistant at a partner agency.

after.summary: Safe at Home is a free program run by the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to survivors of rape, sexual battery, or another sex crime, and of domestic abuse, stalking, or human trafficking, who meet its eligibility and application rules. Once approved, you get a substitute address to use as your official mailing address for state and local government.

rule.summary: Safe at Home is a free program run by the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to survivors of rape, sexual battery, or another sex crime, and of domestic abuse, stalking, or human trafficking, who meet its eligibility and application rules. Once approved, you get a substitute address to use as your official mailing address for state and local government.
rule.quote: The Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program is a statewide address confidentiality program administered by the Office of the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to all victims of domestic abuse, stalking, human trafficking, rape, sexual battery, or any other sexual offense who satisfy eligibility and application requirements at no cost. Once a participant has been approved, they are provided with a 'substitute' address that can be used by them and their children as their official mailing address for all state and local government purposes
rule.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ 'What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?'; statute T.C.A. 40-38-601 to 40-38-604 (enroll text from 40-38-604(a))
rule.source_title: Tennessee Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ: What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?

added.summary: Other victims can be paid moving costs and rent when a move is needed to protect their health or safety.
added.quote: A victim other than a victim described by Subsection (c), a dependent of any victim, a family member of any victim if that family member has previously resided with the victim for a period of not less than two years, or a household member of any victim may receive compensation for the following expenses, if the expenses are necessary to protect the health or safety of the victim, dependent, or family or household member: (1) relocation expenses, including expenses for rental deposit, utility connections, expenses relating to moving belongings, motor vehicle mileage expenses, temporary or emergency lodging, and for an out-of-state move, expenses for transportation, lodging, and meals; and (2) housing rental expenses.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: If you were subpoenaed to appear in court, the program does not pay for those trips. Its page says to ask the prosecutor's office instead.
added.quote: Note: Victims or claimants subpoenaed to appear in court cannot receive reimbursement through the CVC program for those appearances. If subpoenaed, please seek reimbursement from the prosecutor’s office.
added.pinpoint: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement page, Note
added.source_title: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement

added.summary: For care sought after August 31, 2025, Emergency Medical Care also pays for prescribed care tied to the assault in the 30 days after the exam.
added.quote: For medical care sought after August 31, 2025, EMC also covers any prescribed continuing medical care that is related to the sexual assault and provided to the victim during the 30-day period following the exam.
added.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation page
added.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

added.summary: If the victim is a child, the time to apply counts from the day the victim or claimant learns of the crime. It ends on the third anniversary of that day, and no later than the child's 21st birthday.
added.quote: If the victim is a child, the application must be filed not later than the third anniversary of the date the claimant or victim is made aware of the offense, but not after the child attains 21 years of age.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: If medical records show the crime left you unable to apply, that time does not count toward the deadline.
added.quote: If a claimant or victim presents medically documented evidence of a physical or mental incapacity that was incurred by the claimant or victim as a result of the criminally injurious conduct and that reasonably prevented the claimant or victim from filing the application within the limitations period under Subsection (a), the period of the incapacity is not included.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: The attorney general may give more time to report in extraordinary circumstances. The report rule does not apply if the victim is a child.
added.quote: The attorney general may extend the time for reporting the criminally injurious conduct if the attorney general determines that the extension is justified by extraordinary circumstances. (c) Subsection (a) does not apply if the victim is a child.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.scope: the forensic part of an exam or the evidence kit

rule.summary: A sexual assault survivor cannot be made to pay for the forensic part of the exam or the evidence kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed for it.
rule.quote: A victim of a sexual assault may not be required to pay for: (1) the forensic portion of the forensic medical examination; or (2) the evidence collection kit.
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

rule.summary: The Attorney General reimburses the provider or examiner for the forensic portion of the exam, the evidence kit, and medical care given during the exam.
rule.quote: a health care provider that provides a forensic medical examination to a sexual assault survivor in accordance with this subchapter, or the sexual assault examiner or sexual assault nurse examiner who conducts that examination in accordance with this subchapter, as applicable, is entitled to be reimbursed in an amount set by attorney general rule for: (1) the reasonable costs of the forensic portion of that examination; (2) the evidence collection kit;
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

before.summary: Emergency Medical Care (EMC): the Attorney General pays for medical care given during a sexual assault forensic exam, and prescribed related follow-up care, at medical fee guideline rates, up to $25,000. rule.summary: Texas law keeps your compensation application and the Attorney General's records on it private, with some exceptions. added.summary: The SAFE Payment Program pays only if the crime was in Virginia and evidence is collected.

added.summary: As this section describes, the State covers the costs of certain medical care for victims of a crime committed in Vermont who have no health insurance or whose insurance does not pay for all of the care.

added.summary: Prosecution for lewd and lascivious conduct must begin within 6 years, so that is also the time limit to apply for it.
added.quote: (b) Prosecutions for lewd and lascivious conduct, sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(a) of this title, grand larceny, robbery, burglary, embezzlement, forgery, bribery offenses, false claims, fraud under 33 V.S.A. § 141(d), and felony tax offenses shall be commenced within six years after the commission of the offense, and not after.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

added.summary: For lewd and lascivious conduct against a child under 18, lewd or lascivious conduct with a child, and sexual exploitation of children, prosecution must begin within 40 years. That is also the time limit to apply.
added.quote: (c) Prosecutions for any of the following offenses shall be commenced within 40 years after the commission of the offense, and not after: (1) lewd and lascivious conduct alleged to have been committed against a child under 18 years of age; (2) maiming; (3) lewd or lascivious conduct with a child; (4) sexual exploitation of children under chapter 64 of this title; and (5) sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(b) of this title.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

after.summary: For a sexual assault that happened in Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Department of Justice pays exam costs directly to the health care provider through the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Fund. before.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury. The department may waive this in the interest of justice; if late, attach a written explanation of the delay.

after.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury.

rule.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury.

before.summary: If more than 1 year has passed, the program still accepts an application with a written statement explaining the delay.

after.summary: If the application is not filed within 1 year, the program asks for a written statement explaining the delay.

rule.summary: If the application is not filed within 1 year, the program asks for a written statement explaining the delay.

before.summary: For compensation (beyond the exam), the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when it could reasonably be reported. The department may waive this in the interest of justice. No sexual-assault-specific alternative to a police report was found.

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could, and the program can waive this

after.summary: For compensation (beyond the exam), the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when it could reasonably be reported. The department may waive this in the interest of justice.

rule.summary: For compensation (beyond the exam), the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when it could reasonably be reported. The department may waive this in the interest of justice.
rule.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense which had been reported to the police within 5 days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within such period, within 5 days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made. The department may waive the requirements under this subsection in the interest of justice.
rule.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rule.summary: Sexual assault (s. 940.225) is a compensable crime. Child sexual assault, sexual exploitation by a therapist, trafficking, and sexual extortion are also on the list.

rule.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Crime Victim Compensation Application

before.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Wisconsin Department of Justice, gives Wisconsin residents who are victims of sexual abuse and other listed abuse a legal substitute address to use in place of their actual address, with free mail forwarding. Applicants first make a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant.

after.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Wisconsin Department of Justice, provides a legal substitute address to people who live in Wisconsin and are victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, or trafficking, or who fear for their physical safety. You must live at an address the person you fear does not know, and not share it with them. To enroll, you first make a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant.

rule.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Wisconsin Department of Justice, provides a legal substitute address to people who live in Wisconsin and are victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, or trafficking, or who fear for their physical safety. You must live at an address the person you fear does not know, and not share it with them. To enroll, you first make a safety plan with a designated Application Assistant.
rule.quote: Safe at Home is an address confidentiality program that provides victims of domestic abuse, child abuse, sexual abuse, stalking, trafficking, or those who simply fear for their physical safety with a legal substitute address
rule.pinpoint: Wisconsin DOJ, Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program page, program description; Wis. Stat. 165.68
rule.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: The Fund's page says a victim who was under 18 at the time must apply before turning 20.
added.quote: The application for an adult victim (18 years or older at the time of crime) must be filed with the Fund within two years of the crime. The application for a minor victim (under 18 year of age at the time of the crime) must be filed with the Fund before the minor’s 20th birthday.
added.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Time Limitations for Filing Application
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

rule.summary: A survivor does not have to report to police or cooperate with law enforcement to get a state-paid forensic exam.
rule.quote: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require an alleged victim of sexual assault to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement in order to be provided a forensic medical examination pursuant to the provisions of this section.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 61-8B-16 (Payment for forensic medical examination)

params.exception: or more in some cases

rule.summary: For an injury claim, total compensation to the victim and all other claimants may not exceed $35,000.
rule.quote: Except in the case of death, or as provided in subdivision (2) of this subsection, compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to that victim may not exceed $35,000 in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rule.summary: Reasonable charges for needed medical and psychological care, including eyeglasses, dentures and rehabilitation, are allowable expenses.
rule.quote: Reasonable charges incurred or to be incurred for reasonably needed medical care, including products, services, and accommodations related to medical and psychological care, prosthetic devices, eye glasses, dentures, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment and care
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

params.scope: mental health counseling by a licensed counselor

rule.summary: Mental health counseling by a licensed counselor is a reimbursable expense.
rule.quote: Mental Health Counseling by a Licensed Counselor
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

params.scope: travel to and from a medical facility

rule.summary: Reasonable travel to and from a medical facility is an allowable expense.
rule.quote: Reasonable travel expenses for the transportation of a victim to and from a medical facility.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Lost income from work the victim could not do because of the injury counts as economic loss.
rule.quote: "Work loss" means loss of income from work that the injured person would have performed if he or she had not been injured
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Income lost to attend court proceedings in the prosecution also counts as work loss.
rule.quote: "Work loss" also includes loss of income from work by the claimant, the victim, or the parent or legal guardian of a minor victim who must miss work to attend court proceedings conducted for the prosecution of the offender.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-3 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Dental costs are listed with medical costs as reimbursable.
rule.quote: Medical/Dental Mental Health Counseling by a Licensed Counselor Lost Wages/Income
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

before.summary: Damaged or stolen personal property (for example a phone) and stolen money are not covered. Eyeglasses and dentures are an exception.

after.summary: Damaged or stolen property, including money, is not covered.

rule.summary: Damaged or stolen property, including money, is not covered.
rule.quote: No. Damaged or stolen property, including money, is NOT recoverable.
rule.source_title: Application for West Virginia Crime Victims Compensation

params.exception: or later with good cause, and minors need neither
params.exam_condition: done within 96 hours of the assault

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 96 hours, but for a sexual offense a forensic medical exam within 96 hours meets the requirement instead. Good cause can excuse a late report or exam, and juvenile victims are exempt.
rule.quote: The commissioner may not approve an award of compensation if the criminally injurious conduct upon which the claim is based was not reported to a law-enforcement officer or agency or, in the case of sexual offense, the victim did not undergo a forensic medical examination, within 96 hours after the occurrence of the conduct, unless it is determined that good cause existed for the failure to report the conduct or undergo a forensic medical examination within the 96-hour period: Provided , That reporting to a law-enforcement officer or agency or a forensic medical examination is not required if the victim is a juvenile in order for a commissioner to approve an award of compensation
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

params.scope: filing of a criminal charge, not just a report; exceptions for unknown offender, juvenile claimant, or adult claimant who did not block charges where law enforcement confirms a crime occurred

before.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown, when the claimant was a juvenile, or when an adult claimant did not cause the lack of charges and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.

params.scope: filing of a criminal charge, not just a report; exceptions for unknown offender, juvenile claimant, or adult claimant who did not block charges where law enforcement confirms a crime occurred

after.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown or the claimant was a juvenile. It is also not required for an adult claimant when no charges were filed for reasons other than the claimant's own wish and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.

rule.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown or the claimant was a juvenile. It is also not required for an adult claimant when no charges were filed for reasons other than the claimant's own wish and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.
rule.quote: The filing of a criminal charge shall be a prerequisite for receipt of compensation unless it is determined that no charges were filed due to the identity of the perpetrator being unknown: Provided, That no criminal charges need be filed if: (1) The claimant is an adult at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred and no criminal charges were filed for reasons other than the desire of the claimant and a law-enforcement agency confirms that the available evidence supports a finding that a crime occurred; or (2) the claimant was a juvenile at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-18 (Effect of no criminal charges)

before.summary: An award may be denied or reduced if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or the claim investigator.

after.summary: A commissioner may deny a claim, reduce an award, or reconsider an approved claim if the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement or the claim investigator.

rule.summary: A commissioner may deny a claim, reduce an award, or reconsider an approved claim if the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement or the claim investigator.
rule.quote: A commissioner, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law-enforcement agencies or the claim investigator, may deny a claim, reduce an award of compensation, or reconsider a claim already approved.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rule.summary: Sexual assault is listed among the crimes resulting in personal injury that the fund covers.
rule.quote: Murder Other Violent Crimes Robbery Sexual Assault Kidnapping Human Trafficking
rule.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Crimes Resulting in Personal Injury
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Fund: Eligibility, Benefits, and Applications

before.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program gives victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking and human trafficking a substitute address to use with state and local agencies, plus free first-class mail forwarding. You apply in person through an approved application assistant at a local victim service program.

after.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program is designed to help victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking and human trafficking deal with government agencies without risking that their home address gets out. You apply in person through an approved application assistant at a local victim service program.

rule.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program is designed to help victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking and human trafficking deal with government agencies without risking that their home address gets out. You apply in person through an approved application assistant at a local victim service program.
rule.quote: The West Virginia Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) is a program designed to help victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and human trafficking do business with government agencies and other entities without risking disclosure of their home address.
rule.pinpoint: WV Secretary of State ACP page; program created by W. Va. Code 48-28A-103(a)
rule.source_title: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), WV Secretary of State

before.summary: Only for a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition: the Fund's records and proceedings are confidential and the parties' identities may not be published. No West Virginia statute or rule found makes an adult survivor's compensation claim confidential.

after.summary: For a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition, the Fund's records and proceedings are confidential and may not be shared with anyone who is not a necessary participant.

rule.summary: For a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition, the Fund's records and proceedings are confidential and may not be shared with anyone who is not a necessary participant.
rule.quote: All crime victims’ compensation fund records and proceedings related to a claim filed on behalf of a minor child who is the subject of a civil abuse and neglect petition are confidential and may not be disclosed to any person who is not a necessary participant in the proceedings.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-11a (Application when the victim is the subject of a civil abuse or neglect petition; confidentiality of records)
