added.summary: For a catastrophic injury, the division may award up to $10,000 more than the maximum award, to cover future lost wages, special medical needs, and other special help the injury requires.
added.quote: In addition to the maximum award authorized in subsection (d) of this section, in the case of catastrophic injury the division may award an additional amount not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) to the victim to cover future lost wages, special medical needs and any other special assistance needed as a result of the injury.
added.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

added.summary: Losses that happen more than 24 months after the injury or the discovery of the crime are not paid.
added.quote: Compensation shall only be awarded for economic losses occurring within a twenty-four (24) month period from the date of the injury or discovery of the crime.
added.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

before.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000. A separate catastrophic injury award can add more (see notes).

after.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000.

rule.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000.
rule.quote: the maximum individual award of compensation paid to any victim or dependent shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000.00).
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

rule.summary: Counseling and other losses for an associated victim (such as a family or household member) are limited to $1,500 per year and $4,500 for the life of the claim, and count toward the primary victim's $15,000 award.
rule.quote: Associated victims may be eligible for compensation with regard to counseling and other economic losses in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00 per year for a maximum of $4,500.00 for the life of the claim (effective July 1, 2019). The compensation paid to an associated victim is included in the primary victim's award of $15,000.00.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Payment Threshold on Associated Victim Claims
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Losses are paid only if they happen within 24 months of the injury or discovery of the crime. The division can extend this by 12 months for mental health counseling, for a total of 36 months.

after.summary: The division can extend the 24-month limit by 12 more months for mental health counseling, for 36 months in all.

rule.summary: The division can extend the 24-month limit by 12 more months for mental health counseling, for 36 months in all.
rule.quote: However, the division may extend the twenty-four (24) month period to allow compensation for mental health counseling and care occurring within an additional twelve (12) month period for a total of thirty-six (36) months.
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

rule.summary: For counseling to be covered, the first session must be within 1 year of the crime; for juvenile victims reported after the filing period, within 1 year of the report.
rule.quote: The first counseling session must be within one (1) year of the date of the crime. The first counseling session for juvenile victims (crimes reported past the one year filing requirement) must be within one year of reporting date of the crime.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Mental Health Expenses
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage, for up to 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months total. The victim must have been employed at the time of the crime, and sick and vacation leave count as other sources.

after.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage. The limit is 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months in all.

rule.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage. The limit is 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months in all.
rule.quote: Maximum amount must not exceed the federal minimum hourly wage for eight (8) hours per day, or forty (40) hours per week, or one hundred seventy-three (173) hours per month up to three (3) months total.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Loss of Earnings, Financial Limits
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

params.scope: trips of at least 10 miles outside your home community

rule.summary: Travel is covered when a victim has to go at least 10 miles outside their home community for counseling, medical treatment not available locally, or to give a victim impact statement at sentencing. Mileage is paid at the state rate, with no separate cap beyond the total award.
rule.quote: Expenses incurred when required to travel at least ten (10) miles outside the home community to receive the following services.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Travel Expenses
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground (see the relocation caps).

after.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground.

rule.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground.
rule.quote: Victim may need to relocate if the crime scene was the home of the victim and returning would do greater harm to the victim.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Relocation, Requirements
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.

after.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other elective electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.

rule.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other elective electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.
rule.quote: Cell phones, laptops, tablets, and any other elective electronic devices are not covered under the CVCP, unless good cause is shown for reimbursement.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Replacement of Personal Property Seized as Evidence, Exemptions
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible for replacement.

after.summary: The benefit that replaces things police took as evidence does not cover things that were damaged or ruined in the crime.

rule.summary: The benefit that replaces things police took as evidence does not cover things that were damaged or ruined in the crime.
rule.quote: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Replacement of Personal Property Seized as Evidence
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

params.extension: The division may extend the time for good cause shown.
or later if the division allows more time for good cause

rule.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury. The division can allow more time for good cause.
rule.quote: The application for compensation is filed with the division within one (1) year after the date of the injury to or death of the victim, or within any extension of time the division allows for good cause shown
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-106, Eligibility for compensation (2025, via Justia)

before.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical, and the claimant must cooperate with law enforcement. The statute sets no fixed number of days and lists no alternative to a police report.

after.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical. The claimant must also cooperate with law enforcement.

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical. The claimant must also cooperate with law enforcement.
rule.quote: The appropriate law enforcement authorities were notified of the criminal act allegedly causing the injury to or death of the victim as soon as practical under the circumstance after perpetration of the offense and the claimant cooperates with appropriate law enforcement authorities with respect to the crime for which compensation is sought
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-106, Eligibility for compensation (2025, via Justia)

params.applies_to: mental health counseling only

params.scope: mental health counseling only

rule.summary: Program policy also accepts a valid order of protection instead of a police report, but only for mental health counseling claims. An ex parte (temporary) order is not enough.
rule.quote: A valid Order of Protection (Mental Health Counseling Only). A claim cannot be approved based on an Ex Parte Order of Protection.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Primary Victim Eligibility
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed. The crime only has to be reported to law enforcement.

after.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed to be eligible.

rule.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed to be eligible.
rule.quote: No arrest, prosecution, nor conviction is necessary to be eligible.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation FAQ, Does There Have To Be An Arrest Or Conviction
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

before.summary: The division can make an emergency award of up to $1,000 before a hearing if waiting would cause undue hardship. It is subtracted from the final award.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.
rule.quote: The amount of an emergency award to an applicant shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-111, Emergency awards; limitation (2025, via Justia)

params.scope: only information already covered by a confidentiality privilege under Wyoming law

rule.summary: By statute, information in victims' compensation claim files and records that is covered by a confidentiality privilege under Wyoming law stays confidential and is not open to public inspection. It is also shielded from legal process and cannot be used as evidence in any proceeding without the consent of the person who gave it.
rule.quote: Information contained in the claim files and records of victims, which are subject to any privilege of confidentiality under Wyoming law, shall remain confidential and shall not be open to public inspection. The information shall be immune from legal process and shall not, without the consent of the person furnishing the information, be admitted as evidence or used for any purpose in any action, suit or other judicial, legislative or administrative proceeding.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, W.S. 1-40-101 to 1-40-119 (copy posted by DVS)

added.summary: Relocation requests need the Request for Relocation Assistance form completed before expenses are covered.

added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Relocation
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.pinpoint: VCCB Application page, Additional Forms, Rental Assistance
added.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Alaska's new Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Administration, gives an enrolled person a post office box to use as a substitute mailing address and forwards their mail, and state and municipal agencies must accept that address. A victim of a crime involving sexual assault, domestic violence, or stalking can enroll if a court has issued a protective order for them or they meet other standards the department sets. The department must still adopt regulations setting out how to enroll.
added.quote: (2) designate a post office box as a substitute mailing address for an 02 individual enrolled in the program; 03 (3) forward the mail of an individual enrolled in the program from the 04 post office box designated under (2) of this subsection to the individual's residential 05 street address, post office box, school address, or work address as specified on the 06 individual's application for enrollment in the program; 07 (4) maintain the confidentiality of the address of an individual enrolled 08 in the program; and 09 (5) adopt regulations establishing a procedure for a qualified individual 10 under (c) of this section to enroll in or withdraw from the program. 11 (c) The following individuals may enroll in the program: 12 (1) a victim of a crime involving domestic violence, stalking, or sexual 13 assault if 14 (A) a court has issued a protective order on behalf of the 15 victim; or 16 (B) the victim meets other standards set by the department;
added.pinpoint: AS 44.21.022(b)(2) to (c)(1), enacted by sec. 75 of Chapter 9 SLA 26 (HB 239), effective July 1, 2026 under sec. 94; agencies must accept the address under AS 44.21.022(e)
added.source_title: Enrolled HB 239 (Chapter 9 SLA 26), sec. 75 enacting AS 44.21.022, Address confidentiality program (Alaska Legislature bill text)

added.summary: By statute, a compensation application and personally identifying information about the applicant are confidential records that the Violent Crimes Compensation Board may not release.
added.quote: An application for compensation and personally identifying information relating to an applicant for compensation are confidential records and may not be released by the board.
added.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

params.condition: if you are 16 or older

rule.summary: Police, a hospital, or anyone else may not make a sexual assault survivor age 16 or older pay for the evidence exam, directly or through their health insurance.
rule.quote: A law enforcement agency, health care facility, or other entity may not require a victim of sexual assault under AS 11.41.410 — 11.41.425 who is 16 years of age or older to pay, directly or indirectly, through health insurance or any other means, for the costs of examination of the victim necessary for (1) collecting evidence using the sexual assault examination kit under AS 18.68.010 or otherwise; or (2) determining whether a sexual assault has occurred.
rule.source_title: AS 18.68.010 to 18.68.040, Sexual Assault Examinations (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The Alaska Department of Law tells survivors that sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to them. This page does not address insurance billing; AK-EXAM-1 (the statute) does.

after.summary: The Alaska Department of Law's victims' rights handbook says sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to victims, and cites AS 18.68.040.

rule.summary: The Alaska Department of Law's victims' rights handbook says sexual assault exams are provided at no cost to victims, and cites AS 18.68.040.
rule.quote: Victims of sexual assaults should obtain sexual assault examinations as soon as possible after the crime has occurred. These exams are provided at no cost to victims [AS 18.68.040].
rule.pinpoint: Alaska Department of Law, Victims' Rights Handbook, Crimes of Sexual Assault
rule.source_title: Alaska Department of Law, Victims' Rights Handbook

rule.summary: The most the board can award is $40,000 per victim per incident.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under this chapter in an amount in excess of $40,000 per victim per incident.
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days, or within five days of when a report could reasonably have been made. The statute lists no alternative to a police report for sexual assault.

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

after.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days. If it could not reasonably be reported that soon, it must be reported within five days of when it reasonably could be.

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police within five days. If it could not reasonably be reported that soon, it must be reported within five days of when it reasonably could be.
rule.quote: the personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense listed in AS 18.67.101 that had been reported to the police within five days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

before.summary: The board may also look at whether the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors where appropriate.

after.summary: The board can pay only if it finds that the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors when that was appropriate.

rule.summary: The board can pay only if it finds that the applicant cooperated with police and prosecutors when that was appropriate.
rule.quote: in the discretion of the board, the applicant has cooperated with law enforcement and prosecution officials to further prosecution of the offender if appropriate
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

params.scope: prosecution or conviction, not the police report

rule.summary: An award can be made even if no one is prosecuted or convicted.
rule.quote: An order may be made under this section whether or not a person is prosecuted or convicted of an offense arising out of the act that caused the injury or death involved in the application.
rule.source_title: AS 18.67.010 to 18.67.180, Violent Crimes Compensation Board (Alaska Statutes, print view)

rule.summary: A direct victim's initial counseling award covers up to 24 sessions. The first evaluation and intake session is paid in full, and later sessions with a licensed mental health provider are paid up to $200 each. More sessions can be requested with a treatment plan.
rule.quote: Counseling – Direct Victims: Initial maximum award is 24 sessions. Secondary Victims: initial maximum 12 sessions VCCB will pay first evaluation and intake session in full. Payment after first session: $200/session for services provided by a licensed mental health provider
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Benefits at a Glance, Mental Health Therapy, Payment Maximums
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Benefits at a Glance (last revised July 2026)

rule.summary: Lost wage payments cover only leave without pay, not days already covered by paid leave.
rule.quote: Compensation is limited to leave without pay.
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application, Section 7: Lost Wage Information
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

before.summary: Relocation is covered when the survivor's health or safety is at risk because of the crime.

after.summary: Moving costs can be paid only in some cases, for example when the crime may put your health or safety at risk.

rule.summary: Moving costs can be paid only in some cases, for example when the crime may put your health or safety at risk.
rule.quote: Relocation may only be eligible specific instances, such as when an individuals health or safety may be at risk as a direct result of the crime.
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

params.scope: a cell phone that was damaged or taken as evidence

rule.summary: A cell phone that was damaged or taken as evidence can be covered.
rule.quote: Cell phone (damaged or taken for evidence)
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application, Claim Application and Instructions, covered expenses
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB Application for Crime Victim Compensation (05/2026)

rule.summary: Property loss or damage is generally not covered; essential items taken as evidence (and phones) are limited exceptions.
rule.quote: Note: VCCB does not generally cover property loss or damage, these are limited exceptions.
rule.pinpoint: VCCB Application and Forms, Property Replacement
rule.source_title: Alaska VCCB, Application and Forms page

added.summary: Medical bills that are still unpaid (not psychiatric care, counseling, or dental) may be paid at a reduced rate of 30% of eligible charges, up to $6,000. Medical bills you already paid yourself may be paid back in full, up to $15,000.
added.quote: Outstanding charges for medical treatment, excluding psychiatric care, counseling, and dental treatment, may be compensated at a reduced rate of thirty percent (30%) of eligible charges up to a maximum amount of six thousand dollars ($6,000). When the claimant has already paid out-of-pocket for medical treatment and services, the claimant may be fully reimbursed for all eligible expenses not to exceed $15,000.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: If the survivor has health insurance, the pharmacy, hospital, or clinic filling the prescription must first seek payment from the insurance.
added.quote: If a victim of sexual violence has health insurance, the pharmacy, hospital, or medical clinic filling the prescription for HIV prophylaxis must first seek payment of the expense from the health insurance provider.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission, P.O. Box 231267, Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267.
added.quote: The completed application can be returned by: FAX: (334)290-4455 Email: info@acvcc.alabama.gov Mail: Alabama Crime Victims Compensation Commission P.O. Box 231267 Montgomery, Alabama 36123-1267
added.pinpoint: Compensation page, How Do I File A Claim?
added.source_title: ACVCC: Compensation

added.summary: Email the completed application to info@acvcc.alabama.gov.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Fax the completed application to 334-290-4455.
added.quote: Please download the completed application and email it to info@acvcc.alabama.gov or fax it to 334-290-4455.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, submission box
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: The application must be signed; a fax or electronic signature is accepted, but the Commission may ask for an original notarized signature.
added.quote: The claimant must submit an application that has been signed by either facsimile signature or electronic signature.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.02

added.summary: Include proof of U.S. citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.quote: You must submit proof of US citizenship or that you are an alien eligible for public benefits.
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: Include a copy of the police report if one is available.
added.quote: Complete this section and, if one is available, provide a copy of the Police Report.
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For each type of compensation you request, include the related bills or receipts.
added.quote: Provide any corresponding and directly related bills/receipts.
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you are asking for medical expenses, the victim or a representative must sign and date the health information authorization in the application.
added.quote: Either the patient (victim) or their representative must sign and date this authorization if consideration of medical expenses is being requested.
added.pinpoint: Application, Patient Authorization for Use and Disclosure of Protected Health Information
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If you file more than one year after the incident, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The claim must be filed within one (1) year of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, explain the good cause in writing.
added.quote: The crime must be reported to the proper law enforcement agency within 72 hours of the incident, or good cause must be submitted in writing.
added.source_title: ACVCC: Application Form page

added.summary: If someone other than the victim signs as claimant, include documentation that they are legally authorized to act for the victim.
added.quote: The claimant (if other than victim) must be the person legally authorized to act on the behalf of the victim. Documentation of this authority must be provided.
added.pinpoint: Application, Claim Authorization page, signature note
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: If the victim is 19 or older but incapacitated, include proof of guardianship or conservatorship.
added.quote: If the victim is 19 or older, but is incapacitated, you will have to provide proof of guardianship/conservatorship over the victim.
added.source_title: ACVCC application for compensation (MAR 2026)

added.summary: For lost wages, include written documentation from your employer or a W-2.
added.quote: Lost wages shall be verified by obtaining written documentation from the employer or by submission of a W-2 tax document.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For lost wages, if you are self-employed, include a tax transcript from the IRS.
added.quote: A tax transcript from the IRS is required if the person seeking reimbursement of his/her lost wages is self-employed.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: A sexual assault victim can claim up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse; beyond two weeks, include a doctor's excuse.
added.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse. A doctor's excuse must be provided for lost wages in excess of two weeks to be considered for reimbursement.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For counseling, the Commission needs a letter from the clinician certifying that therapy is necessary because of the victimization.
added.quote: ACVCC must receive a letter from the clinician certifying that the victim is engaged in necessary therapy due to his/her victimization.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For ongoing counseling, the clinician must send quarterly updates certifying the treatment is still necessary.
added.quote: Quarterly updates from the clinician certifying that the treatment is necessary and the result of victimization must be submitted in order for payment to be considered.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For counseling, the clinician must provide an itemized bill for the treatment sessions.
added.quote: The clinician must provide an itemized bill for treatment sessions.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

added.summary: For moving expenses, include written estimates or receipts.
added.quote: Written estimates and/or receipts are required for payment of moving expenses.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: For temporary relocation, include a copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or another verifiable document.
added.quote: A copy of the hotel bill, credit card receipt, or other verifiable document is required for verification.
added.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

added.summary: The Commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who applied for compensation, or the facts of the crime against them.
added.quote: The commission may not disclose the names and addresses of victims or claimants who have applied for compensation pursuant to this article or the facts or circumstances of the criminally injurious conduct perpetrated against them.
added.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-4 (Justia)

before.summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Commission pays for forensic exams and STI prevention treatment after sexual abuse crimes.

after.summary: State law lets the Commission pay for forensic exams that collect evidence after sexual abuse crimes, and for treatment to prevent sexually transmitted infections.

rule.summary: State law lets the Commission pay for forensic exams that collect evidence after sexual abuse crimes, and for treatment to prevent sexually transmitted infections.
rule.quote: Provide for the cost of forensic medical examinations for the purpose of gathering evidence and treatment for preventing sexually transmitted infections in sexual abuse crimes and offenses.
rule.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-5 (Justia)

before.summary: When the victim is a minor, individual therapy is limited to 15 sessions (except when the victim is deceased).

after.summary: When the victim is a minor, the person who files the claim is limited to 15 individual therapy sessions, unless the victim has died.

rule.summary: When the victim is a minor, the person who files the claim is limited to 15 individual therapy sessions, unless the victim has died.
rule.quote: When the victim is a minor, the claimant shall be limited to 15 individual therapy sessions, unless the victim is deceased.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.07

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 9, 2020, lost wages are paid at up to $400 a week for up to 26 weeks.
rule.quote: For incidents of criminally injurious conduct occurring on or after July 9, 2020, lost wages are limited to $400.00 per week for a maximum of 26 weeks.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rule.summary: A sexual assault victim can get up to two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's note. Employer verification is still required.
rule.quote: A victim of sexual assault may be granted compensation for maximum of two weeks of lost wages without a doctor's excuse.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rule.summary: Moving and temporary relocation together are capped at $1,000.
rule.quote: Moving and temporary relocation expenses may not exceed a combined total of $1,000.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.scope: travel for medical and psychological treatment needed because of the crime

rule.summary: Travel for medical and psychological treatment needed because of the crime can be covered.
rule.quote: Travel may be allowed for medical and psychological treatment that is needed as a result of the victimization.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

before.summary: If a survivor is at risk of HIV exposure, the Commission may pay for a 28-day course of HIV prophylaxis, including directly to the survivor. Health insurance has to be billed first.

params.scope: a 28-day course of HIV prevention medicine, if you are at risk of HIV exposure

after.summary: If a survivor is at risk of HIV exposure, the Commission may pay for a 28-day course of HIV prophylaxis, including directly to the survivor.

rule.summary: If a survivor is at risk of HIV exposure, the Commission may pay for a 28-day course of HIV prophylaxis, including directly to the survivor.
rule.quote: If it is determined that a victim of sexual violence is at risk for exposure to HIV, the Commission may provide payment for a 28-day drug regimen of HIV prophylaxis to a SANE facility, hospital, medical clinic, pharmacy, or victim of sexual violence.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-11-.01

params.scope: windows and locks for a home you own, or rent and must pay to repair

rule.summary: Listed under the property rule as an allowed item: windows and locks for a home the victim owns, or rents when the victim must pay for repairs.
rule.quote: Security enhancement. Windows and locks for real property owned by the claimant/victim; and windows and locks for rental property leased by the claimant/victim when the claimant/victim is financially responsible for repair(s) to the leased property.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

rule.summary: The Commission does not reimburse or replace property, so a lost or damaged phone or other personal item is not covered. The only items listed under this rule are security windows and locks and damaged prescription eyeglasses.
rule.quote: The Commission does not provide property reimbursement or replacement.
rule.source_title: Ala. Admin. Code r. 262-X-4-.04

params.extension: good cause
or later if the Commission finds good cause

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within one year of the injury, unless the Commission finds good cause for filing late.
rule.quote: A claim has been filed with the commission later than one year after the injury or death upon which the claim is based, unless the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to file within that time.
rule.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

before.summary: The crime has to be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours unless the Commission finds good cause for the delay. No sexual-assault-specific alternative to a police report was found.

params.exception: or later if the Commission finds good cause

after.summary: The crime has to be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the Commission finds good cause for the delay.

rule.summary: The crime has to be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the Commission finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: The criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer later than 72 hours after its occurrence, unless the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rule.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-12 (Justia)

params.rule: Crimes that happen in Alabama are covered.

before.summary: Crimes committed in Alabama are covered regardless of where the victim lives.

params.rule: Crimes in Alabama that cause serious personal injury or death can qualify; the victim does not have to live in Alabama.

after.summary: A crime in Alabama, or an attempt, that causes serious injury or death can qualify, wherever the victim lives.

rule.summary: A crime in Alabama, or an attempt, that causes serious injury or death can qualify, wherever the victim lives.
rule.quote: An act occurring or attempted within the geographical boundaries of this state which results in serious personal injury or death to a victim for which punishment by fine, imprisonment, or death may be imposed.
rule.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-3 (Justia)

before.summary: Alabama residents hurt by a crime in another US state can qualify if they had a permanent home in Alabama and meet one of the listed conditions (for example, a job in Alabama or full-time student out of state).

after.summary: Citizens of Alabama hurt by a crime in another US state can qualify if they had a permanent home in Alabama and meet one of the listed conditions (for example, a job in Alabama or full-time student out of state).

rule.summary: Citizens of Alabama hurt by a crime in another US state can qualify if they had a permanent home in Alabama and meet one of the listed conditions (for example, a job in Alabama or full-time student out of state).
rule.quote: provided however, the citizen at the time such act was committed had a permanent place of residence within the geographical boundaries of this state
rule.source_title: Ala. Code 15-23-3 (Justia)

added.summary: If the board finds the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement, it may deny, withdraw, or reduce the award. This does not apply to a minor victim of a sex offense or a victim of human trafficking.
added.quote: Except as provided in subdivision (c)(2) of this section, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, the board may deny, withdraw, or reduce an award of reparations. (2) This subsection does not apply if the claimant or victim is a victim of human trafficking or a minor victim of a sex offense, as defined in § 12-12-903.
added.source_title: A.C.A. 16-90-712 (2025), Conditions for reparations

added.summary: The program offers an online application, which its Documents and Forms page marks as the preferred way to apply.
added.quote: We offer an ONLINE APPLICATION process for Victim Compensation! Access the Online Application
added.pinpoint: CVRB home page, Crime Victim Compensation Application
added.source_title: Arkansas DPS, Crime Victims Reparations Board home page

added.summary: A paper application can be sent to the Crime Victims Reparations office, listed on the DPS site at 322 South Main Street, Suite 615, Little Rock, AR 72201.
added.quote: Victims may apply for compensation by submitting an application to the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office. Applications are available from the Arkansas Crime Victim's Reparations office or from one of Arkansas's 28 elected prosecutors. These programs are funded by fees collected from criminal offenders and a federal grant through the Victims of Crime Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Justice. Contact CVRB 322 South Main Street, Suite 615 Little Rock, AR 72201
added.pinpoint: About CVRB page, applying and Contact CVRB
added.source_title: Arkansas DPS, About CVRB page

added.summary: Attach a copy of the law enforcement agency's incident report to the application.

added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: When asking for medical or counseling costs, attach copies of all itemized medical and counseling bills or other statements verifying the expenses.
added.quote: NOTE: In addition to completing this section, you must attach copies of all itemized medical bills, mental health counseling bills, or other statements verifying expenses.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section C, Request for Medical Treatment/Mental-Health Counseling
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, attach your most recent pay stub, or if self-employed, your tax returns from the last three years.
added.quote: Attach a copy of your most recent pay stub from your employer. If you are self-employed, you must furnish copies of your tax returns from the last three (3) years so lost wages can be most accurately determined.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, give the name and address of the physician who can verify your time off, or attach a recent disability statement.
added.quote: You must also provide the complete name and address of the physician who can verify your disability period, or you may attach a copy of a recent disability statement.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section D, Request for Lost Wages
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, include a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate.
added.quote: NOTE: You must submit a copy of the funeral bill and the death certificate with this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section E, Request for Funeral/Burial Expenses
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For loss of support after a victim's death, include the victim's last three years of tax returns, Social Security benefit verification, and proof of guardianship for a minor dependent.
added.quote: NOTE: You must attach copies of the deceased victim's last three (3) years' tax returns. You must also provide verification regarding the denial or receipt of any benefits from the Social Security Administration. You must be the legal guardian of a minor dependent to request loss of support on their behalf and must provide verification of guardianship.

added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: For crime scene cleanup, attach receipts or other supporting documentation.

added.pinpoint: Application, Section G, Request for Assistance with Crime Scene Clean Up
added.source_title: Arkansas CVRB, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (10-6-2023)

added.summary: Arkansas's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the DFA Office of Driver Services, is free and puts a post office box on the driver's license or ID card instead of the home address. It is only for victims of domestic violence and their dependents, and the person must also present a valid order of protection under the Domestic Abuse Act and an affidavit. Sexual abuse counts as domestic violence only when it is by a family or household member or a dating partner.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program is a free program administered by the Office of Driver Services. Participants in tis program will be issued a driver’s license or identification card that displays a post office box in lieu of a residential address.
added.pinpoint: DFA Address Confidentiality Program page, Program Description
added.source_title: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: Medical treatment documents a claimant submits with a reparations application are confidential by statute, and so are law enforcement investigative reports if another law makes them confidential. The statute does not make the whole claim file or the applicant's identity confidential.
added.quote: When submitted to the Crime Victims Reparations Board as part of an application, the following information shall be confidential: (1) Documents submitted by a claimant which relate to medical treatment; and (2) Law enforcement investigative reports, if confidential under any other law.

rule.summary: Survivors are exempt from paying for a sexual assault medical-legal exam received within 96 hours of the attack. The 96-hour limit can be waived for a minor or when the board finds good cause.

rule.summary: Under the board's rules, good cause for a late police report includes the victim's physical incapacity, mental incompetence, or age. It also includes an injury that could not reasonably be discovered. Other reasons can count too.

Factors evidencing that a sexual assault crime has occurred may include, but are not limited to, medical records documenting injuries consistent with allegations of sexual assault, mental health records, or that the victim received a sexual assault examination.

rule.quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
rule.pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
rule.source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

rule.summary: Travel to and from medical appointments is not an eligible expense.
rule.quote: Property loss and damage, pain and suffering, and travel to and from medical appointments are not eligible expenses.
rule.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

rule.summary: The statute bars compensation for property crime losses and for pain and suffering.
rule.quote: no compensation shall be awarded for losses sustained for crimes against property or for noneconomic detriment such as pain and suffering
rule.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params.extension: waiver available, including for physical, emotional or psychological injury, minors not at fault, and good cause with compelling equitable circumstances

after.summary: The application must be made within 3 years after the date of the injury.

rule.summary: The application must be made within 3 years after the date of the injury.
rule.quote: the application has been made within three years after the date of the personal injury or death
rule.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

before.summary: The crime must be reported to police, but a sexual assault survivor does not lose eligibility for skipping the report if they went to a health care facility within 120 hours for an evidence collection exam, or met the disclosure or protective order rules of section 54-209(d).

params.exam_condition: done within 120 hours of the assault

after.summary: The crime must be reported to police, but a sexual assault survivor does not lose eligibility for skipping the report if they went to a health care facility within 120 hours of the assault for an evidence collection exam, or met the disclosure or protective order rules of section 54-209(d).

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police, but a sexual assault survivor does not lose eligibility for skipping the report if they went to a health care facility within 120 hours of the assault for an evidence collection exam, or met the disclosure or protective order rules of section 54-209(d).
rule.quote: (C) such incident or offense has been reported to the police, except that a victim of a sexual assault shall not be ineligible for the payment of compensation by reason of failing to make a report pursuant to this subparagraph if such victim presented himself or herself to a health care facility within one hundred twenty hours of such sexual assault for examination and collection of evidence of such sexual assault in accordance with the provisions of section 19a-112a , or if such victim complied with subsection (d) of section 54-209 .
rule.source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

after.summary: To decide on an award, the office looks at what matters in the case. This includes anything the victim did that helped cause the injury, how much the victim helped the office check the claim, and how much the victim helped police catch and prosecute the offender.

rule.summary: To decide on an award, the office looks at what matters in the case. This includes anything the victim did that helped cause the injury, how much the victim helped the office check the claim, and how much the victim helped police catch and prosecute the offender.
rule.quote: shall consider all circumstances determined to be relevant, including, but not limited to, provocation, consent or any other behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to such victim's injury or death, the extent of the victim's cooperation in investigating the application and the extent of the victim's cooperation with law enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend and prosecute the offender

added.summary: The program may waive the time limits to apply and to report to police for good cause. Serious health or safety concerns can count.
added.quote: The time limit requirements of this section may be waived for good cause shown, including compelling health or safety concerns.
added.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

added.summary: A new 1-year window opens if a request to change the offender's sentence is filed or decided. The same is true for any other motion after conviction in a case where you were the victim.
added.quote: (C) The filing or resolution of a first application, or any subsequent application entertained by the court, for a sentence modification as described in § 24-403.03 ; (D) The filing or resolution of a motion to modify a term of imprisonment as described in § 24-403.04 ; or (E) The filing or resolution of any other post-conviction motion in which the claimant was a victim or secondary victim
added.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

added.summary: Email the completed application and supporting documents to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov.
added.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the CVCP office at 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001.
added.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: Drop off the completed application in person at the CVCP office, 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001, or at a remote site.
added.quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: The application page also lists fax as a way to submit: 202-879-4230.
added.pinpoint: CVCP Application page, ways to submit
added.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

added.summary: Apply online through the self-guided interactive interview linked from the D.C. Courts.
added.quote: OR ONLINE AT Self-Guided Interactive Interview Application https://lawhelpinteractive.org/Interview/Gene rateInterview/8116/engine
added.pinpoint: CVCP Information Brochure, Where can I get an application?
added.source_title: CVCP Information Brochure (English)

added.summary: Include a valid photo ID with the application.
added.quote: DOCUMENTS NEEDED • CVCP Application • Valid Photo ID
added.source_title: CVCP Information Brochure (English)

added.summary: Include a copy of the DC police report or DC civil protection order, plus any bills or receipts you want reimbursed.
added.quote: submit it along with a copy of your DC police report or DC civil protection order (the program does not accept temporary restraining orders), any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
added.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

added.summary: A forensic medical examination is one of the crime documentation options on the application.
added.quote: Forensic medical examination
added.pinpoint: CVCP Application (rev. 4/21/23), p.2, Documentation of Crime
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: Send any bills or receipts you want the program to reimburse.
added.quote: any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
added.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

added.summary: Submit copies of all medical, dental, or mental health bills received so far.
added.quote: Submit copies of all available bills received to date.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: Attach all insurance payment statements and denials for treatment costs.
added.quote: Attach all insurance payment statements and rejections.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: The program will ask you to complete authorization and release forms.
added.quote: YOU WILL BE REQUIRED TO COMPLETE AUTHORIZATION AND RELEASE FORMS
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: For lost wages, submit a disability statement from the doctor who can verify how long you could not work.
added.quote: (Please submit disability statement from the verifying doctor)
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: If you are self-employed and claiming lost wages, attach your federal income tax returns for the 12 months before the crime.
added.quote: If yes, you must attach a copy of your Federal Income Tax Returns for the last 12 months preceding crime.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: For temporary housing or moving expenses, submit a copy of the lease and a referral form.
added.quote: If yes, submit a copy of lease. A referral form must also be submitted.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: If your car was held as evidence, submit copies of your alternate transportation receipts.
added.quote: Please submit copy of transportation receipts.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: When listing dependents or secondary victims, submit copies of the children's birth certificates.
added.quote: Submit copies of birth certificates for children.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: If you apply online, complete the Confidential Information form and attach it at the end of the online interview.
added.quote: Please click here to complete a Confidential Information form. Once completed, you can attach it at the end of the online interactive interview that you are completing, such as the Crime Victims Compensation Form.
added.pinpoint: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims
added.source_title: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims (guided online CVCP application)

added.summary: Allow 5 business days for a CVCP team member to review the application.
added.quote: Please allow 5 business days for a CVCP team member to review your compensation application.
added.source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

added.summary: D.C.'s Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, gives eligible D.C. residents who fear for their safety and have experienced sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking a legal substitute address that District agencies must accept, plus forwarding of first-class, certified, and registered mail. Applicants must also have moved recently, plan to move soon, or have kept their current address off public records, and apply through an application assistant.
added.quote: The District’s Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), administered by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), provides a legal substitute address for eligible DC residents to maintain the confidentiality of her or his actual address.
added.pinpoint: OVSJG Address Confidentiality Program page, program description
added.source_title: Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: Information, records, and hearing transcripts in compensation claim files are confidential and not open to public inspection. The law lists exceptions.
added.quote: Information, records, and transcripts of hearings contained in the claims files under the provisions of this chapter are confidential and not open to public inspection
added.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-511, Confidentiality

before.summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. A victim who cares for more than 2 children living with them may get up to $5,000 more per child, starting with the third child.

params.exception: or more if you care for more than 2 children who live with you

after.summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or main caregiver of more than 2 children who live or lived with them, the program may award up to $5,000 more for each child living with the claimant, starting with the third child.

rule.summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or main caregiver of more than 2 children who live or lived with them, the program may award up to $5,000 more for each child living with the claimant, starting with the third child.
rule.quote: The Court shall not award compensation in an amount exceeding $25,000 per victimization; except, that: (1) If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or primary caregiver to more than 2 children who reside or resided with the victim, the Court may award additional compensation to the claimant of up to $5,000 for each child who resides with the claimant, beginning with the third child
rule.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

params.scope: counseling from a licensed provider

rule.summary: Out-patient mental health counseling needed because of the crime is covered when provided by a licensed psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, marriage, family, or child counselor, or a counselor licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling.
rule.quote: Out-patient mental health counseling expenses which became necessary as a direct result of the crime and which are provided by a: (i) Licensed psychiatrist or psychologist; (ii) Licensed social worker; (iii) Licensed marriage, family, or child counselor practicing within the scope of licensure; or (iv) Individual licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling
rule.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

before.summary: Pain and suffering, and the value of property damaged or taken during the crime (for example a phone or other belongings), are not economic loss and are not paid.

after.summary: Pain and suffering are not paid, and neither is the value of property damaged or taken during the crime.

rule.summary: Pain and suffering are not paid, and neither is the value of property damaged or taken during the crime.
rule.quote: “Economic loss” does not mean: (i) Pain and suffering; (ii) The value of any property damaged or taken during the crime;
rule.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

rule.summary: The program cannot pay attorney's fees for help filing an application. A fee may be awarded only for an appeal.
rule.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Program cannot pay attorney's fees for assisting a victim with the filing of a compensation application.
rule.pinpoint: CVCP Application page, Information on Attorneys
rule.source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params.extension: one year from learning of the program if the delay in learning of it was reasonable

before.summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime, or within one year after learning of the program if the delay in learning of it was reasonable. Other one-year windows run from certain post-conviction filings.

params.extension: If you learned of the program later, you may have 1 year from then if the delay was reasonable.

after.summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime. If you learned of the program later and the delay was reasonable, you have one year from when you learned of it.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime. If you learned of the program later and the delay was reasonable, you have one year from when you learned of it.
rule.quote: The claimant filed a claim under this subchapter within one year after: (A) The crime occurred; (B) Learning of the Program, with an adequate showing that the delay in learning of the Program was reasonable;
rule.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

rule.summary: A sexual assault survivor can meet the reporting requirement without a police report by getting a temporary or final civil protection order or a forensic medical exam, or by reporting to law enforcement any time before the statute of limitations runs out.
rule.quote: In the case of a sexual assault victim: (A) Obtaining a: (i) Temporary civil protection order or civil protection order from the Court; or (ii) Forensic medical examination; or (B) Reporting the offense to a law enforcement office before expiration of the applicable statute of limitations for that offense
rule.source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

added.summary: Delaware's victim compensation law applies to victims of crimes committed in Delaware, including people who do not live there. That law includes the free forensic exam rule.
added.quote: This chapter shall apply to: (1) All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: You do not need a lawyer before the Appeals Board, but if you have one, the Board may award an amount for the lawyer's services.
added.quote: A claimant need not be represented by an attorney before the Appeals Board, but if such person is represented the Appeals Board may award an amount for services rendered.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: The program may not turn away a claim from sexual assault or abuse of a child because it was filed late.
added.quote: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the Agency may not limit acceptance or consideration of any applications arising from sexual assault or abuse of a child which may have otherwise been barred from consideration by a statute of limitations.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: If the crime happened before your eighteenth birthday, the program may pay for mental health counseling. This holds even if you applied late, did not report to police in time, or did not cooperate with police. The crime must be properly documented, and you must apply before your twentieth birthday.
added.quote: Notwithstanding the provision of paragraph (10) of this section and § 9010(a)(3), (4), and (5) of this title to the contrary, the Agency may make an award for the payment of mental health counseling services under this chapter on a claim made by the victim of a crime that occurred before the victim’s eighteenth birthday so long as the occurrence of the crime is appropriately documented, and the claim is filed before the victim’s twentieth birthday.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: For sexual assault or abuse, that twentieth-birthday limit does not apply.
added.quote: However, the foregoing limitations in this paragraph (11) regarding the victim’s twentieth birthday do not apply in cases of crimes involving sexual assault or abuse.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: If you were a child when the sexual assault or abuse happened, the program cannot deny your claim just because you waited to report or to apply.
added.quote: In no event may the Agency deny any claim solely because the victim was a child victim of sexual assault or abuse, and the victim either delayed reporting the abuse or assault to authorities or the victim delayed an application for services to mitigate the effects of the impact of sexual assault or abuse.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: Mail the claim form to VCAP at 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801.
added.quote: You must submit a claim form to get the process started. Your claim can be submitted in the following ways: Mail: 900 N. King Street, 4th Floor Wilmington, DE 19801
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Fax the claim form to VCAP at (302) 577-1326.
added.quote: Fax: (302) 577-1326 If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Apply online through the VCAP claim portal at https://ccvcde.org.
added.quote: If you would prefer to apply online, please visit: https://ccvcde.org
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), How do I file a claim?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: The claim must be filed in writing on VCAP's own claim form and signed by the claimant.
added.quote: All claims filed with the Agency must be in writing on the Agency's provided claim form and signed by the claimant.
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

added.summary: The official claim form includes subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements that must be part of the filing.
added.quote: claims must be filed in the office of VCAP on official forms which include subrogation, authorization, and consent agreements.
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Every loss must be backed by documentation before VCAP awards compensation.
added.quote: All losses must be supported by documentation prior to compensation being awarded.
added.pinpoint: Delaware DOJ VCAP page, FAQs, Are there any limits?
added.source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

added.summary: If VCAP asks for more documentation while investigating, it must be sent within 45 days of the request.
added.quote: If VCAP, in its investigation of a claim, requires further documentation from the claimant, such documentation must be submitted to VCAP no later than 45 days of the date of VCAP's request.
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: Survivors claiming temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs must send documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request.
added.quote: A victim who seeks compensation for temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture and/or moving expenses must submit documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request therefor, unless an extension is granted by the Agency.
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: If the injury happened on the job, the survivor must file a workers' compensation claim and send proof of it before applying to VCAP.
added.quote: If the victim seeks compensation for an injury sustained while in the course and scope of employment, the victim must submit a claim for worker's compensation, and provide documentation thereof, before making application to VCAP for compensation.
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: To ask for an emergency award, the claimant must request it in writing with the claim form and show just cause.
added.quote: The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered.
added.source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

added.summary: A decision on a claim can take up to 60 days, and longer in rare cases.
added.quote: It can take up to 60 days to make a decision on your claim. In rare cases, it can take longer.
added.pinpoint: VCAP brochure (English), What can I expect next?
added.source_title: VCAP brochure (English)

added.summary: Delaware's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Justice, gives certified participants a substitute address and forwards their mail. Victims of sexual assault can apply if they have filed for a protection from abuse order or are named as a victim in a criminal or delinquency case, and they state that they fear future violence from the perpetrator.
added.quote: All of the following persons are eligible to apply to become program participants: (1) A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, kidnapping, or stalking who has filed for a protection from abuse order or who is or was named as a victim in any criminal or delinquency proceeding
added.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 96, subch. II, Address Confidentiality Act (sections 9611 to 9619)

added.summary: Under Delaware's Freedom of Information Act, the investigative files the Victims' Compensation Assistance Program compiles or maintains are not public records.
added.quote: (14) Investigative files compiled or maintained by the Victims’ Compensation Assistance Program
added.source_title: 29 Del. C. ch. 100, Freedom of Information Act

before.summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must give sexual offense forensic medical exams free of charge, and the survivor pays no out-of-pocket cost and does not have to file a compensation application for the exam. The provider bills the patient's insurance first.

after.summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.

rule.summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.
rule.quote: The victim of the sexual offense shall not pay any out-of-pocket costs associated with the forensic medical examination and shall not be required to file an application with the Agency.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must provide forensic medical exams free of charge to sexual offense victims.
rule.quote: Hospitals and health-care professionals shall provide forensic medical examinations free of charge to the victims of sexual offenses.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

before.summary: The provider must bill the patient's insurance (including Medicaid and Medicare) first; whatever insurance does not cover can be billed to the Victims' Compensation Fund, not the survivor.

after.summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.

rule.summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rule.quote: Any hospital or health-care professional performing a forensic medical examination shall seek reimbursement for the examination from the patient's insurance carrier, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If insurance is unavailable, or does not cover the full costs of the forensic medical examination, the service provider may seek reimbursement from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.exception: or up to $50,000 if you are left fully and permanently disabled

rule.summary: Total compensation is capped at $25,000, or up to $50,000 for victims who are permanently and totally disabled.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded under the chapter to a claimant in a total amount in excess of $25,000; provided, however, that the Agency may award compensation to victims who are permanently and totally disabled in an amount not to exceed $50,000.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: replacing items seized as evidence

rule.summary: Replacing items seized as evidence is covered; this is separate from the general bar on property loss.
rule.quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.scope: the deposit plus up to 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider

rule.summary: Child care is covered, limited to the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed provider.
rule.quote: l. Child care not to exceed the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: Pecuniary loss does not include property damage, so damaged personal property (for example a phone) is generally not paid. The cost to replace items seized as evidence is the exception.
rule.quote: “Pecuniary loss” means any expenses actually and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death resulting from a crime, but does not include property damage.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params.extension: Agency may grant an extension or waive the deadline when the circumstances make it unreasonable; claims from child sexual assault or abuse may not be barred by a statute of limitations (§ 9009(12))
unless the program gives you more time

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the injury, unless the Agency grants an extension or finds the deadline unreasonable in the circumstances.
rule.quote: Where the claim has not been filed within 1 year after the personal injury on which the claim in based, unless an extension is granted by the Agency or the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances render this requirement unreasonable.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, but this is waived if it was reported to protective services or Family Court, the victim has a protection from abuse order, the victim cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in a sexual assault case, or the Agency finds the requirement unreasonable.
rule.quote: Where the victim has failed to report the crime to a law-enforcement agency within 72 hours of its occurrence. This requirement is waived in any of the following circumstances: a. The crime has been reported to an appropriate governmental agency, such as child or adult protective services or the Family Court. b. The victim can provide a protection from abuse order. c. The victim has cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in cases of crimes involving domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. d. Where the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances of the crime or the victim render this requirement unreasonable.
rule.source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

rule.summary: A Delaware domiciliary hurt by a crime in another state may apply if the crime would be compensable in Delaware and that state has no eligible program with equal benefits.
rule.quote: A person whose domicile is in Delaware and who is the victim or secondary victim of a crime that occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States may make an application for compensation if both of the following are true: a. The crimes would be compensable had they occurred in Delaware. b. added.summary: For a crime before October 1, 2019, the claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime. If you filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived.
added.quote: (a)1. A claim arising from a crime occurring before October 1, 2019, must be filed within 1 year after: a. The occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based. b. The death of the victim or intervenor. c. The death of the victim or intervenor is determined to be the result of a crime, and the crime occurred after June 30, 1994. 2. Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim under this paragraph occurred because of a delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under subsection (1) may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline.
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

added.summary: For an older crime, the department may also allow up to 2 years after the crime for other good cause.
added.quote: 3. For good cause based on reason other than a delay described in subparagraph 2., the department may extend the time for filing a claim under subparagraph 1. for a period not exceeding 2 years after such occurrence.
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

added.summary: If you were under 18 at the time of a crime before October 1, 2019, you have 1 year after turning 18 to file.
added.quote: (b) For a claim arising from a crime that occurred before October 1, 2019, when a victim or intervenor who was under the age of 18 at the time the crime occurred reaches the age of 18, the victim or intervenor has 1 year to file a claim
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

added.summary: If you were a minor when it happened and filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived. For other good cause, the department may add up to 1 more year for an older crime, or up to 2 more years for a newer one.
added.quote: Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim occurred because of delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under this subsection may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline. For good cause based on any other reason, the department may extend the time period allowed for filing a claim under paragraph (b) for an additional period not to exceed 1 year or under paragraph (c) for an additional period not to exceed 2 years.
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

added.summary: The program may deny, reduce, or take back an award if it finds you have not cooperated with the state attorney, law enforcement, and the program.

added.summary: The program must deny an award if it finds you would not face serious financial hardship without it. It looks at all of your financial resources.

In determining serious financial hardship, the department shall consider all the financial resources of the claimant.
added.source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)
