added.quote: Any portion of a public record which reveals the identity, including the name or personal identification number, home or employment telephone number, home or employment address, or personal assets, of a victim, or any other information that could be used to locate, intimidate, harass, or abuse the victim, which identifies that person as the victim of a crime, and which is a public record that is generated or received by any agency that regularly generates or receives information from or concerning the victims of crime is exempt from s. 119.07 (1) and s. 24(a), Art. added.quote: If the sexual assault occurred after May 12, 2008 you are not required to have a police report to apply for the CVCP. The program may use documentation from the forensic medical exam which shows that a sexual assault occurred.
added.pinpoint: CJCC Victims Compensation FAQ, police report question
added.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Itemized bills for the expenses being claimed must be submitted with the application.
added.quote: Benefits received are based on actual eligible expenses and itemized bills must be submitted with your application for review.
added.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Please Note
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

added.summary: Prescription claims need an itemized summary and an itemized bill from the prescribing doctor.
added.quote: Prescriptions must include an itemized summary and an itemized bill from the prescribing doctor.
added.pinpoint: CJCC What Our Programs Cover, Medical and Dental Expenses
added.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

added.summary: A medical release is not required, but sending one with the packet may speed up processing later.
added.quote: While not required, submitting a medical release with your completed application packet may expedite processing later, if needed.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

added.summary: After the first counseling visit, the program pays only once a complete Psychological Service Report, treatment plan, or counseling verification form is submitted.
added.quote: After the first visit, compensation will not be provided for counseling services without the submission of a complete Psychological Service Report ("PSR")/ treatment plan or counseling verification form.
added.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

added.summary: Lost wages claims need proof of at least 60 days of income before the crime.
added.quote: Proof of at least 60 days of income prior to the victimization.
added.pinpoint: Documentation Request: Lost Wages-Victim, Required Documents
added.source_title: Documentation Request: Lost Wages (Victim)

added.summary: Lost wages claims need proof of employment, which the employer sends on the program's form or on letterhead.
added.quote: Proof of employment. The employer may submit A) the enclosed Employment Verification Form along with their business card or B) a letter on business letterhead
added.pinpoint: Documentation Request: Lost Wages-Victim, Required Documents
added.source_title: Documentation Request: Lost Wages (Victim)

added.summary: If the survivor missed more than a week of work, a doctor's release showing the time out and the return date is needed.
added.quote: Proof of return to work. If you were out of work more than one (1) week, the doctor may submit the enclosed Work Release Form OR you need to submit a doctor’s release stating the length of time you were out of work and the date you were released to return back to work.
added.pinpoint: Documentation Request: Lost Wages-Victim, Required Documents
added.source_title: Documentation Request: Lost Wages (Victim)

added.summary: Sending a completed W-9 with the packet helps speed up payment once a claim is approved.
added.quote: Submitting a completed W-9 Form with your Complete Application Packet will assist with processing of your approved payments.
added.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Instructions item 3
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

added.summary: Funeral benefit claims must include a death certificate.
added.quote: A death certificate must be submitted with your application for funeral benefits.
added.pinpoint: GA application instructions (Revised Sept 2026), Benefits Covered footnote
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

added.summary: Once a claim is awarded, payment can take up to eight weeks to arrive from the GBI.
added.quote: Once a claim is awarded, please allow up to eight weeks for a payment to be mailed/sent from the Georgia Bureau of Investigation (GBI).
added.pinpoint: CJCC Victims Compensation FAQ, How Soon Will I Get My Reimbursement Check?
added.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Georgia's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, helps survivors of sexual assault and others whose safety may be at risk if their home address is made public.
added.quote: The Georgia Safe at Home Program is an address confidentiality program that helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, stalking, or other eligible individuals whose safety may be compromised by public disclosure of their residential address.
added.source_title: Georgia Secretary of State: Safe At Home

added.summary: When the compensation board requests records from police, prosecutors, courts, or other agencies to decide a claim, it must keep those records confidential.
added.quote: provided, however, that the board shall preserve the confidentiality of any such records received
added.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-4 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: A survivor cannot be made to pay, directly or indirectly, for a forensic medical exam; the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund pays, whether or not the survivor reports or cooperates with police.
rule.quote: A victim shall have the right to have a forensic medical examination regardless of whether the victim participates in the criminal justice system or cooperates with law enforcement in pursuing prosecution of the underlying crime. A victim shall not be required to pay, directly or indirectly, for the cost of a forensic medical examination. The cost of a forensic medical examination shall be paid for by the Georgia Crime Victims Emergency Fund, as provided for in Chapter 15 of this title.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-5-72 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

params.applies_to: exam costs above the $1,000 limit

rule.summary: The program says providers may not bill law enforcement or the patient's insurance for exam costs above the $1,000 limit.
rule.quote: If FME expenses are over $1,000.00, can we bill law enforcement or the patient’s insurance for the difference? No. The maximum allowable amount is $1,000.00 for the collection of evidence for a FME.
rule.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2002, the total award to a claimant cannot exceed $25,000.
rule.quote: with respect to any claim filed with the board as a result of a crime occurring on or after July 1, 2002, no award made under the provisions of this chapter payable to a claimant sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of a victim shall exceed $25,000.00 in the aggregate
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Medical expenses are capped at $15,000.
rule.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Counseling is capped at $3,000.
rule.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Lost wages are capped at $10,000.

rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $6,000.

rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Crime scene sanitization is capped at $1,500.
rule.quote: No award under this chapter for the following losses shall exceed the maximum amount authorized: Category Maximum Award Lost wages $ 10,000.00 Funeral expenses 6,000.00 Financial hardship or loss of support 10,000.00 Medical 15,000.00 Counseling 3,000.00 Crime scene sanitization 1,500.00
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Medical and dental bills, including prescriptions and copays, are covered up to $15,000.
rule.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Dental expenses are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.
rule.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Prescriptions and copays are covered within the $15,000 medical and dental limit.
rule.quote: Medical and Dental Expenses (including prescriptions and copays) Up to $15,000
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Mental health counseling is covered up to $3,000; itemized counseling bills must be submitted.
rule.quote: Mental Health Counseling Up to $3,000 Submit copies of any itemized counseling bills related to the victimization.
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: Crime scene sanitization by a trained company is covered up to $1,500.
rule.quote: Crime Scene Sanitization Up to $1,500 Submit an itemized bill from a company trained in crime scene and biohazard clean-up.
rule.source_title: CJCC: What Our Programs Cover

rule.summary: No award is made for loss of property, so items like a damaged or taken phone are not reimbursed.
rule.quote: No award of any kind shall be made under this chapter to a victim of a crime for loss of property.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-7 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: Compensation funds are not awarded to pay attorney's fees for a claimant who hires a lawyer for a Board hearing.
rule.quote: if a claimant chooses to be represented by an attorney, that claimant shall be responsible for the payment of their attorney's fees. Compensation funds shall not be awarded to pay attorney's fees.
rule.source_title: Criminal Justice Coordinating Council Administrative Rules (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. ch. 144)

params.extension: The board may extend the time for good cause shown.
or later if the board extends it for good cause

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the crime, and the board may extend that for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim shall be filed by a victim not later than three years after the occurrence of the crime upon which such claim is based or not later than three years after the death of the victim; provided, however, that if such victim was a minor at the time of the commission of the crime, he or she shall have until three years after his or her eighteenth birthday to file such claim; and provided, further, that upon good cause shown, the board may extend the time for filing a claim.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-5 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: A victim who was a minor at the time of the crime has until three years after their eighteenth birthday to file.
rule.quote: if such victim was a minor at the time of the commission of the crime, he or she shall have until three years after his or her eighteenth birthday to file such claim
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-5 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

rule.summary: By statute, no award is made if records show the crime was reported more than 72 hours after it happened, unless the board finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: In no case may an award be made where the police records, records of an investigating agency, or records created pursuant to a mandatory reporting requirement show that such report was made more than 72 hours after the occurrence of such crime unless the board, for good cause shown, finds the delay to have been justified
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

before.summary: An award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources such as workers' compensation; gifts from family or charitable donations do not count.

after.summary: By statute, an award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources, such as workers' compensation, but gifts from family members or charitable donations do not count.

rule.summary: By statute, an award may be reduced by payments received from the offender or from other private or public sources, such as workers' compensation, but gifts from family members or charitable donations do not count.
rule.quote: Any award made pursuant to this chapter may be reduced by or set off by the amount of any payments received or to be received as a result of the injury, serious mental or emotional trauma: (1) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; and (2) From any other private or public source, including an award of workers’ compensation pursuant to the laws of this state, provided that private sources shall not include contributions received from family members or persons or private organizations making charitable donations to a claimant.
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-8 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

before.summary: A sexual assault victim who is not the primary policyholder may opt out of giving insurance information by checking the opt-out box on the application.

after.summary: The application's instructions say that if you are a victim of sexual assault and are not the main policyholder, you may opt out of giving insurance information for this incident.

rule.summary: The application's instructions say that if you are a victim of sexual assault and are not the main policyholder, you may opt out of giving insurance information for this incident.
rule.quote: If you are not the primary policyholder and are a victim of sexual assault or family violence, you may opt out of providing insurance information for this incident by checking the opt-out box in Section 6 of the application.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Program Application and Instructions (English)

rule.summary: The program lists sexual offenses among its most common compensable crimes.
rule.quote: Most Common Compensable Crimes Child Molestation Cruelty to Children Child Abuse Human Trafficking Sexual Offenses
rule.source_title: CJCC: Victims Compensation program page

rule.summary: A covered crime includes an act in Georgia, or for a Georgia resident, an act in a state with no compensation program or a state that paid less than Georgia would.
rule.quote: An act which is committed in this state; in a state which does not have a victims’ compensation program, if the claimant is a resident of this state; or in a state which has compensated the claimant in an amount less than the claimant would be entitled to pursuant to this chapter, if the claimant is a resident of this state
rule.source_title: O.C.G.A. 17-15-2 (Justia, 2025 Georgia Code)

added.summary: Hawaii's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Law Enforcement, is free and lets survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, or stalking use a substitute address instead of their home, work, and school addresses with state and county agencies. It also forwards mail and accepts legal service for participants. Survivors apply through an application assistant at a certified victim services organization, not directly with the Department.
added.quote: The Hawaii Address Confidentiality Program is a free resource that helps to protect survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, and stalking. The program enables participants to use a substitute address in place of their residential, work, and school addresses with state and county government agencies.
added.pinpoint: Dept. of Law Enforcement, Hawaii ACP page, "What is Hawaii ACP?"; see HRS 801G-1, 801G-2, 801G-3
added.source_title: Department of Law Enforcement: Hawaii Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

params.applies_to: what police are to do

rule.summary: The Attorney General's sexual assault response program page says a primary police role is to make sure victims are offered and given free forensic exams, whether or not they report to police. This is a program role statement, not a statute, and it does not say who pays or whether insurance can be billed.
rule.quote: The primary roles of the police are to ensure that victims are offered and provided free forensic examinations regardless if a police report is made
rule.pinpoint: Dept. of the Attorney General, HSART Program page, "Who We Are and What We Do"

params.exception: or more when covered medical costs are over $10,000

rule.summary: The maximum award is $10,000; if compensable medical expenses exceed $10,000, the award can go up to $20,000 or the actual medical expenses, whichever is lower.
rule.quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter in an amount in excess of $10,000; provided that, if a case involves compensable medical expenses in excess of $10,000, no compensation shall be awarded in excess of $20,000 or the actual amount of compensable medical expenses, whichever is lower.
rule.source_title: HRS 351-62 Limitations upon award of compensation

or later only if you show good cause

rule.summary: The application must be filed within eighteen months after the date of injury; the commission may accept a later application for good cause.
rule.quote: No order for the payment of compensation shall be made under this chapter unless the application has been made within eighteen months after the date of injury, death, or property damage; provided that upon a showing of good cause, the commission may consider applications filed beyond this time period.
rule.source_title: HRS 351-62 Limitations upon award of compensation

params.exception: unless an arrest was made

rule.summary: No prosecution or conviction is needed, but an arrest must have been made or the crime must have been reported to police without undue delay.
rule.quote: An order may be made under this section whether or not any person is prosecuted for or convicted of a crime arising out of an act or omission described in subsection (a) if an arrest has been made or the act or omission has been reported to the police without undue delay.
rule.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

rule.source_title: HRS 351-31 Eligibility for compensation

before.summary: Anyone hurt by a covered crime within Hawaii's criminal jurisdiction can apply, and Hawaii residents hurt by a covered crime in another state can also apply.

after.summary: Under the statute, people hurt by a covered crime within Hawaii's criminal jurisdiction can apply. The statute also names Hawaii residents hurt by a covered crime in another state.

The requirement to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department under subsection 3 does not apply to this subsection.

added.source_title: Iowa Safe at Home (Iowa Secretary of State address confidentiality program home page)

added.summary: Records that Iowa's public records law already keeps confidential, and information taken from them, stay confidential when the program gets them.
added.quote: Information and records which are confidential under section 22.7 and information or records received from the confidential information or records remain confidential under this section.
added.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: After the exam program pays, the provider may not send the survivor a bill for any leftover balance.
rule.quote: A medical provider must not submit any remaining balance to the sexual abuse victim after the sexual abuse examination program has determined payment.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: Glasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetics, wheelchairs, and medication taken, lost, or destroyed in the crime can be replaced.
rule.quote: Compensation may be paid for the replacement of a medical device including but not limited to a sight or hearing device, dentures, a prosthetic device, a wheelchair, and medication that was taken, lost or destroyed during the crime.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: Lost wages are figured from gross pay for scheduled hours missed, then reduced by 25 percent.
rule.quote: Lost wages are computed as the gross rate of pay multiplied by the number of scheduled hours of work missed, decreased by 25 percent
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

rule.summary: To count as emergency relocation, the move must happen within 30 days of the crime, its discovery, or when it could reasonably be reported, or within 30 days before or after the offender's release from incarceration.
rule.quote: "Emergency relocation" means a relocation that takes place within thirty days of the date of a crime or the discovery of a crime, or within thirty days after a crime could reasonably be reported. "Emergency relocation" also includes a relocation that takes place within the thirty days before or after an offender related to the crime is released from incarceration.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.scope: clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement

rule.summary: Clothing and bedding held as evidence by police can be paid for.
rule.quote: Compensation may be paid for clothing and bedding held as evidence by law enforcement.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

before.summary: Lost or damaged property (for example a phone or other belongings) is not paid, nor are legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.

after.summary: The program does not pay for property loss or repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for property loss or repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rule.quote: The program cannot pay for property loss, property repair, legal fees, phone bills, meals, or pain and suffering.
rule.pinpoint: Iowa AG, Crime Victim Compensation Facts page
rule.source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

before.summary: Pregnancy care for the victim is covered, but care for a newborn child is not.

after.summary: The program does not pay for the care of a newborn child.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for the care of a newborn child.
rule.quote: Expenses incurred for the care of a newborn child are not compensable.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

params.extension: Two years may run from discovery of the crime; the department may waive the limit for good cause (61 IAC 9.28(2) lists age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, and health or safety reasons).
or later if the crime was discovered later or you show good cause

rule.summary: Apply within two years of the crime or its discovery. The program can waive the deadline for good cause.
rule.quote: file the application with the department within two years after the date of the crime, the discovery of the crime, or the date of death of the victim. The department may waive the time limitation if good cause is shown.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

params.exception: or within 72 hours of when you reasonably could, and the program may waive this for good cause

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police or the sheriff within 72 hours, or within 72 hours of when a report could reasonably be made. The program may waive this for good cause.
rule.quote: A person is not eligible for compensation unless the crime was reported to the local police department or county sheriff department within seventy-two hours of its occurrence. If the crime cannot reasonably be reported within that time period, the crime shall have been reported within seventy-two hours of the time a report can reasonably be made. The department may waive this requirement if good cause is shown.
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

rule.summary: For sexual abuse, the 72-hour police report rule may be waived for good cause if a forensic exam was done within 72 hours or the survivor told a medical provider, mental health professional, or victim service provider.
rule.quote: For a victim of sexual abuse, the 72-hour reporting requirement may be waived for good cause if a sexual abuse evidentiary examination was completed within 72 hours of the crime or if the crime was disclosed to another provider including but not limited to a licensed medical provider, a licensed mental health professional, or a designated victim service provider.
rule.source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

before.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further (see the next residency rule).

after.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if the act would be covered had it happened in Iowa and that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further.

rule.summary: Under the statute, an Iowa resident hurt in another state can apply to Iowa if the act would be covered had it happened in Iowa and that state has no eligible compensation program. The program's administrative rules go further.
rule.quote: To a victim of an act committed outside this state who is a resident of this state, if the act would be compensable had it occurred within this state and the act occurred in a state that does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program
rule.source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

added.summary: If the program gets a bill for your exam but no signed application from you, it holds the bill for 30 days and contacts you. If no signed application comes within 60 days, the bill is destroyed.
added.quote: If the Program received a medical bill for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination but does not receive a signed application from the victim, CVCP will hold the medical bill(s) for 30 days. The program will contact the victim to request completion of the application. The medical bills will be destroyed if no signed application is received within 60 days.
added.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Medical bills received by CVCP, but no application received
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

added.summary: Email the completed and signed application to cvcp.admin@iic.idaho.gov.
added.quote:
Completed and signed applications can be sent via:
Email to: cvcp.admin@iic.idaho.gov
added.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

added.summary: Fax the completed and signed application to 208-332-7559.
added.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

added.summary: Mail the completed and signed application to Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, P.O. Box 83720, Boise, ID 83720-0041.
added.quote:
Mail to: IDAHO CRIME VICTIMS COMPENSATION PROGRAM
P.O. BOX 83720
BOISE, ID 83720-0041
added.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

added.summary: The application must be completed and signed before it is sent.
added.quote: Completed and signed applications can be sent via:
added.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 4, submission box
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

added.summary: If you sign as the victim's legal guardian or conservator, include a copy of the court order.
added.quote:
IF LEGAL GUARDIAN and /or
CONSERVATOR
added.pinpoint: Application for Compensation, page 2, Claimant Information
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP Application for Compensation (June 2026)

added.summary: To be paid back for co-pays, deductibles, or prescriptions you paid yourself, contact your case manager; receipts are required.
added.quote: If you have paid co-pays, deductibles, prescriptions, then please reach out to your Case Manager. Receipts are required.
added.pinpoint: Complete an Application page, Out of Pocket Expenses
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Complete an Application

added.summary: For exam and medical costs, the program asks the medical providers for itemized bills.
added.quote: The Program will request the following from medical providers who assisted the victim: UB04, CMS1500, or itemized billing statements with CPT and REV codes.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

added.summary: The program asks the medical provider for the sexual assault nurse examination records.
added.quote: Sexual Assault Nurse Examination Records
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

added.summary: If the victim has federal or state insurance, the program asks the provider for the Explanation of Benefits.
added.quote: Explanation of Benefits if the victim has federal/state insurance.
added.pinpoint: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, provider documentation list
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

added.summary: For counseling, the program works with your mental health provider to collect bills, the initial intake, and a treatment plan.
added.quote: CVCP will work with your mental health providers directly to gather the required CVCP documentation (bills, Initial Intake, CVCP Mental Health Treatment Plan, etc.).
added.pinpoint: Complete an Application page, Mental Health
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Complete an Application

added.summary: Before paying, the program may ask the claimant for documents such as a W-9 form.
added.quote: For the purpose of dispersing payment, the claimant may be required to provide certain documentation, including a W-9 form.
added.source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

added.summary: After the program receives the application, its review can take 60 to 90 days.
added.quote: The next step of the process involves a thorough review of your application, which can take 60-90 days.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, What happens after my application is received?
added.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Idaho's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes a substitute mailing address and mail forwarding so their new address stays confidential; state and local agencies must accept the substitute address.
added.quote: If you move to a new location to escape domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, malicious harassment or human trafficking, the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) helps keep your new address confidential using a mail-forwarding service and substitute address.
added.pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, introduction; Idaho Code 19-5701 and 19-5703
added.source_title: Idaho Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
added.quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
added.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

rule.summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
rule.quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

rule.summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
rule.quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

before.summary: An adult survivor's (18 or older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical exam; the program pays instead. Federal programs such as Medicaid, Medicare, or VA are billed first, and a minor's exam goes through all insurance first. This is a rule about insurance billing; no Idaho source flatly bars billing the survivor.

params.payer: Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, instead of an adult's private insurance

after.summary: The program says an adult's (18 or older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical exam.

rule.summary: The program says an adult's (18 or older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical exam.
rule.quote: an adult victim's (18 years of age and older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination.
rule.pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

params.payer: Industrial Commission; a provider it has paid may not collect more from the victim for the same services, except as subsection (3) allows

rule.summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
rule.quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

rule.summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
rule.quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
rule.quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
rule.quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
rule.quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
rule.quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
rule.quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params.scope: necessary travel to get benefits the program covers

rule.summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
rule.quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Covered exam costs include examiner, facility, and lab fees, STI antibiotics, HIV prophylaxis, and other medications; follow-up visits may also be covered.
rule.quote: Sexual assault forensic and medical examination costs covered by the program include but are not limited to examiner fees, facility fees, laboratory fees, antibiotics for Sexually Transmitted Infections, HIV prophylaxis, medical prescriptions, and other medications. Follow up visits as prescribed by the treating physician due to an assault may also be covered.
rule.pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP?
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
rule.quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

rule.summary: The program will not pay counseling cancellation or missed-appointment fees, or sessions that included the offender.
rule.quote: CVCP will not reimburse for cancellation or missed appointment fees nor will they consider payments for sessions that included the offender.
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

rule.summary: Mileage is not paid for the first 15 miles of a round trip, or for round trips of 15 miles or less; one round trip per day.
rule.quote: Reimbursement is limited to one (1) round trip per day. The claimant shall not be reimbursed for the first fifteen (15) miles of any round trip, nor for traveling any round trip of fifteen (15) miles or less.
rule.source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

before.summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover, so this page is not fully reliable.

after.summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover.

rule.summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover.
rule.quote: A victim may request the criminal court to order the offender to pay restitution for expenses that are not covered by the program, such as property damage, wage loss, expenses to attend criminal court, or costs for crime-scene cleanup.
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params.extension: the commission may extend the time for good cause shown
or later if the commission extends it for good cause

rule.summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

params.exception: or later if the commission finds good cause for the delay

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

params.scope: exam costs only, adult victims

before.summary: An adult who does not want to report to police can use a separate exam reimbursement application that covers mainly the exam cost; it is not for minors and does not open the program's other benefits.

params.scope: exam costs only, adult victims

after.summary: An adult who does not want to report to police can use a separate application. It is meant for people who mainly want only the cost of the sexual assault forensic and medical exam paid. It is not for minors.

rule.summary: An adult who does not want to report to police can use a separate application. It is meant for people who mainly want only the cost of the sexual assault forensic and medical exam paid. It is not for minors.
rule.quote: This application should be used by victims who did not or do not wish to disclose to law enforcement at this time and are primarily seeking reimbursement for only the cost of sexual assault forensic and medical examination This form is not applicable for minor victims.
rule.pinpoint: Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application, page 1
rule.source_title: Idaho CVCP Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application (April 2026)

before.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with law enforcement and prosecutors; the commission may deny or reduce an award if they do not.

after.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in catching and prosecuting the offender.

rule.summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in catching and prosecuting the offender.
rule.quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
rule.quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
rule.quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
rule.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
rule.quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

rule.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
rule.quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

rule.summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.
rule.quote: means actual bodily harm or disfigurement and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy, venereal disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Crimes committed in Idaho qualify. An Idaho resident hurt in another state qualifies only if that state has no compensation program the victim is eligible for.
rule.quote: Occurs or is attempted in this state or occurs outside the state of Idaho against a resident of the state of Idaho and which occurred in a state which does not have a crime victims compensation program for which the victim is eligible
rule.source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling expenses, send copies of itemized bills, and submit those bills to insurance or other payment sources too.
added.quote:
Please submit copies of itemized bills. All bills must be submitted to other sources of recovery available to
the victim.
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: Keep receipts, bills, and other proof of payment for every expense you want reimbursed.
added.quote: Keep receipts, bills, and any other proof of payment for all items you are seeking to receive compensation for.
added.pinpoint: Compensation guide (Rev. 11/24), What proof of my expenses should I keep?
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

added.summary: If you are the legal guardian of a minor or incapacitated adult victim, include documentation showing guardianship.
added.quote: If the answer is YES, please provide documentation to show guardianship.
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: When eligibility depends on where you live, you may be asked for proof of residence such as a lease, utility bill, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
added.quote:
A person may be required to provide verification or proof of residence including, but not limited to,
a lease agreement, utility bill, license registration, document showing the mailing address, pay stub, tax form, or notarized statement.
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Program guide (Rev. 11/24)

added.summary: If the crime involved a law enforcement officer's use of force and you filed a complaint, lawsuit, or got a settlement, provide documentation of it.
added.quote: If yes, please explain and provide documentation for all complaints, proceedings or settlements
added.pinpoint: Application (Rev. 12/2024), Section 2, Use of Force Claims
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation Application (English, Rev. 12/2024)

added.summary: The Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, and stalking a substitute address to use with State and local government agencies instead of their home, school, or work address.
added.quote: The Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) provides a substitute address for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, and stalking to use instead of their home, school, or work addresses when interacting with State and local government agencies.
added.pinpoint: Illinois AG ACP page, opening paragraph; statutory basis 750 ILCS 61/11 and 61/15
added.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Illinois Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Under the Freedom of Information Act, the Attorney General's office does not have to release the records it gets to process a compensation application, such as the application, documents, and photographs.
added.quote: Any records obtained by the Attorney General's office to process the application, including but not limited to applications, documents, and photographs, shall be exempt from disclosure by the Attorney General's office under the Freedom of Information Act.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

before.summary: A hospital or provider giving a sexual assault medical forensic exam, outpatient treatment, transport, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of it, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, or denied claims. The survivor's insurance can still be billed, and inpatient services are an exception.

after.summary: A hospital or other provider giving a sexual assault survivor a medical forensic exam, medical care and treatment, transportation, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of those costs, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, or denied claims.

rule.summary: A hospital or other provider giving a sexual assault survivor a medical forensic exam, medical care and treatment, transportation, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of those costs, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, or denied claims.
rule.quote: shall not: (1) charge or submit a bill for any portion of the costs of the services, transportation, or medications to the sexual assault survivor, including any insurance deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim by an insurer, spenddown, or any other out-of-pocket expense
rule.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: If the survivor has health insurance or a coverage program, the provider bills that insurer or program, and the survivor's out-of-pocket share goes to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program instead of the survivor.
rule.quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall bill the insurance company or program. With respect to such insured patients, applicable deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim, or any other out-of-pocket insurance-related expense may be submitted to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program of the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rule.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: When the survivor has no Medicaid or insurance, or has opted out of billing private insurance, the provider sends the bill to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program.
rule.quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall submit the request for reimbursement to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rule.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: A survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder on the insurance (for example, someone on a parent's or partner's plan) may opt out of billing that private insurance; the exam bill then goes to the state program.
rule.quote: a sexual assault survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder of the sexual assault survivor's insurance policy may opt out of billing the sexual assault survivor's private insurance provider
rule.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: Follow-up care, lab work, and prescriptions after the exam are billed to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program when the survivor presents the sexual assault services voucher the hospital issues.
rule.quote: If a sexual assault survivor presents a sexual assault services voucher for follow-up healthcare, the healthcare professional, pediatric health care facility, or laboratory that provides follow-up healthcare or the pharmacy that dispenses prescribed medications to a sexual assault survivor shall submit the request for reimbursement for follow-up healthcare, pediatric health care facility, laboratory, or pharmacy services to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
rule.source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: trips to and from medical and counseling treatment

rule.summary: Travel to and from medical and counseling appointments is covered.
rule.quote: transportation expenses to and from medical and counseling treatment facilities
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: locks, doors, or windows needed or damaged because of the crime

rule.summary: Locks, doors, or windows that are needed or were damaged because of the crime are covered.
rule.quote: locks, doors, or windows necessary or damaged as a result of the crime
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: replacing clothing and bedding used as evidence

rule.summary: Replacing clothing and bedding kept as evidence is covered.
rule.quote: replacement costs for clothing and bedding used as evidence
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params.scope: lost tuition, if the crime leaves the victim unable to keep attending school

rule.summary: Lost tuition is covered when the victim was enrolled in school or college and cannot keep attending because of the crime.
rule.quote: loss of tuition paid to attend grammar school or high school when the victim had been enrolled as a student prior to the injury, or college or graduate school when the victim had been enrolled as a day or night student prior to the injury when the victim becomes unable to continue attendance at school as a result of the crime of violence
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says stolen, damaged, or lost property cannot be paid, except locks, doors, and windows.
rule.quote: Stolen, damaged or lost property (except locks, doors and windows)
rule.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses cannot be paid
rule.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

rule.summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ says counseling by an unlicensed person working under a licensed provider cannot be paid.
rule.quote: Services by an unlicensed person working with a licensed person cannot be paid.
rule.pinpoint: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims, What types of expenses may the Crime Victims Compensation Program pay?
rule.source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

params.extension: or within one year after a criminal charge
or within 1 year after someone is charged with the crime

rule.summary: Apply within 5 years of the crime, or within one year after someone is criminally charged for it.
rule.quote: Within 5 years of the occurrence of the crime, or within one year after a criminal charge of a person for an offense, upon which the claim is based, the applicant presents an application
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

before.summary: A victim who was under 18 or under a legal disability can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability ends, and a posttraumatic stress disorder diagnosis counts as a legal disability.

after.summary: A victim who was under 18, or under a legal disability, when it happened can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability is removed. The Act counts a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder as a legal disability.

rule.summary: A victim who was under 18, or under a legal disability, when it happened can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability is removed. The Act counts a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder as a legal disability.
rule.quote: he or she may present the application required by this subsection within 3 years after he or she attains the age of 18 years or the disability is removed, as the case may be. Legal disability includes a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

before.summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances. A medical visit, evidence collection, a protective order, or a mental health provider evaluation can stand in for the police report.

after.summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances.

rule.summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances.
rule.quote: For victims of offenses defined in Sections 10-9, 11-1.20, 11-1.30, 11-1.40, 11-1.50, 11-1.60, 12-13, and 12-14 of the Criminal Code of 1961 or the Criminal Code of 2012, the appropriate law enforcement officials were notified within 7 days of the perpetration of the crime allegedly causing death or injury to the victim or, if the notification was made more than 7 days after the perpetration of the crime, the applicant establishes that the notice was timely under the circumstances.
rule.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

before.summary: Instead of a police report, going to a medical facility for care or sexual assault evidence collection, getting an order of protection or no contact order, or getting an evaluation from a mental health provider counts as notice.

after.summary: Instead of a police report, going to a medical facility for care or sexual assault evidence collection, getting an order of protection or no contact order, or getting an independent medical evaluation from a mental health provider counts as notice.

rule.summary: Instead of a police report, going to a medical facility for care or sexual assault evidence collection, getting an order of protection or no contact order, or getting an independent medical evaluation from a mental health provider counts as notice.
rule.quote: If, in lieu of a law enforcement report, the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, has presented to a mental health provider for an independent medical evaluation, or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking or law enforcement use of force, such action shall constitute appropriate notification under this Section.
rule.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-1) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

rule.summary: A survivor who uses a medical facility visit as notice does not have to name the offender to the medical provider.
rule.quote: except that the victim shall not be required to identify the offender to the medical provider
rule.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-2) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

before.summary: The same steps (a protective order, a medical or evidence collection visit, or a mental health evaluation) also count as cooperating with law enforcement.

after.summary: The same steps also count as cooperating with law enforcement. One is getting an order of protection or a no contact order. Another is going to a medical facility for care or evidence collection. Another is getting an independent exam from a mental health provider.

rule.summary: The same steps also count as cooperating with law enforcement. One is getting an order of protection or a no contact order. Another is going to a medical facility for care or evidence collection. Another is getting an independent exam from a mental health provider.
rule.quote: If the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, obtained an independent medical examination from a mental health provider as described in subsection (b-4), has taken any of the actions described in subsection (b-3), or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking, such action shall constitute cooperation under this subsection (c).
rule.pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(c) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

added.summary: The program pays the costs this law lists only if they are reasonable, documented, and incurred within 180 days after the crime, unless the director extends that period.
added.quote: (d) Subject to subsections (b) and (c), the division may order the payment of compensation under this chapter for any of the following reasonable, documented expenses incurred within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of the violent crime:
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

added.summary: A victim of a child sex crime can apply until turning 31, or later in some cases.
added.quote: (e) An alleged victim of a child sex crime may submit an application to the division until the victim becomes thirty-one (31) years of age or in accordance with subsection (f).
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-16 (applications for assistance) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

added.summary: For some child sex crimes, a victim can also apply within 5 years after the earliest of these: the state first finds DNA evidence or a recording that is enough to charge the offender, or someone confesses.
added.quote: (f) An alleged victim of a child sex crime described in IC 35-41-4-2 (e) which meets the requirements of IC 35-41-4-2 (p) may submit an application to the division not later than five (5) years after the earliest of the date on which: (1) the state first discovers evidence sufficient to charge the offender with the offense through DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) analysis; (2) the state first becomes aware of the existence of a recording (as defined in IC 35-31.5-2-273 ) that provides evidence sufficient to charge the offender with the offense; or (3) a person confesses to the offense.
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-16 (applications for assistance) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

added.summary: Mail the paper application to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
added.quote: If applying online isn't an option, PDF applications can be mailed or hand delivered to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute at: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
added.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: The paper application can also be hand delivered to the same office in the Indiana Government Center South.
added.quote: If applying online isn't an option, PDF applications can be mailed or hand delivered to the Indiana Criminal Justice Institute at: Indiana Government Center South, 402 W. Washington Street, Room W469, Indianapolis, IN 46204.
added.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: The paper application can be faxed to 317-232-7103.
added.quote: They can also be faxed to: 317-232-7103.
added.pinpoint: Apply for Violent Crime Compensation, File a PDF claim
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: The claims analyst gathers the police report and supplemental reports during the review; you do not have to send it with the application.
added.quote: (1) A police report including all supplemental reports and victim and witness statements made to law enforcement personnel.
added.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

added.summary: Expenses are paid only when an itemized bill verifies them, so keep itemized bills for every crime-related cost.
added.quote: Expenses that cannot be verified via an itemized bill.
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: Out-of-pocket costs are reimbursed only with proof of payment, so keep receipts.
added.quote: Out of pocket expenses without proof of payment.
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: For lost wages or child care, the program collects documentation of employment, earnings, or substitute child care costs.
added.quote: (4) Documentation regarding substitute child care expenses, employment, or earnings information.
added.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

added.summary: Because the program pays last, it collects records of insurance and other benefits that covered any of the costs.
added.quote: (5) Documentation concerning the following: (A) Medical or life insurance benefits, or both. (B) Social Security, pension, or retirement benefit information. (C) Worker's compensation or unemployment compensation benefits.
added.source_title: 203 IAC 1 (Victim Services Division administrative procedure), Indiana Administrative Code

added.summary: Dependents claiming loss of support must verify their dependent status and the support the victim provided.
added.quote: (Note: This requires verification of legal dependent status, marriage and support, or paternity and support).
added.source_title: ICJI Victim Compensation Division (program page)

added.summary: If the claimant is under 18, a parent or legal guardian signs and dates the application.

added.source_title: Application for Benefits from Violent Crimes Compensation Fund, State Form 23776 (R14 / 9-21)

added.summary: Once an award is computed, it must be paid within 30 days; the FAQ says claims are typically processed within a few months.
added.quote: an award must be paid not more than thirty (30) days after the date on which the award is computed
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-43 (computation and payment of awards) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

added.summary: Indiana's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General's Office, is free and lets survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes keep a confidential address: first-class mail goes to a secure substitute address and is forwarded, and the substitute address is used for state and local government services.
added.quote: The ACP is a free program that allows victims of domestic violence, sexual assault stalking, human trafficking, harassment, intimidation, or invasion of privacy to maintain a confidential address through the Attorney General's Office.
added.pinpoint: Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program page, opening paragraphs
added.source_title: Indiana Attorney General, Address Confidentiality Program

added.summary: Indiana law makes a compensation claimant's personal information and medical records confidential, along with records from the division's claim investigation that are not publicly available.
added.quote: The following are confidential: (1) A claimant's: (A) personal information (as defined in IC 9-14-6-6 ); and (B) medical records. (2) Records obtained during an investigation under section 26 of this chapter that are not publicly available.
added.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-11.5 (confidentiality) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rule.summary: Necessary medical, hospital, dental, optometric, chiropractic and ambulance services, prescription drugs, and prosthetic devices are covered if incurred within 180 days of the crime.
rule.quote: the division may order the payment of compensation under this chapter for any of the following reasonable, documented expenses incurred within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of the violent crime: (1) Necessary: (A) medical, chiropractic, hospital, dental, optometric, and ambulance services; (B) prescription drugs; and (C) prosthetic devices;
rule.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rule.summary: The director may extend the 180-day expense window up to 2 years after the crime when the victim asks and medical records support it.
rule.quote: The director may extend the one hundred eighty (180) day compensation period established by subsection (d) for a period not to exceed two (2) years after the date of the violent crime if: (1) the victim or the victim's representative requests the extension; and (2) medical records and other documentation provided by the attending medical providers indicate that an extension is appropriate.
rule.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

rule.summary: Lost income is covered if the victim was employed at the time of the crime.
rule.quote: (2) Loss of income: (A) the victim would have earned had the victim not died or been injured, if the victim was employed at the time of the violent crime;
rule.source_title: IC 5-2-6.1-21.1 (compensable losses) via Justia, 2025 Indiana Code

params.scope: emergency shelter to stay away from the offender, up to 30 days
