added.summary: Except as section 81-1813 provides, the program cannot award more than $25,000 for each applicant per incident.
added.quote: Except as provided in section 81-1813 , no compensation shall be awarded under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act from the Victim's Compensation Fund in an amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars for each applicant per incident.
added.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1823

added.summary: If you were under 19 when it happened, you can apply on or before your twenty-second birthday.
added.quote: For a victim who was under nineteen years of age at the time of the personal injury, on or before the victim's twenty-second birthday
added.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

added.summary: The committee may still look at a late application if it finds good cause for the delay.
added.quote: The committee may evaluate applications submitted beyond the deadline established in this section if the committee finds that good cause existed for missing such deadline.
added.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

added.summary: The program's FAQ says you must cooperate with criminal justice officials in the investigation and prosecution of the crime.
added.quote: You must cooperate with criminal justice officials in the investigation of the crime and the prosecution of the offender.
added.pinpoint: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (4-5-2023), What must I do to be eligible?
added.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

added.summary: Mail the completed, signed application and documentation to the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program, PO Box 94946, Lincoln, NE 68509-4946.
added.quote: Return the completed/signed application and documentation to the below address: Nebraska Crime Victim’s Reparations Program PO Box 94946 Lincoln, NE 68509-4946
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Email the claim application and the supporting documentation requested to ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov.
added.quote: Submit, along with supporting documentation requested, by email or mailing to: CVR Claim → ncc.cvr@nebraska.gov
added.pinpoint: Crime Victim Reparations program page, Apply
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

added.summary: The application's return-to block also lists the program's fax number, 402.471.2837.
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Include itemized copies of all medical bills related to the incident.
added.quote: Submit itemized copies of all medical bills relating to the incident.
added.pinpoint: FAQ, What must I do to apply for compensation?
added.source_title: CVR Frequently Asked Questions (updated 4-5-2023)

added.summary: Attach copies of crime-related bills and any receipts for bills you already paid.
added.quote: Attach copies of crime related bills and any paid receipts.
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Sign and date the Authorization to Release Information; no action is taken on the claim until it is signed.
added.quote: This authorization is an integral part of your application and must be signed and dated by the victim or claimant before any action will be taken on your claim.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Authorization to Release Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: Complete the citizenship attestation; if you attest as a qualified alien, you agree to provide a copy of your USCIS documentation.
added.quote: I am a qualified alien under the federal Immigration and Nationality Act and I agree to provide a copy of my USCIS documentation.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), United States Citizenship Attestation
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay periods of work missed because of the incident.
added.quote: Copy of pay stubs or an earning statement for the pay period(s) for missed work as a result of the incident.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages when self-employed, include your most recent federal tax returns with Schedule C and copies of estimates, bids, or contracts.
added.quote: If Self-Employed: submit the most recent federal tax returns including the schedule C form, Copies of Estimates, Bids, and/or Contracts.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For lost wages, include a doctor's release back to work.
added.quote: A Doctor’s release back to work.
added.pinpoint: CVR Claim Application (Oct 2023), Section 6: Loss of Wage Information
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: For funeral or burial expenses, a copy of the death certificate is needed.
added.quote: Funeral or Burial Expenses (A copy of the death certificate will need to be provided.)
added.source_title: CVR Claim Application (October 2023)

added.summary: By statute, a hearing officer rules on an application within 180 days after receiving all required information; the clock does not start until the file is complete.
added.quote: A hearing officer shall consider and rule upon any application made under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act within one hundred eighty days after receipt of all required information related to the crime.
added.pinpoint: Claims Process, quoting Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1809(1)
added.source_title: CVR Claims Process

added.summary: The program says claims are typically fully processed within 6 to 9 months.
added.quote: CVR program applications take time, typically claims are fully processed within 6-9 months.
added.source_title: Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Program pamphlet (English)

added.summary: Nebraska's Address Confidentiality Program is for victims of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fear for their safety, among other conditions.
added.quote: To be eligible for ACP, an individual must be (1) a victim of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fears for his or her safety
added.source_title: Nebraska Secretary of State: Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: By statute, the name of a sexual assault victim in the reparations committee's records when applying for compensation may not be made public. The statute protects the name; it does not say the whole claim file is confidential.
added.quote: The name of any victim of a sexual assault appearing in information or records of the Crime Victim's Reparations Committee when the victim is applying for compensation under the Nebraska Crime Victim's Reparations Act shall not be made public.
added.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1842 (sexual assault victim; records; confidential)

rule.summary: Lost or damaged property is not covered.
rule.quote: The program does not cover property crime, property loss, property damage or pain and suffering.
rule.pinpoint: NCC Crime Victim Reparations page, Limitations
rule.source_title: Nebraska Crime Commission: Crime Victim Reparations program page

params.extension: The committee may accept a late application for good cause (81-1821(3)). A victim under nineteen at the time of injury may apply on or before their twenty-second birthday (81-1821(2)(c)).

params.condition: if you were 19 or older when it happened

rule.summary: A victim who was 19 or older at the time of the injury must apply within 2 years of the injury.
rule.quote: For a victim who was nineteen years of age or older at the time of the personal injury or death, within two years after the date of the personal injury or death
rule.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

params.exception: or, if you could not reasonably report that soon, within 5 days of when you could

rule.summary: Generally the crime must be reported to police within 5 days, or within 5 days of when a report could reasonably be made.
rule.quote: The personal injury or death was the result of an incident or offense which had been reported to the police within five days of its occurrence or, if the incident or offense could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within five days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made.
rule.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

rule.summary: For sexual assault, the 5-day police report rule does not apply if, before applying, the crime was reported to police at any time, a protection order was obtained, or the victim had a forensic medical exam.
rule.quote: An application submitted by or for a victim of sexual assault, domestic assault, child abuse, or sex trafficking is not subject to the five-day reporting requirement in subsection (1) of this section if, prior to submitting the application the: (a) Applicant or victim has reported such crime to the police; (b) Applicant or victim has obtained a protection order related to such incident or offense; or (c) Victim has presented for a forensic medical exam.
rule.source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1821

added.summary: A claim is denied if the victim did not cooperate in a meaningful way with law enforcement, unless there was good cause, such as fear of retaliation.
added.quote: The primary victim failed to cooperate materially with law enforcement agencies without good cause such as fear of retaliation by or on behalf of the offender
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
added.quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
added.quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
added.pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
added.quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
added.quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
added.quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
added.quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
added.quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
added.quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
added.quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
added.quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
added.quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
added.quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
added.source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

added.summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.
added.quote: Once the program receives your application, you will be contacted by mail or email within 2 weeks.
added.pinpoint: Program page FAQ, How Long Will It Take?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
added.quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.summary: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking can apply to New Hampshire's Address Confidentiality Program if they meet its eligibility guidelines.
added.quote: Any adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor or guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person, may apply to the program if they are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking and meet the eligibility guidelines.
added.pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

added.summary: You do not need a restraining order, pending criminal charges, or a police report to take part in the program.
added.quote: Having a restraining order, criminal charges pending or even reporting the abuse to law enforcement are not required in order to participate in the ACP.
added.pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
added.source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

added.summary: Everything the compensation program receives or keeps about a claim is confidential and may not be released to anyone unless the claimant authorizes it or another law allows it.
added.quote: All information received, obtained, or maintained by the program in connection with any claim for victims' compensation shall be maintained as confidential material, and shall not be released or disclosed to any person or entity whatsoever, except as authorized by the claimant or as otherwise provided by law.
added.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

before.summary: A physician or hospital that examines a survivor to gather evidence must provide the exam without charge to the survivor. Private insurance is billed only if the survivor chooses to use it.

after.summary: A physician or hospital that examines a survivor of an alleged sexual offense to gather evidence must provide the exam without charge to the survivor.

rule.summary: A physician or hospital that examines a survivor of an alleged sexual offense to gather evidence must provide the exam without charge to the survivor.
rule.quote: If a physician or a hospital provides any physical examination of a victim of an alleged sexual offense to gather information and evidence of the alleged crime, these services shall be provided without charge to the individual.
rule.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

rule.summary: The bill for a sexual assault medical exam may not be sent or given to the survivor or the survivor's family.
rule.quote: The bill for the medical examination of a sexual assault victim shall not be sent or given to the victim or the family of the victim.
rule.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

before.summary: If a survivor with insurance chooses to bill it, the provider bills the insurer, and neither the survivor nor the department may be billed for anything above the coverage limit. Survivors on Medicaid or Medicare whose kit is not anonymous are billed to Medicaid or Medicare under a separate rule.

after.summary: If a survivor with insurance chooses to bill it, the provider bills the insurer, and neither the survivor nor the department may be billed for anything above the coverage limit. A separate rule says that for survivors on Medicaid or Medicare whose kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare.

rule.summary: If a survivor with insurance chooses to bill it, the provider bills the insurer, and neither the survivor nor the department may be billed for anything above the coverage limit. A separate rule says that for survivors on Medicaid or Medicare whose kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare.
rule.quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault has insurance, and chooses to bill their healthcare insurance, the health provider shall seek payment from the patient's healthcare insurer. Neither the patient nor the department shall be billed for anything above the coverage limit
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: A person examined by a physician or hospital after a felonious sexual assault, for treatment or to gather evidence, may not be charged for services related to the assault or other crime-related injuries. Payments are at the fee for service Medicaid rate.
rule.quote: a person who claims to be a victim of a felonious sexual assault who is examined by a physician or hospital for the purpose of treatment, gathering information or evidence shall not be charged for such services or examination that relate to the sexual assault and any other crime-related injuries
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: If the survivor is covered by Medicaid or Medicare and the kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare directly. This is an exception to billing insurance only by choice.
rule.quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault is covered by Medicaid or Medicare and the reporting kit is not anonymous, the health provider shall seek payment directly from Medicaid or Medicare.
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: Counseling is covered up to $4,000 or 40 visits, whichever comes first.
rule.quote: The commission shall award compensation up to $4,000 in total expenses, or 40 visits, whichever comes first
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: Lost wages are covered at up to 75% of pre-crime wages for up to 3 months, counting any workers' compensation or disability benefits.
rule.quote: The total compensation paid for lost wages shall not exceed 75% of the claimant's pre-crime wages, not to exceed 3 months, including any workers' compensation or disability benefits received.
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

before.quote: If the claimant does not have a restraining order against the abuser, the claimant shall present a letter from a victim's advocate setting forth the basis for not obtaining a protective order, which may include, among other reasons, safety concerns for the claimant
before.summary: Relocation can be paid when the offender poses a continuing threat; without a restraining order, a letter from a victim's advocate explaining why can stand in.

after.quote: The offender poses a continuing credible threat to the safety of the claimant; (2) There is either: a. A police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order have been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser or a final restraining order has been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser; or b. If the claimant does not have a restraining order against the abuser, the claimant shall present a letter from a victim’s advocate setting forth the basis for not obtaining a protective order, which may include, among other reasons, safety concerns for the claimant
after.summary: Relocation is paid only if the offender is a continuing, credible threat to your safety. You also need a police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order. A final restraining order also counts. If you have no restraining order, a letter from a victim's advocate explaining why can count instead.

rule.summary: Relocation is paid only if the offender is a continuing, credible threat to your safety. You also need a police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order. A final restraining order also counts. If you have no restraining order, a letter from a victim's advocate explaining why can count instead.
rule.quote: The offender poses a continuing credible threat to the safety of the claimant; (2) There is either: a. A police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order have been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser or a final restraining order has been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser; or b. If the claimant does not have a restraining order against the abuser, the claimant shall present a letter from a victim’s advocate setting forth the basis for not obtaining a protective order, which may include, among other reasons, safety concerns for the claimant
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: Mileage to medical appointments is paid at the Medicaid rate for trips over 10 miles round trip, capped at 100 miles round trip.
rule.quote: Mileage to and from appointments with licensed health care providers, at the rate used by Medicaid to compensate mileage. Mileage shall be paid for trips over 10 miles round trip and is capped at 100 miles round trip
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: Shelter for the survivor and family is one of the goods a crisis center can pay for from emergency funds, which the commission then reimburses to the crisis center.
rule.quote: The cost of shelter for the victim and the victim's family
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: Hospital care is not paid if the victim had health insurance and the hospital has not denied free or reduced-fee care.
rule.quote: The commission shall not award compensation for hospital care if: a. The victim had health insurance at the time of treatment for injuries sustained as a direct result of the crime; and b. Free or reduced fee care has not been denied by the hospital
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params.extension: good cause; no deadline for a victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking who was a minor at the time
You can apply later with good cause, and some sexual abuse survivors have no deadline.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years of the crime unless good cause is shown. A survivor of sexual abuse that happened when they were a minor may file at any time.
rule.quote: The claimant, guardian ad litem or child advocate, or parent may file a claim for compensation within 2 years of the crime, unless good cause is shown. A claimant who was the victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking under subparagraph I(a)(3), or a guardian ad litem, child advocate, or parent on behalf of such claimant, may file a claim at any time.
rule.source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

rule.summary: A claim is denied if the crime was not reported within 5 days, unless good cause is shown, such as a medical condition, fear for safety, fear of retribution, or the survivor's emotional state or mental health.
rule.quote: The crime was not reported within 5 days of the crime unless good cause, which shall include but not be limited to the following, is shown
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

rule.summary: A crisis center can give a domestic violence or sexual assault victim 10-day emergency funds (food, clothing, shelter, transportation, locks, medications), and the commission reimburses the crisis center, not the victim. The crisis center must send a police report or a restraining order with its request.
rule.quote: the commission shall award compensation to a crisis center for payment of 10-day emergency funds by the crisis center to a victim of domestic violence or sexual assault
rule.source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

added.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

added.summary: The program will not pay if the victim did not cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement. A compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating is the exception.
added.quote: No compensation shall be awarded if: a. Compensation to the victim proves to be substantial unjust enrichment to the offender or if the victim did not cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement authorities unless the victim demonstrates a compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating

of the incident report. If you don't have one, the

Include

added.summary: For lost wages, supply pay stubs from before the crime and from your return to work.

If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.

added.summary: For lost wages, supply a doctor's letter stating the period of disability.

If available, please supply your pay stubs from the week before the crime, the week you returned to work
and a letter from your doctor stating your period of disability.

added.summary: Self-employed applicants claiming lost wages must supply income and business tax returns for the 2 years before the crime.
added.quote: If you are self-employed, you must supply copies of your income tax returns and business tax returns for the last 2 years before the crime.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Section 8 (Lost Wages/Support Information)

added.summary: The HIPAA release in the application must be completed, signed and dated before the claim can be processed.

This authorization is necessary to obtain information
from your health care providers under federal law.
It must be completed, signed and dated in order
for the VCCO to process your claim.

added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: The VCCO decides on an application within 90 days after it acknowledges receiving the completed application and all supporting information; this can be extended for good cause.
added.quote:
The Office will make its determination regarding the application within 90 days of acknowledgment by the
Office of receipt of the completed application and any and all necessary supplemental information
added.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

added.summary: The application instructions say claims take 3 months to process once all documentation is received.
added.quote:
the turn around time for processing a claim is 3 months of receipt of
all documentation.
added.pinpoint: NJ VCCO Claim Application and Instructions (oag.rev.8.25.20), Instructions page II
added.source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

added.summary: New Jersey's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families, is meant to keep the addresses of victims of domestic violence, stalking and sexual assault confidential. The law lets public agencies accept a program participant's substitute mailing address.
added.quote: to enable interagency cooperation with the Director of the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families in providing address confidentiality for victims of domestic violence, stalking, and sexual assault, and reproductive health service patients and providers, and to enable public agencies to accept a program participant's use of an address designated by the director as a substitute mailing address.
added.source_title: N.J.S.A. 47:4-2 Address confidentiality for certain individuals (Justia 2025)

added.summary: VCCO claim files are confidential and are not government records open under the Open Public Records Act; nobody may inspect a victim's or claimant's file unless the law or a court order allows it.
added.quote: The files maintained by the Office that relate directly to the handling of any claim for compensation filed by a victim or claimant are not government records subject to disclosure under the Open Public Records Act and shall be considered confidential.
added.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rule.summary: As part of crime scene clean-up, the Office may pay the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing.
rule.quote: The Office may award compensation for the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing;
rule.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params.extension: good cause for delayed filing
or later if the program finds good cause for the delay

rule.summary: Apply within 5 years of the injury, or later if the Office finds good cause for the delay.
rule.quote: unless the application has been made within five years after the date of the personal injury or death or after that date upon determination by the office that good cause exists for the delayed filing

rule.summary: If the victim was under 18, the 5-year clock starts on their 18th birthday.
rule.quote: If the victim is under 18 years of age, the five-year limit on filing shall commence on the day the victim turns 18 years old.

params.exception: counted from the crime or from when it was reasonably discovered

rule.summary: The crime must have been reported to police or another law enforcement agency within 9 months of when it happened or was reasonably discovered.

params.exception: or later for good cause

rule.summary: The Office can excuse a late police report for good cause.
rule.quote: The Office reserves the right to, upon determination that good cause exists for the delayed filing, make an exception to the requirement that the incident be reported to the police within the stated time period.
rule.source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

rule.summary: There is no minimum loss requirement for crimes on or after June 26, 1995.

added.summary: You can file online through the CVRC application portal, where you sign in or create an account and submit the application.

added.pinpoint: CVRC online application portal, home page
added.source_title: CVRC online compensation application portal (home page)

added.summary: A paper application goes to the Crime Victims Reparation Commission office in Albuquerque; the rules count it as filed on the postmark date.
added.quote: Crime Victims Reparation Commission 6200 Uptown Blvd., Suite 210 Albuquerque, NM 87110
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?
added.source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

added.summary: A paper application can be faxed to the commission's office.
added.pinpoint: Compensation Application page, How do I apply?

added.summary: The application asks for a copy of the police report if one is available.

added.summary: The commission reviews the application with a complete offense report or a provider incident verification form, which its office requests.

added.summary: Expenses must be documented with invoices, receipts or canceled checks that show who was paid, who paid, the amount, the date and the service.

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer must give a statement of the work dates missed, hourly wage and average weekly hours.

added.summary: New Mexico's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, lets survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, attempted sexual assault or stalking use the Secretary of State's address as a substitute address with state and local agencies, with mail forwarded to their real address. params.scope: collecting the evidence kit

rule.summary: A health care provider may not charge the survivor, directly or indirectly, for the costs of collecting a sexual assault examination kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.

rule.summary: Under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, the state administrator must provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes, arrange free exams, or reimburse victims for the exam cost.

rule.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

rule.summary: If the victim is reimbursed for the exam instead of getting it free, reimbursement covers the full cost with no deductible or limit, and the victim can apply for reimbursement for one year from the exam date.
rule.quote: the reimbursement covers the full cost of the forensic medical exam, without any deductible requirement or limit on the amount of the reimbursement; (2) the victim of a sexual crime is entitled to apply for reimbursement for a period of one year from the date of the forensic medical exam
rule.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

params.exception: or up to $30,000 more if an injury leaves you fully disabled for life

rule.summary: The maximum award is $20,000 per victim. The commission may add up to $30,000 more for extraordinary losses when the injury is catastrophic and causes permanent total disability.
rule.quote: No award of reparation shall be in excess of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per victim, except that the commission may award up to an additional thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for extraordinary pecuniary losses, if the personal injury to a victim is catastrophic and results in a permanent total disability.

rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

params.scope: gas for trips over 30 miles one way from home, at 20 cents a mile

rule.source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

rule.quote: An application for reparation shall be made within two years after the injury or death, except for minors who are victims of criminal activity under the provisions of Section 30-6-1 NMSA 1978, regarding abandonment or abuse of a child, Section 30-9-11 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual penetration, or Section 30-9-13 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual contact of a minor.

rule.summary: Criminal sexual penetration and criminal sexual contact of a minor are covered crimes.

rule.source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-8 (Crimes enumerated)

added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 10, Medical Care
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: If the victim has Workers' Compensation or disability insurance coverage, OVS needs that provider's decision letter.
added.quote: If the victim has coverage through either Worker's Compensation or a Disability Insurance provider, OVS will need the decision letter from either Worker's Compensation or the Disability Insurance provider to help determine eligibility for compensation.
added.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 16, Workers Compensation/Disability
added.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

added.summary: The Department of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives eligible victims, including victims of a sexual offense, a designated substitute address to use instead of their real address, with free mail forwarding.
added.quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "address confidentiality program" to protect victims of domestic violence, victims of human trafficking, victims of kidnapping, victims of a sexual offense, victims of stalking, and reproductive health care services providers, employees, volunteers, patients, or immediate family members of reproductive health care services providers by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and their minor children.
added.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 108 (Address confidentiality program)

added.summary: OVS records and proceedings on a victim's or claimant's compensation claim are confidential and are not shared with government or private entities, except for listed purposes such as criminal justice requests, judicial subpoenas, the claimant's own requests, and program administration.
added.quote: Records maintained by the office and proceedings by the office based thereon regarding a claim submitted by a victim or a claimant shall be deemed confidential and shall not be shared with any government or private entity, with the following exceptions:
added.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 633 (Confidentiality of records)

rule.summary: The provider must accept the OVS exam fee as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the forensic exam services.
rule.quote: The hospital, sexual assault examiner program, or licensed health care provider must accept this fee as payment in full for these specified services. No additional billing of the survivor for said services is permissible.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Private insurance can be used for the exam only if the survivor chooses to assign it, and then the survivor owes no deductible, coinsurance, or balance bill.
rule.quote: A sexual assault survivor may voluntarily assign any private insurance benefits to which they are entitled for the healthcare forensic examination, in which case the hospital or healthcare provider may not charge the office; provided, however, in the event the sexual assault survivor assigns any private health insurance benefit, such coverage shall not be subject to annual deductibles or coinsurance or balance billing by the hospital, sexual assault examiner program or licensed health care provider.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: A provider that accepts OVS payment for the exam takes it as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the difference between its charges and what OVS paid.
rule.quote: The billing provider may not bill victims/survivors or their guardians for the difference between charged amounts and the amount reimbursed by OVS.
rule.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III.c Reimbursement Rates
rule.source_title: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program Provider Billing Manual (March 2026, Version 2.0)

params.payer: OVS pays only for exam-related services; unrelated care goes to insurance first, then a compensation claim

before.summary: OVS direct payment covers only services and medicines related to the forensic exam. Unrelated care in the same visit is not paid under the exam claim; it goes to the survivor's insurance first, then can be submitted to OVS as a regular compensation claim.

params.payer: OVS pays only for exam-related services and medicines under the exam claim

after.summary: OVS direct payment covers only services and medicines related to the forensic exam.

rule.summary: OVS direct payment covers only services and medicines related to the forensic exam.
rule.quote: Only services and pharmaceuticals that are related to the forensic rape exam may be reimbursed under an FRE claim.
rule.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III Reimbursement
rule.source_title: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program Provider Billing Manual (March 2026, Version 2.0)

rule.summary: Unreimbursed medical care and other necessary services caused by the injury count as out-of-pocket loss.
rule.quote: Out-of-pocket loss shall mean unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses or indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical care or other services necessary as a result of the injury upon which such claim is based
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

params.scope: trips to necessary medical care caused by the crime

rule.summary: Reasonable travel to crime-related medical care is covered, with receipts for fares or the federal mileage rate for driving yourself.
rule.quote: medical expenses shall also include the reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary, causally related medical care which may include, but are not limited to, reasonable airplane, cab, bus or train fare, with receipts, or if a claimant has provided his or her own transportation, the federally recognized mileage reimbursement rate at the time the expense was incurred
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.3 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.scope: trips to court for the prosecution

rule.summary: Reasonable transportation to necessary court appearances in the prosecution is covered.
rule.quote: an award shall include reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary court appearances in connection with the prosecution of such crimes upon which the claim is based.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.scope: new or better security devices, if a doctor, counselor, or the district attorney says your health is in imminent danger without them

rule.summary: New or enhanced security devices can be covered when a physician, counselor, or the district attorney states the claimant's health is in imminent danger without the device.
rule.quote: In order for the costs associated with new or enhanced security devices, beyond those which, pursuant to the Executive Law are repaired or replaced under subdivision 2 of section 631, or are awarded under subdivision 12 of section 631 , to be compensable, the office shall require a statement from the claimant's physician or counselor, or the district attorney handling the victim's case, indicating that without the aid of such a device the claimant's health is in imminent danger.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.scope: moving when it is necessary for your health or safety

rule.summary: Relocation costs are covered when moving is necessary for the victim's health or safety.
rule.quote: "Relocation expenses" shall mean the cost of relocating a crime victim, when relocation is necessary for the health or safety of the victim.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

rule.summary: Lost earnings or support are paid at no more than $600 per week.
rule.quote: no such award shall exceed six hundred dollars for each week of lost earnings or support.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $2,500.
rule.quote: reasonable relocation expenses not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Employment-related transportation (extra cost of getting to work because of crime injuries) is capped at $2,500. Medical and court travel are not under this cap.
rule.quote: reasonable employment-related transportation expenses, not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Crime scene cleanup and securing a crime scene (for example repairing doors, windows, and locks) are capped at $2,500.
rule.quote: the costs of crime scene cleanup and securing of a crime scene not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Essential property related to the victim's ability to communicate is paid at the receipted amount, up to $1,500 per item.
rule.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's ability to communicate shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rule.summary: Essential property related to safely operating the victim's own means of transportation is paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,500 per item.
rule.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's safe operation of their personal means of transportation shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rule.summary: Medically necessary life-sustaining equipment lost or damaged in the crime has its own cap of $10,000 instead of the general essential property cap.
rule.quote: In the case of medically necessary life-sustaining equipment which was lost or damaged as the direct result of a crime, the award shall be limited to the amount of ten thousand dollars.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params.item: outerwear, suits and footwear
outerwear, suits and footwear

rule.summary: Outerwear, suits, and footwear are paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 per item.
rule.quote: Items of outerwear, suits and footwear shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars per item.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear
clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear

rule.summary: Other clothing is paid at the receipted amount, up to $100 per item.
rule.quote: All other items of clothing shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-hundred dollars per item.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: mattress and platform or box spring
mattress and platform or box spring

rule.summary: A mattress and platform or box spring are paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,000.
rule.quote: Mattress and platform or box spring shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand dollars.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params.item: bedding other than mattress and box spring
bedding other than mattress and box spring

rule.summary: Other bedding is paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 in total.
rule.quote: All other items of bedding shall be the receipted amount, in a cumulative amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rule.summary: For security devices, only the device and installation are covered; monitoring and maintenance fees are not.
rule.quote: Compensable costs shall be limited to the devices themselves and their installation, and shall not include the periodic service charges for monitoring or maintaining any such devices.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

rule.summary: Meals during travel for medical care are not reimbursed as transportation.
rule.quote: Meals shall not be considered a related transportation expense.
rule.source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.3 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params.extension: Runs from the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend for good cause, and must extend if the claimant got no notice of the program and did not know they were eligible.
or of when the crime was discovered, or later if OVS finds good cause

rule.summary: File within 3 years of the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend this for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence or discovery of the crime upon which such claim is based, three years after a court finds a lawsuit to be frivolous, or not later than three years after the death of the victim, provided, however, that upon good cause shown, the office may extend the time for filing.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 625 (Filing of claims)

before.summary: A police report is not required: the crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime (such as a forensic exam facility or protective services agency) can show this instead of police records. No fixed reporting window appears in the statute.

after.summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.

rule.summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.
rule.quote: the records of a support agency for survivors of crime or the records of a criminal justice agency show that such crime was reported.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: A medical facility that provides forensic exams for rape and sexual assault counts as a support agency, so its records can stand in for a police report.
rule.quote: any medical facility established under the laws of the state that provides a forensic physical examination for victims of rape and sexual assault
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, mandated insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, and any emergency award.
rule.quote: Any award made pursuant to this article shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) under insurance programs mandated by law, (c) from public funds, (d) under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary, (e) as an emergency award pursuant to section six hundred thirty of this article.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

before.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam is an exception (see the exam rules).

after.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.

rule.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.
rule.quote: OVS is the payer of last resort and can only consider your out-of-pocket loss. OVS can only process payments for crime-related expenses. You must bill your insurance company or benefits plan before OVS can pay.
rule.source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

rule.summary: OVS considers whether the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury and can reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rule.quote: the office shall determine whether, because of such victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of such victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

rule.summary: Acts committed in New York count as crimes for compensation whether or not anyone was arrested, charged, or prosecuted, and whether or not the claimant dealt with police.
rule.quote: an act committed in New York state which would, if committed by a mentally competent criminally responsible adult, who has no legal exemption or defense, constitute a crime as defined in and proscribed by law, regardless of whether any suspect was arrested, charged, apprehended or prosecuted for the commission of the act or whether the claimant has interacted with a criminal justice agency investigating such act
rule.source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

added.summary: If an adult patient does not report to police and asks to stay fully anonymous, the provider can send the exam's payment form as Jane or John Doe.
added.quote: If the adult patient chooses not to report to law enforcement and asks that their identity be kept completely confidential, a reimbursement form submitted on behalf of “Jane/John Doe” is an acceptable submission.
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

added.summary: The instructions say evidence should sometimes be collected more than 96 hours after the assault, for example when the patient was unconscious. The provider must explain why, and that does not guarantee the SAFE Program will pay.
added.quote: There are cases in which evidence should be collected beyond 96 hours. Examples include where the patient was unconscious or sedentary or where an exam may corroborate chronic injury or excessive force related to the sexual assault. Documentation must clearly justify the reasoning for the forensic collection as it relates to the sexual assault. Documentation does not guarantee payment by the SAFE Program.
added.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 9 (Date/Time of Abuse/Assault)
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

added.summary: Even after these deadlines, the Attorney General may still make an award at any time for good cause.
added.quote: (d) Notwithstanding divisions (A)(2)(a), (b), and (c) of this section, the attorney general is permitted to make an award of reparations at any time for good cause shown.
added.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

added.summary: The Attorney General's billing instructions say Ohio law has health care providers report a sexual assault to police even when the patient does not want to talk to police. If an adult patient stays unnamed, the provider gives police the date, time, and general location of the assault, but not the patient's name or other identifying details.
added.quote: Law enforcement reporting – Ohio Revised Code (ORC) 2921.22 (A) & (B) (see page 7) requires health care providers report a sexual assault to law enforcement whether a patient chooses to speak with law enforcement or not. If the adult patient chooses to remain unnamed, the provider is mandated to provide the date, time, and general location the assault took place, but not the patient’s name or other identifiers.
added.pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 12 (Law enforcement reporting)
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

added.summary: Register on the Attorney General's Crime Victim's Compensation Portal and file the claim application online.
added.quote: Register and file a claim application online.
added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: Print the paper application, fill it out, and mail it to the Attorney General's Crime Victim Services Section in Columbus.
added.quote: Download and print an application , fill it out and mail it to Crime Victim Services Section 30 E. Broad Street, 26th Floor Columbus, OH 43215
added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: The completed paper application can be faxed to either of the Attorney General's fax numbers.
added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: New applications can be emailed, but only as a PDF or Word attachment; photos or screenshots of the pages are rejected.
added.quote: New applications can also be emailed to CrimeVictimsCompensationApplications@OhioAGO.gov but they must be attached as a PDF or Word document . No photos or screenshots of the pages will be accepted.
added.pinpoint: AG Apply for Victims Compensation, Two options for filing a claim
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Apply for Victims Compensation page

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, include copies of the 6 paychecks from before the crime.
added.quote: Complete if filing for loss of earnings. Provide copies of 6 paychecks prior to crime.
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: Send a front and back copy of each insurance or benefit plan card listed on the application.
added.quote: Please send front and back copy of card
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 6: Insurance and Benefit Information
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: The release in the application must be signed and dated, or the application will not be processed.
added.quote: This release must be signed and dated for the application to be processed.
added.pinpoint: Application, Section 12: Subrogation, Authorization, and Signature
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: For funeral expense claims, include a copy of the death certificate if you have one.
added.quote: If you have a copy of the death certificate, please include a copy with your application.
added.source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

added.summary: The Attorney General must issue a written decision within 120 days after receiving the application, but may extend that limit with written reasons.
added.quote: The attorney general shall make a written finding of fact and decision in accordance with sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code within one hundred twenty days after receiving the claim application.
added.source_title: ORC 2743.59 (investigating claim; decision deadline)

added.summary: Ohio's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, gives a substitute address to use on government records. To apply, you must fear for your safety, or a household member's, because one of you is a victim of rape, sexual battery, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking. You apply with a certified Application Assistant at a survivor services organization.
added.quote: The applicant fears for the safety of the applicant, a member of the applicant's household, or the minor, incompetent, or ward on whose behalf the application is made because the applicant, household member, minor, incompetent, or ward is a victim of domestic violence, menacing by stalking, human trafficking, trafficking in persons, rape, or sexual battery.
added.source_title: ORC 111.42 (address confidentiality program; application to secretary of state)

added.summary: Records the Attorney General or Court of Claims gets for a compensation claim (such as medical or counseling records) that were confidential or exempt from public records law in the hands of whoever created them stay confidential once the program has them. This does not make the whole claim file confidential, and the records can still be used in hearings and written decisions on the claim.
added.quote: any record or report that the court of claims or the  attorney general has obtained prior to, or obtains on or after,  June 30, 1998, under the provisions of sections 2743.51 to 2743.72 of the Revised Code and that is confidential or otherwise exempt  from public disclosure under section 149.43 of the Revised Code  while in the possession of the creator of the record or report  shall remain confidential or exempt from public disclosure under  section 149.43 of the Revised Code while in the possession of the  court of claims or the attorney general.
added.source_title: ORC 2743.62 (privilege; confidentiality of records obtained for reparations claims)

before.summary: Hospitals may not bill a sexual assault survivor, or the survivor's insurance, for the medical exam and test done to gather evidence. This covers the evidence exam itself, not every service at the same visit; emergency contraception, late adult exams, and treatment of other injuries are handled in the other SAFE exam rules.

params.scope: the exam and tests done to gather evidence
params.condition: if the crime was in Ohio

after.summary: Hospitals may not bill a survivor of a sex crime under Ohio law, or the survivor's insurance, for the medical exam and tests done to gather evidence. The rule covers only that evidence exam, not other care at the same visit.

rule.summary: Hospitals may not bill a survivor of a sex crime under Ohio law, or the survivor's insurance, for the medical exam and tests done to gather evidence. The rule covers only that evidence exam, not other care at the same visit.
rule.quote: No costs incurred by a hospital or emergency facility in conducting a medical examination and test of any victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution of a person shall be billed or charged directly or indirectly to the victim or the victim's insurer.

after.summary: Payment for the forensic exam does not depend on the survivor cooperating with police.

rule.summary: Payment for the forensic exam does not depend on the survivor cooperating with police.

params.payer: Patient, when an adult's last incident was more than 96 hours before the exam

before.summary: Attorney's fees to get a protective, restraining, or custody order that physically separates the victim from the offender are covered up to $1,000, at no more than $100 an hour.

after.summary: Attorney's fees for successfully getting a restraining order, custody order, or other order that physically separates the victim from the offender are covered up to $1,000, at no more than $100 an hour.

rule.summary: Attorney's fees for successfully getting a restraining order, custody order, or other order that physically separates the victim from the offender are covered up to $1,000, at no more than $100 an hour.

params.scope: replacing dentures, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and mobility aids

rule.source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

rule.quote: If the claimant was under twenty-one years of age at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, the claim is not barred under division (A)(2)(a) of this section until after the claimant's twenty-fourth birthday.
rule.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

before.summary: The crime must have been reported to police at some point. Ohio no longer has a reporting deadline, and the statute lists no alternative to a police report for sexual assault.

after.summary: The crime must have been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency at some point. Without a report, no award can be made.

rule.summary: The crime must have been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency at some point. Without a report, no award can be made.
rule.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall not make or order an award of reparations to a claimant if the criminally injurious conduct upon which the claimant bases a claim never was reported to a law enforcement officer or agency.
rule.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rule.summary: The award is reduced by anything recovered from other sources, such as insurance, so the program pays after those sources.
rule.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations that is otherwise payable to a claimant to the extent that the economic loss upon which the claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources.
rule.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rule.summary: An award can be reduced or denied for contributory misconduct, which the statute defines narrowly as unlawful or intentionally tortious conduct at the time of the crime that caused or threatened serious harm and provoked the crime.
rule.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations to the extent it is determined to be reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or the victim.
rule.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

rule.summary: An award can be denied or reduced if the victim or claimant did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
rule.quote: The attorney general or the court of claims, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny a claim or reconsider and reduce an award of reparations.
rule.source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

added.quote: Medical, dental, and prescriptions

added.summary: Fax the printed and signed claim form to 405/264-5097.

added.summary: Fill out every section of the paper form and sign all three signature areas on page four.

added.summary: List the injuries from the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.
added.quote: List the injuries suffered as a result of the crime and attach all itemized medical statements.

added.summary: Send all the bills you have received with the application; bills that arrive later can be added.

added.pinpoint: FAQ, Do I need to submit all bills with the application?

added.summary: Out-of-pocket medical, dental, and counseling costs are reimbursed at 100% only with documentation of payment.
added.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.

added.summary: The DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator requests the police report while documenting the claim.
added.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Lost income must be verified by both your employer and your attending physician.
added.quote: Work loss must be verified by the employer and the attending physician.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Income Loss / Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For lost wages, a physician or mental health professional and your employer must verify the disability time.
added.quote: provided the crime prevented the person from working and the disability can be verified by a physician or mental health professional and by the victim’s employer.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Instructions, Section G
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: If you are self-employed, tax returns for the last 3 years are required for lost wages.
added.quote: IF SELF-EMPLOYED, TAX RETURNS FOR THE LAST THREE YEARS WILL BE REQUIRED.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Section G heading
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For mileage to medical or counseling appointments, include documentation from the provider verifying the dates of service.

added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: To ask for future costs, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect and an explanation.
added.quote: To submit a request for future economic loss, include an itemized list of the expenses you expect to incur, along with an explanation regarding the expense.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For future dental work or surgery, ask the attending physician for a written estimate of the work and the cost.
added.quote: For future dental work or surgery necessary to repair damage from the criminal incident, ask the attending physician to write an accurate estimate which clearly states the work to be performed and the cost.
added.pinpoint: Official Claim Form (Revised June 2019), Types of Expenses Covered, Future Economic Loss
added.source_title: OCVC Official Claim Form (2019)

added.summary: For traditional American Indian healing or burial services, receipts must note each item's purpose.
added.quote: In order for reimbursement of these expenses, receipts must be provided with the item’s purpose clearly noted on the receipt.
added.pinpoint: Eligible Expenses, Traditional American Indian Services
added.source_title: OCVC Fund Eligibility page

added.summary: If you paid the forensic exam bill yourself, the program needs your Social Security number to reimburse you.
added.quote: If the victim/guardian paid the bill out of their own pocket, we will need a Social Security number in order to reimburse them.
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Processing can take anywhere from 4 to 12 months depending on where the crime occurred.
added.quote: Depending on the area in which the crime occurred, the processing time could vary anywhere from 4-12 months
added.pinpoint: FAQ, How Long is the Process?
added.source_title: OCVC Frequently Asked Questions

added.summary: Once the Victim-Witness Coordinator sends all documentation, claims are generally docketed for decision within 30 days.
added.quote: Claims are generally placed on a docket for decision within 30 days of receipt of all documentation from the Victim-Witness Coordinator.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Payments are generally made within 3 weeks of approval.
added.quote: PAYMENTS are generally made within three weeks of approval.
added.source_title: DAC Victims Compensation Program page (application process)

added.summary: Sexual Assault Examination Fund payments are usually made within 30 days of receiving the application.
added.quote: Payment is usually made within 30 days of the receipt of the application by the Compensation Program.
added.source_title: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

added.summary: Oklahoma's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, gives victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction who have moved somewhere unknown to their abuser a substitute address to use with state and local agencies, plus free mail forwarding. Applicants apply in person through a designated victim assistance program with an ACP-trained application assistant.
added.quote: The ACP aids in protecting the physical address of victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, and child abduction from disclosure. ACP contributes to the safety of victims by denying abusers the opportunity to use public records to violate the rights of others. Victims who have moved to a new location unknown to their abuser are provided with a substitute address when interacting with state and local agencies.
added.source_title: Oklahoma Attorney General Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) page

added.summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board to process a claim are confidential and generally cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case, with narrow exceptions for an appeal of a Board decision or a strict showing to a court.
added.quote: All records and information given to the Board to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim shall be confidential.
added.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.9 Limits of compensation, provider payment, debt collection

before.summary: Oklahoma law lists a free forensic medical examination among the rights of a sexual assault victim.

after.summary: Oklahoma's written notice of rights for sexual assault victims lists the right to a free forensic medical examination. In this law, sexual assault means rape, rape by instrumentation, or forcible sodomy.

rule.summary: Oklahoma's written notice of rights for sexual assault victims lists the right to a free forensic medical examination. In this law, sexual assault means rape, rape by instrumentation, or forcible sodomy.
rule.quote: The right to a free forensic medical examination
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142A-3 Notice of rights to victims of sexual assault

rule.summary: The exam fund pays whether or not the survivor has health insurance, and the survivor does not have to give insurance or employment information or file with a private insurer.
rule.quote: The payment of a sexual assault examination will be made, regardless of whether the victim is medically insured. (b) In order to provide anonymity to the sexual assault victim and maintain confidentiality, any victim who has obtained a forensic sexual assault examination, will not be required to provide information to the Board relative to employment or insurance; and, shall not be required to file a claim with any private insurance company for the payment of a forensic sexual assault examination.
rule.source_title: Okla. Admin. Code 185:15-1-6 Insurance (Sexual Assault Examination Fund)

before.summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Board pays for the sexual assault forensic exam and related medications out of the Sexual Assault Examination Fund.

after.summary: Once the victim applies, the Crime Victims Compensation Board can pay for the forensic exam and the medicine the health care professional orders. The money comes from the Sexual Assault Examination Fund.

rule.summary: Once the victim applies, the Crime Victims Compensation Board can pay for the forensic exam and the medicine the health care professional orders. The money comes from the Sexual Assault Examination Fund.
rule.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board is authorized to pay for this examination and the medications directed by the qualified licensed health care professional upon application submitted by the victim of a sexual assault.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

params.scope: medicine ordered at the forensic exam, paid by the exam fund

rule.summary: The exam fund pays at most $100 for medications related to the sexual assault that the health care professional directs.
rule.quote: One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) for medications which are related to the sexual assault and directed and deemed necessary by the health care professional
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.20 Sexual Assault Examination Fund

params.exception: or up to $25,000 more, but only for lost pay or lost support

rule.summary: Total compensation for one victim is capped at $25,000. After that, the Board may add up to $25,000 more only for the victim's lost wages or a dependent's loss of support.
rule.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00) in the aggregate. The Board may, after approval of an initial award of Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), grant an additional sum not to exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), specifically for loss of wages for the victim or loss of support for dependents of a deceased victim, provided there is verifiable economic loss after deducting payments from other sources.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

params.item: inpatient mental health treatment
inpatient mental health treatment
params.scope: inpatient mental health treatment

rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

caregiver lost income
