rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

rule.summary: The Board may pay for the victim's lost income from work (work loss).
rule.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board may compensate for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

before.summary: Outpatient counseling is covered when it focuses on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health provider.

after.summary: The Board may consider outpatient counseling costs when the counseling focuses on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.

rule.summary: The Board may consider outpatient counseling costs when the counseling focuses on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.
rule.quote: Outpatient counseling expenses for a victim of criminally injurious conduct may be considered by the Board provided the counseling is focused on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

params.scope: mileage to the victim's medical, dental, and counseling appointments

rule.summary: The program lists mileage to the victim's medical, dental, and counseling appointments as a covered expense.
rule.quote: Mileage reimbursement for medical, dental, and counseling appointments for the victim
rule.source_title: Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation home page

params.extension: The Board may extend the filing period for good cause or in all cases of sexual assault; for adult sexual assault it may count from the date the evidence kit was tested.

before.summary: A claim must be filed within 30 months after the injury. The sexual assault and good-cause extensions are in the next rule.

after.summary: A claim must be filed within 30 months after the injury or death it is based on.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 30 months after the injury or death it is based on.
rule.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the Crime Victims Compensation Board within thirty (30) months after the injury or death upon which the claim is based.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 72 hours, but a sexual assault survivor can instead meet this by having a forensic medical exam within 120 hours, and the Board can excuse either for good cause.
rule.quote: such conduct was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence, b. in the case of sexual assault, the victim undergoes a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after its occurrence, or c. the Board finds there was good cause for the failure to report the crime or obtain a forensic medical examination within the time specified in subparagraph a or b of this paragraph.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

before.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours is treated as having fully cooperated with law enforcement. This is the cooperation rule; the report rule itself is OK-RPT-1.

after.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours after the assault is found to have fully cooperated.

rule.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours after the assault is found to have fully cooperated.
rule.quote: Victims of sexual assault who undergo a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after the sexual assault shall be found to have fully cooperated.
rule.source_title: 21 O.S. 142.10 Award of compensation, criteria, reduction

You can apply electronically through the Crime Victims’ Compensation Portal at

added.pinpoint: CVC FAQ, loss of earnings benefit
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

added.summary: If you missed more than 2 weeks of work, a work release from your doctor is required.

added.source_title: Oregon Crime Victims' Compensation Application (English, 2026)

added.summary: Payment requests must be itemized billing statements listing the services, the provider's name, and the date of service.

added.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: Insurance EOBs, chart notes, and bills can be combined into one upload in the CVC Portal.

added.pinpoint: Applying for CVC, Crime Victims Portal FAQs, How do I upload documents?

added.summary: If CVC pays for a car rental or bus, train, or air fare instead of mileage, it needs a valid receipt.

added.summary: CVC confirms receipt by mail or email and issues a claim number within 2 business days.

We will notify you by mail or email when we receive your application. You will receive a

We will contact you again in 60 to 90 days to tell you if we have accepted your

added.summary: Oregon DOJ's Address Confidentiality Program is a free mail forwarding service that gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and bias crimes a substitute address to use instead of their real one.
added.quote: It helps survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, bias crimes or bias incidents shield their physical address. Health care providers who provide physical and behavioral reproductive and gender-affirming health care also can participate in ACP. Program participants are provided with a substitute address to use instead of their real address.
added.pinpoint: Oregon DOJ ACP page, 'Protecting Addresses for Victims'; program established by ORS 192.822
added.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Information an applicant gives the DOJ is open to the public by default, but the department may keep it confidential when the crime is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, trafficking, or domestic violence and the victim's interests require it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
added.quote:
All information submitted to the Department of Justice by an applicant and
all hearings of the Workers’ Compensation Board under ORS 147.005 to 147.367
shall be open to the public unless the department or board determines that the
information shall be kept confidential or that a closed hearing shall be held
because: (a) The alleged
assailant has not been brought to trial and disclosure of the information or a
public hearing would adversely affect either the apprehension or the trial of
the alleged assailant; (b) The offense
allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse,
trafficking in persons or a crime involving domestic violence as defined in ORS
135.230, and the interests of the victim or of the victim’s dependents require
that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from
the hearing;
added.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rule.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund for a sexual assault medical assessment may not bill the survivor for it, unless the Fund lacks money or declines to pay. The statute does not address billing the survivor's insurance; the SAVE Fund rule does, and it bars billing insurance too.
rule.quote: A provider who submits a bill under this subsection may not bill the victim for the medical assessment except to the extent that the department is unable to pay the bill due to lack of funds or declines to pay the bill.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.condition: if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it

rule.summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurance for the exam, evidence collection, or other services given with the exam (exceptions: the Fund lacks money or declines to pay for reasons other than a late or incomplete bill).
rule.quote: An eligible medical services provider (including subcontractor or other designee) who submits a bill to the Fund under these rules may not bill the victim or the victim's insurance carrier for a medical examination, collection of forensic evidence using the Oregon State Police SAFE Kit, or other services provided in conjunction with the sexual assault exam
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: The Oregon Department of Justice pays for a sexual assault medical assessment through the SAVE Fund, subject to available funds and the time frame set by rule.
rule.quote: Subject to the availability of funds from gifts, grants and donations in the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund, the Department of Justice shall pay the costs of a medical assessment obtained by a victim if the victim obtains the medical assessment within the time frame established in rules adopted by the department.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: A survivor can get a SAVE Fund paid medical assessment without reporting the assault to police.

after.summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.

rule.summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.
rule.quote: A victim may obtain a medical assessment and complete and submit a form under this section regardless of whether the victim reports the sexual assault to a law enforcement agency.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Medical and hospital expenses, including counseling and medications, are covered up to $20,000 combined.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: The victim's counseling counts toward the same $20,000 limit as medical and hospital expenses.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are paid at up to $600 per week.
rule.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are capped at $20,000 in total.
rule.quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Lost earnings are figured at 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the crime.
rule.quote: Compensation for lost earnings under ORS 147.035(2)(b) shall be computed on the basis of 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the compensable crime.
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rule.summary: A parent or guardian who misses work to care for a minor victim can get up to $5,000 in lost earnings.
rule.quote: Loss of earnings for the parent or guardian are compensable up to a maximum of $5,000.00 under the child victim's claim under ORS 147.035 (2)(f).
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rule.summary: Travel for the victim's covered medical care or counseling is paid up to $3,000, only when the care is more than 30 miles from home and adequate care is not available closer.
rule.quote: Expenses related to transportation for the victim's medical care or counseling, at a rate determined by the Department of Justice, up to a maximum amount of $3,000, when: (A) The medical care or counseling is compensable under this section; (B) The medical care or counseling is provided more than 30 miles away from the victim's residence; and (C) Adequate medical care or counseling is not available in closer proximity to the victim's residence.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.scope: mileage to medical and mental health treatment

rule.summary: Mileage to medical and mental health treatment is reimbursed at 50 cents per mile, up to $3,000.
rule.quote: Reimbursement of mileage (50¢ per mile) for travel to medical and mental health treatment, up to $3,000.
rule.pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), What Does CVC Pay For?
rule.source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

rule.summary: Rehabilitation expenses, such as physical therapy, are covered up to $4,000.
rule.quote: The victim's rehabilitation expenses, up to a maximum amount of $4,000
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params.extension: good cause shown, at the department's discretion
or later if the department gives you more time for good cause

rule.summary: The application must be filed within one year of the injury, or later if the department allows an extension for good cause.
rule.quote: Within one year of the date of the injury to the victim; or (B) Within such further extension of time as the department, for good cause shown, allows.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Good cause for filing after one year includes not knowing about the program, police not giving the required information, or trauma that got in the way of filing on time.
rule.quote: "Good cause" for failure to file an application for compensation within one year of the date of the crime as required by ORS 147.015(1)(e) includes but is not limited to the victim's lack of knowledge of the Crime Victims' Compensation Program, failure of a law enforcement official to provide information to the victim as required by ORS 147.365(1), or emotional or physical trauma sustained by the victim that was a barrier to timely filing the application for compensation.
rule.source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

before.summary: The reporting requirement is also met by a sexual assault medical assessment or other forensic exam, or a health or mental health provider certifying the victim reported to them, or other documentation the department accepts.

after.summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.

rule.summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.
rule.quote: (E) A medical assessment, as defined in ORS 147.395, for sexual assault, or any other forensic exam or medical assessment; (b) A health provider, tribal health provider, student health provider or community mental health provider certifies that the victim reported the crime to the provider; or (c) The victim provides to the department documentation that qualifies as law enforcement notification under the rules of the department.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source the victim received or is entitled to.

after.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.

rule.summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.
rule.quote: shall deduct the amount of benefits, payments or awards that are payable under the Workers' Compensation Law, from local governmental, state or federal funds or from any source, and that the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim have received or to which the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim are entitled as a result of the death or injury of the victim
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Eligibility depends on the department finding the victim acted reasonably given the victim's specific situation. Shown for information only.
rule.quote: The department determines that the victim acted reasonably with respect to the incident causing the death or injury to the victim, taking into account the specific situation of the victim and what a reasonable action would be for a person in the victim's circumstances
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

rule.summary: Injury includes mental or emotional harm and pregnancy, not only physical harm.
rule.quote: "Injury" means abuse of a corpse, actual bodily harm, mental or emotional harm and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy and mental or nervous shock.
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

before.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state can apply in Oregon only if that state has no reciprocal compensation program; otherwise the state where the crime happened pays.

after.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state that has no reciprocal crime victims' compensation program can apply in Oregon.

rule.summary: An Oregon resident hurt in another U.S. state that has no reciprocal crime victims' compensation program can apply in Oregon.
rule.quote: Who is an Oregon resident killed or injured as a result of a compensable crime perpetrated or attempted against the person in a state, within the United States, without a reciprocal crime victims' compensation program
rule.source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

added.summary: For the program to pay for the exam, the hospital must notify the local police where the assault happened within 12 hours of collecting the evidence.
added.quote: In order for payments to be considered, hospitals or licensed health care providers requesting reimbursement of costs associated with a forensic rape examination are required to notify the local law enforcement agency where the reported sexual assault occurred within 12 hours of collection of the sexual assault evidence as per the Sexual Assault Testing and Evidence Collection Act (Act 165 of 2006).
added.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
added.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

added.summary: Adults 18 or older can choose an anonymous report when evidence is collected, if they are worried about the kit going to police. A minor's exam cannot be done anonymously.
added.quote: Adult victims (age 18 or older) have the option of anonymous reporting and gathering of evidence and may consider this option if they have concerns about the kit being provided to police. An exam cannot be completed anonymously for a minor.
added.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

added.summary: A helper who is not a family member is paid at most $8 an hour. A family member who does the work is paid their own lost earnings, up to the average weekly wage.
added.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation. (i) Members of the family of the direct victim or intervenor engaged to perform the services will be paid their net loss of earnings not to exceed the average weekly wage and if not otherwise reimbursed for the loss of earnings. (ii) Individuals engaged to perform services who are not family members will be paid a maximum hourly rate of $8.
added.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: The program's page says the 5-year limit is for crimes on or after 9/8/2022. For an older crime, it asks you to contact the program to find out the filing rules.
added.quote: For crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, the claim must be filed within 5 years of the crime. For crimes occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the Program to determine filing requirements.
added.pinpoint: PA.gov Apply for Victims' Compensation page, Who is eligible?
added.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

added.summary: Claims for counseling related to sexual abuse are an exception to the filing deadline.
added.quote: (2) Exceptions shall be as follows: (i) ((i) deleted by amendment). (i.1) Claims for counseling services related to sexual abuse under section 701.1.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the abuser was a parent, a caretaker, someone living in the same home, or a parent's partner, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21. It then runs until the later of the criminal time limit for the crime or the usual deadline.
added.quote: If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the alleged offender is the direct victim's parent or a person responsible for the direct victim's welfare, an individual residing in the same home as the direct victim or a paramour of the direct victim's parent, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age. (B) The limitation period shall run until the later of: (I) the end of the limitation period for the offense as set forth in 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 55 Subch. C (relating to criminal proceedings); or (II) the end of the limitation period under paragraph (1).
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the claim is only for counseling, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21.
added.quote: (ii.1) If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the direct victim is seeking reimbursement for counseling services only, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The Office of Victims' Services may accept a late claim for good cause, such as when the victim was incapacitated or a minor, feared retaliation, or the crime was not readily apparent.
added.quote: (iii.1) The Office of Victims' Services may find good cause to accept a claim beyond the limitation period under paragraph (1) if one of the following circumstances existed at the time of the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the occurrence of the crime: (A) The direct victim, intervenor or claimant was mentally or physically incapacitated. (B) The victim was a minor. (C) There was a fear of retaliation. (D) The occurrence of the crime was not readily apparent. (E) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The program's manual says the filing, reporting, and minimum loss rules are different for a crime before 9/8/2022, and asks you to contact the program about them.
added.quote: For eligibility requirements for crime occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the program as there are different filing requirement, reporting requirement, and minimum loss requirements.
added.pinpoint: VCAP Manual for Compensation Assistance, Eligibility
added.source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

added.summary: If you start a protection order case to meet the report rule and then drop it, you cannot get an award unless the program finds you had good reason to drop it.
added.quote: An award may not be made if the record shows that the petition was withdrawn, except if the Office of Victims' Services finds the withdrawal to have been justified, consistent with regulations of the Office of Victims' Services.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: For a standard claim, the survivor must also have fully cooperated with law enforcement and the program, unless the program finds there was a good reason not to.
added.quote: The direct victim, intervenor or claimant has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and the Office of Victims' Services, unless the Office of Victims' Services finds the noncompliance to have been justified consistent with the Office of Victims' Services regulations.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

added.summary: The program may excuse not cooperating if the survivor was incapacitated, feared retaliation, was a minor, or shows other good cause.
added.quote: OVS may consider a failure to cooperate with law enforcement and OVS to be justified when one of the following circumstances exist: (1) The direct victim, intervenor or the claimant is mentally or physically incapacitated. (2) There is a fear of retaliation. (3) The victim is a minor. (4) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
added.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: Mail the completed claim form to VCAP's mailing address, PO Box 1167, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167.
added.quote: Mailing Address PO Box 1167 Harrisburg, PA 17108-1167
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: File the claim online through the DAVE portal (the Crime Victims App also files online).
added.quote: File online at https://www.dave.pa.gov
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Email the completed claim form to VCAP at ra-davesupport@pa.gov.
added.quote: Email ra-davesupport@pa.gov
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), back page contact block; PA.gov apply page step 4: 'Mail or email your claim'
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized medical bills related to the crime, in the victim's name.
added.quote: Provide all itemized medical bills related to the crime. Medical bills must be in the name of the victim.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.quote: Provide all itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Include copies of cancelled checks or receipts for any bills the victim or claimant already paid.
added.quote: Provide copies of cancelled checks and/or receipts for any bills paid by the victim/claimant.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: If insured, submit bills to insurance first and include the insurance statements showing payments or rejections.
added.quote: Provide insurance statements of all payments and/or rejections for corresponding bills.
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include two pay stubs from right before the crime, W-2 statements, or the most recent tax return with all schedules.
added.quote: Provide two pay stubs immediately prior to the crime incident, W-2 statements, or most recently filed IRS tax returns including all schedules.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages from crime injuries, a doctor, psychologist, or other listed provider must certify the disability.
added.quote: If filing for loss of earnings due to crime-related injuries a physician verification certifying disability is needed.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For lost wages, include proof of any sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay or other benefits received.
added.quote: Provide documentation of any reimbursements received, such as sick, vacation, personal, or disability pay
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: For relocation, include a letter from a human service agency, law enforcement, or a medical provider saying the move is needed for safety and health.
added.quote: Please provide a verification letter explaining that the immediate need for relocation is necessary to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the same household
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: Sign the Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information (and the HIPAA release for medical or counseling expenses) before the claim can be processed.
added.quote: The Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information must be signed before a claim can be verified and processed for payment.
added.pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Acknowledgement & Reimbursement Agreements section
added.source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

added.summary: The program says most claims are processed in 12 weeks or less, though each claim differs.
added.quote: Most organizations process claims in 12 weeks or less.
added.pinpoint: PA.gov apply page, FAQ: How long does it take the Program to make a decision?
added.source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

added.summary: Once approved, payments owed to the victim or claimant of $5,000 or less are released within 2 business days.
added.quote: Payments owed to the victim/claimant that total $5,000.00 or less are released within 2 business days of being approved.
added.source_title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

added.summary: Pennsylvania's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Advocate, can give survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction an alternate mailing address to keep their address out of public records, once the office approves their application.
added.quote: The ACP can provide you with an alternate mailing address to keep your address out of public records if you are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or child abduction.
added.pinpoint: OVA Address Confidentiality Program page; statute: 23 Pa.C.S. 6703(a), 6704(2)
added.source_title: PA Office of Victim Advocate: Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)

added.summary: Everything VCAP obtains or produces while processing a claim is confidential and privileged, is not subject to subpoena or discovery, and may be used only to process the claim; disclosure needs the victim's written consent except as the law provides.
added.quote:
All reports, records or other information
obtained or produced by the Office of Victims' Services during
the processing or investigation of a claim shall be confidential
and privileged, shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery,
shall be used for no purpose other than the processing of a
claim
added.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor. Insurance is billed first unless the survivor asks that it not be.

after.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.

rule.summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.
rule.quote: The cost of a forensic rape examination and the cost of medications prescribed to the direct victim shall not be charged to the victim.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rule.summary: If the program pays the maximum and a balance remains, the provider still may not bill the survivor; the program payment is payment in full.
rule.quote: No. A health care provider must accept the payment in full for the costs of the forensic rape examination.
rule.source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

rule.summary: The provider must file the exam claim within one year of the crime or its discovery; if the provider misses that deadline, the survivor still cannot be billed.
rule.quote: The claim must be filed by a hospital or other licensed health care provider, within one year of the date of the crime or discovery of the crime. Failure to file within the prescribed time frame will result in non-payment of the claim and the victim cannot be billed for those costs.
rule.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.4
rule.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params.exception: not counting some costs that are paid on top

rule.summary: The total award is capped at $35,000, except that counseling, forensic rape exam costs, and crime scene cleanup are paid on top of that cap.
rule.quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

rule.summary: Lost earnings caused by the injury are covered, up to the state average weekly wage for each week, if not otherwise reimbursed.
rule.quote: OVS may make an award within the monetary limitations of the act to compensate a direct victim, intervenor or claimant for loss of earnings attributable to the injury not to exceed the average weekly wage if the claimant was not otherwise reimbursed for the loss.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

rule.summary: Temporary or permanent relocation is covered when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and household, verified by a medical provider, human services provider, or law enforcement.
rule.quote: expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a direct victim and individuals residing in the household of the direct victim due to the incident forming the basis of the victim's claim when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the household, as verified by a medical provider, human services provider or law enforcement
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

rule.summary: The move must happen within 120 days of the crime, or within 120 days of a new threat or sign of danger.
rule.quote: Relocation must occur within 120 days from the date of crime, or 120 days from the date the victim is threatened by any change of circumstance or indicator of danger.
rule.source_title: VCAP flyer: Relocation Expenses (11/2023)

params.item: replacing medical devices, eyeglasses, and prescription medicine

rule.summary: Replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dental devices, prescription medications and similar health items stolen or damaged in the crime is capped at $1,000, with eyeglass frames limited to $200. This is not a cap on ordinary medical bills.
rule.quote: OVS will reimburse a claimant for costs for the replacement of each prosthetic device, wheelchair, cane, walker, hearing aid, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, dental device or prescription medications. Reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 and will be subject to the following limitations: (1)  Two hundred dollars for eyeglass frames.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.scope: services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, or laundry

rule.summary: Services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, laundry, and meal preparation, can be reimbursed.
rule.quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params.extension: Good cause can excuse a late filing (incapacity, victim was a minor, fear of retaliation, crime not readily apparent, other good cause; 18 P.S. 11.702(b)(2)(iii.1)). For a victim under 18 abused by a parent, caretaker, household member or parent's paramour, the period is tolled until age 21 and runs to the later of the criminal limitation period or the standard period. Sexual abuse counseling claims under 18 P.S. 11.701.1 are excepted from this deadline.

before.summary: A claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered, under the current law; the program may accept a late claim for good cause. Older crimes had a shorter deadline, so those survivors should call the program.

params.extension: or later in some cases, such as sexual abuse counseling claims, some survivors who were children, or when the program finds good cause

after.summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.

rule.summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.
rule.quote: a claim must be filed not later than five years after the discovery of the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: The crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities; the statute sets no fixed number of hours. A protection order filing (statute) or a forensic rape exam (program policy) also counts.

after.summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.

rule.summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.
rule.quote: The crime was promptly reported to the proper authorities.
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: Filing for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order satisfies the reporting requirement, even without a police report.

after.summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.

rule.summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.
rule.quote: may satisfy the eligibility requirement under subsection (a)(3) for reporting a crime to the proper authorities by commencing an action brought in accordance with 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 62A (relating to protection of victims of sexual violence or intimidation)
rule.source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

before.summary: Having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without going to police.

params.exam_condition: for a crime on or after September 8, 2022

after.summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.

rule.summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.
rule.quote: Effective for crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, a forensic rape exam is considered acceptable for reporting to proper authorities. This change allows victims who have the FRE completed to be eligible for a standard claim without having to report the crime to law enforcement.
rule.pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
rule.source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

before.summary: An emergency award of up to $5,000 per claim is available for urgent financial need.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.
rule.quote: The total amount of an emergency award will not exceed $5,000 per claim.
rule.source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

added.summary: The Attorney General's bill of rights page also warns that choosing not to take part in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for compensation benefits.
added.quote: However, your decision not to participate in the criminal justice system will likely limit your eligibility for benefits under the crime victim compensation program.
added.pinpoint: Attorney General's Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights page, Your right to choose whether to report
added.source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

added.summary: If you found out about the crime more than 1 year after it happened, the time to apply starts when you found out, or should have. This applies only if the crime led to a criminal complaint, an indictment or criminal information, or another court finding of probable cause.
added.quote: If the Applicant did not discover the act which constitutes a crime until more than one year after the crime was committed, the filing period shall not commence until the Applicant discovered or, in exercise of reasonable diligence, should have discovered, the act which constitutes a crime, provided, however, that in such cases, the crime for which the Applicant seeks compensation must have resulted in the issuance of a criminal complaint, indictment or criminal information, or other judicial determination of probable cause that an act constituting a crime occurred
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Not knowing the filing rules does not count as good cause for a late application.
added.quote: Delay resulting from the lack of knowledge of the filing requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-25-1, et seq. shall not constitute good cause.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Believing police will not investigate, or not knowing that an award depends on reporting the crime, is not good cause for a late report. The program's rule also says good cause excuses only the delay, not the reporting requirement itself.
added.quote: Delay resulting from a belief that law enforcement authorities will not investigate the crime, or delay resulting from lack of knowledge that an award under R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-1 et. seq. is contingent upon reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities, does not constitute good cause for delay. d. A finding of good cause for delay does not excuse the reporting requirement which must be satisfied as a condition of receiving compensation.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: The program's rule says a victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. It says this includes reporting the crime, helping identify the suspect, and following reasonable requests for information and help.
added.quote: A victim must cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. a. Victim’s obligations: Cooperation with law enforcement agencies and personnel includes reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities; assisting in identifying the suspect; and complying with all reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel for information and assistance.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: Emergency relocation is capped at $5,000. Any relocation award is deducted from the final award.
added.quote: Compensation awarded for emergency relocation expenses shall not exceed the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). Any award for emergency relocation expenses shall be deducted from the final award.
added.source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

added.summary: To be paid for a move, the crime must have happened in your home. If it did not, you must show the crime makes you reasonably afraid to stay there. You must also need to move right away, reasonably fear living as you did before the crime, or be unable to afford your documented housing costs right after the crime.
added.quote: The crime must have occurred in the victim’s primary place of residence or the Applicant must demonstrate that, as a result of the crime, he or she reasonably fears for his or her continued safety in his or her primary place of residence. (2) An Applicant must have an immediate need to relocate, a reasonable fear to continue to live within the arrangements as established prior to the crime, or, alternatively, immediately following the crime, the Applicant must be unable to afford the documented housing costs.

added.summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of State, helps victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move. To qualify, you must live in Rhode Island, fear for your own or your children's safety, live or plan to live at an address the person who harmed you does not know, and agree not to give that person the address. You apply by mailing a sworn application to the Department, which can help you fill it out.

added.summary: Medical, counseling, psychiatric, employment, financial, and investigative records the compensation office gets with a claim are confidential and cannot be released without the applicant's permission unless law allows it. rule.summary: The total award to a victim cannot exceed $25,000 (plus any attorney fees awarded on appeal).
rule.quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter to the victim, or in the case of death to dependent relatives or to the legal representative, in a total amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)

rule.summary: For a victim who was a minor, the application is due within three years after turning eighteen.

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 15 days, but the office may allow a claim without a police report when a sexual assault survivor had a medical forensic exam within 15 days of the crime.

after.summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws 15-15-3 with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.

rule.quote: Good cause for delay shall include, but not be limited to, delay caused by physical or psychological incapacity which prevented the making of a report; or by reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.

before.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior contributed to the injury; the same subsection also lets it weigh cooperation with police and violent criminal history.

after.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.

rule.summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.
rule.quote: The behavior of the victim, including past behavior, that directly or indirectly contributed to his or her injury or death, unless the injury or death resulted from the victim’s lawful attempt to prevent the commission of a crime or to apprehend an offender. before.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days of the latest qualifying event (usually the crime). For good cause the deadline can be extended, but not past four years after the crime, diagnosed manifestation, or death.

params.extension: or of a later date in some cases, such as when police learned it was a crime. With good cause, the program can allow up to 4 years after the crime

after.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.
rule.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than one hundred eighty days after the latest of the following events: (1) the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; (2) the death of the victim; (3) the discovery by the law enforcement agency that the occurrence was the result of crime; or (4) the manifestation of a mental or physical injury is diagnosed as a result of a crime committed against a minor. (C) Upon good cause shown, the time for filing may be extended for a period not to exceed four years after the occurrence, diagnosed manifestation, or death.

added.summary: The claimant must give written proof that the offense happened; medical records from a health care provider are one accepted form of proof.
added.quote: Medical records from a healthcare provider, as those terms are defined in
added.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-103 (burden of proof; documentation; proof of offense), 2025 via Justia

added.summary: If claiming lost wages, include wage documentation; the statute lists lost wage verifications and W-2 forms.
added.quote: Lost wage verifications; (iii) W-2 forms
added.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-103 (burden of proof; documentation; proof of offense), 2025 via Justia

added.summary: For lost wages, the employer completes the program's Employer's Statement and sends it to the program in Nashville.
added.quote: Complete the form request below and send to: State of Tennessee Treasury Department Criminal Injuries Compensation Program 502 Deaderick Street w Nashville, TN 37243-0202
added.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation Employer's Statement (RDA-1178)

added.summary: The division must make every effort to approve or deny a claim within 90 days of receiving it.
added.quote: the division shall investigate every claim for compensation and shall make every effort to honor or deny each claim within ninety (90) days of receipt of the claim
added.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

added.summary: Safe at Home is a free program run by the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to survivors of rape, sexual battery, or another sex crime, and of domestic abuse, stalking, or human trafficking, who meet its eligibility and application rules. Once approved, you get a substitute address to use as your official mailing address for state and local government.
added.quote: The Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program is a statewide address confidentiality program administered by the Office of the Tennessee Secretary of State. It is open to all victims of domestic abuse, stalking, human trafficking, rape, sexual battery, or any other sexual offense who satisfy eligibility and application requirements at no cost. Once a participant has been approved, they are provided with a 'substitute' address that can be used by them and their children as their official mailing address for all state and local government purposes
added.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ 'What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?'; statute T.C.A. 40-38-601 to 40-38-604 (enroll text from 40-38-604(a))
added.source_title: Tennessee Secretary of State, Safe at Home FAQ: What is the Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program?

added.summary: For victims who apply for compensation, Tennessee law makes the home address, home and personal cell phone numbers, Social Security number, and the crime the victim is being compensated for confidential and closed to public inspection. The statute does not list the victim's name or the rest of the claim file.
added.quote: The following information regarding victims who apply for compensation under the Criminal Injuries Compensation Act, compiled in title 29, chapter 13, shall be treated as confidential and shall not be open for inspection by members of the public: (1) Residential information, including the street address, city, state and zip code; (2) Home telephone and personal cell phone numbers; (3) Social security number; and (4) The criminal offense from which the victim is receiving compensation.
added.source_title: T.C.A. 10-7-504 (confidential records; (k) Criminal Injuries Compensation Act applicants), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: A victim does not have to report to police or cooperate with prosecution for the forensic exam to be paid.
rule.quote: the victims shall not be required to report the incident to law enforcement officers or to cooperate in the prosecution of the crime in order to be eligible for payment of forensic medical examinations
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params.condition: for a crime on or after July 1, 2025

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 1, 2025, the Treasury lists an overall maximum of $34,100 for all expenses on claims from the crime. The cap depends on the crime date.
rule.quote: For crimes occurring on or after July 1, 2025: $34,100
rule.pinpoint: Treasury Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025); set under T.C.A. 29-13-106(h)
rule.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025)

params.item: pain and suffering
params.scope: for victims of rape, human trafficking, or another sexual crime

rule.summary: Pain and suffering is not paid for most crimes, but it can be paid to victims of rape, human trafficking, and crimes involving sexual deviancy.
rule.quote: Compensation must not be awarded for any personal injury or loss alleged to have been incurred as a result of pain and suffering, except for victims of the crime of rape, victims of a human trafficking offense, and victims of a crime involving sexual deviancy
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.item: pain and suffering

rule.summary: A pain and suffering award for a victim of a sexually-oriented crime may not exceed $3,000.
rule.quote: Any award based on the pain and suffering experienced by a claimant victimized by a sexually-oriented crime is to be made in an amount deemed necessary and appropriate, not to exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: Lost wages caused by the crime are paid on the workers' compensation temporary total disability schedule, but at 85 percent of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rule.quote: Any award made for lost wages proximately caused by a violent crime is to be based upon those schedules of compensation for temporary total disability allowable by the workers' compensation statutes, found in § 50-6-207, in effect at the time of the commission of the crime giving rise to such claim; provided, however, that the sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) rate prescribed in the workers' compensation statutes shall not be used in determining the amount of any award hereunder. Instead, such rate shall be eighty-five percent (85%) of the claimant's average weekly wage.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: If the assault happened at the victim's home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and utility transfer fees are covered, for no more than 2 moves.

params.scope: moving costs, if the assault happened at your home, for up to 2 moves

after.summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.

rule.summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.
rule.quote: The victim's reasonable moving expenses, storage fees and fees for transfer of utility service if the move is a direct result of an assault committed upon such victim at the victim's residence, provided that the victim shall not receive compensation for more than two (2) moves resulting from the assault
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params.scope: cleaning the scene, if it was your home or a relative's home

rule.summary: Reasonable costs to clean the scene of a sexual assault are covered when the scene was the home of the victim or a relative.
rule.quote: Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred for cleaning supplies, equipment rental and labor needed to clean the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault, if the scene was the residence of the victim or a relative of the victim
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial (and later appeals) is capped at a cumulative $1,250. This cap is only for court travel.

after.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.

rule.summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.
rule.quote: Any award made under the preceding sentence to a claimant shall not exceed a cumulative total of one thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($1,250) for all such travel.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: The Treasury lists travel to doctor appointments as not covered.
rule.quote: Travel to Doctor Appointments
rule.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rule.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

params.item: eyeglasses and hearing aids; property damaged in processing a sexual assault scene at the residence

before.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, repair, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged by the crime are covered, as is property damaged while processing a sexual assault scene at the home of the victim or a relative.

params.item: eyeglasses and hearing aids; property damaged in processing a sexual assault scene at the residence
params.scope: cleaning, fixing, or replacing the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids damaged by the crime or the crime scene work

after.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, fix, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids are covered when the crime or the crime scene work damaged them.

rule.summary: Reasonable costs to clean, fix, or replace the victim's eyeglasses and hearing aids are covered when the crime or the crime scene work damaged them.
rule.quote: Reasonable costs of cleaning, repairing or replacing eyeglasses and hearing aids owned by the victim that were damaged or destroyed by the crime or the processing of the crime scene
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: The Treasury lists deposits, rent, and utility bills as not covered.
rule.quote: Deposits, Rent and Utility Bills
rule.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rule.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

rule.summary: The Treasury lists costs from identity theft or fraud as not covered.
rule.quote: Cost from Identity Theft or Fraud
rule.pinpoint: Treasury CIC resource guide, Eligible versus Ineligible
rule.source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation resource guide (brochure)

params.extension: Good cause can extend the period, before or after it runs. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, the claim may also be filed within 2 years after a resulting mental or physical injury is diagnosed.
or later if the program extends it for good cause

rule.summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years after the crime. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, it can also be filed within 2 years after a resulting injury is diagnosed, and good cause can extend the time.
rule.quote: A claim for compensation must be filed not later than two (2) years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based, two (2) years after the death of the victim, or two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses; provided, that upon good cause shown, the time period for filing such claim may be extended either before or after the expiration of the filing period.
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

params.exception: or later if there is good cause, which can include sexual assault

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authorities within 15 days, but a late report can be excused for good cause, and being a victim of sexual assault is a listed reason for good cause.
rule.quote: A claim cannot be filed until the crime upon which the claim is based has been reported by the victim, or a member of the victim's family, to the proper authorities within fifteen (15) days after the occurrence of such crime unless, for good cause shown, it is found that the delay was justified. Good cause for the failure of a victim or a member of the victim's family to report a crime may be found if the victim is: (1) Physically unable; (2) A victim of sexual assault;
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

rule.summary: To qualify, the claimant needs at least $100 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 2 continuous weeks of lost earnings or support, unless the limit would not serve the interest of justice.
rule.quote: no award shall be made unless the claimant has incurred a minimum out of pocket loss of one hundred dollars ($100) or has lost at least two (2) continuous weeks earnings or support, unless it is determined that the interest of justice would not be served by such a limitation
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

before.summary: The claims commission may make an emergency award of up to $500 before a final decision when an award is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship. It is deducted from the final award.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.
rule.quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
rule.source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-114 (emergency award), 2025 via Justia

added.summary: Other victims can be paid moving costs and rent when a move is needed to protect their health or safety.
added.quote: A victim other than a victim described by Subsection (c), a dependent of any victim, a family member of any victim if that family member has previously resided with the victim for a period of not less than two years, or a household member of any victim may receive compensation for the following expenses, if the expenses are necessary to protect the health or safety of the victim, dependent, or family or household member: (1) relocation expenses, including expenses for rental deposit, utility connections, expenses relating to moving belongings, motor vehicle mileage expenses, temporary or emergency lodging, and for an out-of-state move, expenses for transportation, lodging, and meals; and (2) housing rental expenses.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: If you were subpoenaed to appear in court, the program does not pay for those trips. Its page says to ask the prosecutor's office instead.
added.quote: Note: Victims or claimants subpoenaed to appear in court cannot receive reimbursement through the CVC program for those appearances. If subpoenaed, please seek reimbursement from the prosecutor’s office.
added.pinpoint: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement page, Note
added.source_title: OAG Travel Cost Reimbursement

added.summary: For care sought after August 31, 2025, Emergency Medical Care also pays for prescribed care tied to the assault in the 30 days after the exam.
added.quote: For medical care sought after August 31, 2025, EMC also covers any prescribed continuing medical care that is related to the sexual assault and provided to the victim during the 30-day period following the exam.
added.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation page
added.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

added.summary: If the victim is a child, the time to apply counts from the day the victim or claimant learns of the crime. It ends on the third anniversary of that day, and no later than the child's 21st birthday.
added.quote: If the victim is a child, the application must be filed not later than the third anniversary of the date the claimant or victim is made aware of the offense, but not after the child attains 21 years of age.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: If medical records show the crime left you unable to apply, that time does not count toward the deadline.
added.quote: If a claimant or victim presents medically documented evidence of a physical or mental incapacity that was incurred by the claimant or victim as a result of the criminally injurious conduct and that reasonably prevented the claimant or victim from filing the application within the limitations period under Subsection (a), the period of the incapacity is not included.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: The attorney general may give more time to report in extraordinary circumstances. The report rule does not apply if the victim is a child.
added.quote: The attorney general may extend the time for reporting the criminally injurious conduct if the attorney general determines that the extension is justified by extraordinary circumstances. (c) Subsection (a) does not apply if the victim is a child.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

added.summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Attorney General's Crime Victims' Compensation Program, P.O. Box 12198, Austin, Texas 78711-2198.
added.quote: Mail your completed application to: Office of the Attorney General Crime Victims' Compensation Program (011) P.O. Box 12198 Austin, Texas 78711-2198
added.source_title: Texas Crime Victims' Compensation Program Application (paper, rev. 10/15)

added.summary: Apply online through the CVC Portal, the program's fastest route; the portal also takes uploaded bills and shows status updates.
added.quote: The CVC Portal is the fastest way to apply. Through the portal, you can submit your application online, upload billing documents, and check status updates.
added.pinpoint: OAG How to Apply page, Step 1
added.source_title: OAG How to Apply for Crime Victims' Compensation

added.summary: Send a copy of the police report with the application if you have it.
added.quote: If you have a copy of the police report, protective order with affidavit, hospital or doctor bills, health insurance card, or auto insurance declaration page (if the crime is auto-related), be sure to send them with the application.
added.source_title: Texas Crime Victims' Compensation Program Application (paper, rev. 10/15)

added.summary: Send a copy of any protective order with its affidavit.
added.quote: If you have a copy of the police report, protective order with affidavit, hospital or doctor bills, health insurance card, or auto insurance declaration page (if the crime is auto-related), be sure to send them with the application.
added.source_title: Texas Crime Victims' Compensation Program Application (paper, rev. 10/15)

added.summary: Include itemized medical bills with the application.
added.quote: Gather Medical Care Bills: Include the following documents with your application: Itemized medical bills Receipts for any paid bills Insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOB), if applicable
added.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

added.summary: Include receipts for any bills already paid.
added.quote: Gather Medical Care Bills: Include the following documents with your application: Itemized medical bills Receipts for any paid bills Insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOB), if applicable
added.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

added.summary: Include the insurance Explanation of Benefits (EOB) if insurance was billed.

added.pinpoint: OAG Emergency Medical Care page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Emergency Medical Care Compensation (sexual assault exam)

added.summary: Send a copy of the health insurance card with the application.
added.quote: If you have a copy of the police report, protective order with affidavit, hospital or doctor bills, health insurance card, or auto insurance declaration page (if the crime is auto-related), be sure to send them with the application.
added.source_title: Texas Crime Victims' Compensation Program Application (paper, rev. 10/15)

added.summary: For lost wages, the program may ask for verification of employment, medical documentation, and its lost wage or appointment forms.
added.quote: Provide Supporting Documents: You may need to submit: Lost Wage Affirmation form (for ongoing disability) Travel/Appointment form (for periodic absences) Verification of employment Medical documentation Proof of disability payments
added.pinpoint: OAG Lost Wages page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Lost Wages for Victims

added.summary: For lost wages, the program may ask for medical documentation.
added.quote: Provide Supporting Documents: You may need to submit: Lost Wage Affirmation form (for ongoing disability) Travel/Appointment form (for periodic absences) Verification of employment Medical documentation Proof of disability payments
added.pinpoint: OAG Lost Wages page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Lost Wages for Victims

added.summary: For rent and relocation, the program asks for its acknowledgement and worksheet forms and the complete lease agreement.
added.quote: Relocation and Rental Assistance Acknowledgement Relocation Expense Worksheet Payment Affirmation (if you want payment sent directly to the landlord) Letter of Intent form (if requesting funds before the move) Your complete lease agreement (if requesting funds after the move)
added.pinpoint: OAG Rent and Relocation page, How to apply
added.source_title: OAG Rent and Relocation Reimbursement

added.summary: The Attorney General runs an address confidentiality program for survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes. It gives each participant a substitute P.O. box address to use instead of their real home, work, or school address, and forwards their mail.
added.quote: (a)  The attorney general shall establish an address confidentiality program, as provided by this subchapter, to assist a victim of family violence, sexual assault or abuse, stalking, child abduction, or trafficking of persons in maintaining a confidential address. (b)  The attorney general shall: (1)  designate a substitute post office box address that a participant may use in place of the participant's true residential, business, or school address;
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 58 (Confidentiality of Identifying Information; Address Confidentiality Program, Subch. B)

added.summary: Texas law keeps your compensation application and the Attorney General's records on it private, with some exceptions. Once compensation is awarded, the name of the victim or claimant and the amount are public under Gov. Code 552.132(c). A court order, your consent, or a subpoena in a criminal case can also open some records.
added.quote: An application for compensation under this chapter and any information, document, summary, or other record provided to or received, maintained, or created by the attorney general under this chapter, including a report released to the attorney general under Article 56B.054 (f), is: (1)  except as provided by Section 552.132 (c), Government Code, not subject to disclosure under Chapter 552 of that code; and (2)  except as provided by Subsection (c), not subject to disclosure, discovery, subpoena, or other means of legal compulsion for release.
added.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

params.scope: the forensic part of an exam or the evidence kit

rule.summary: A sexual assault survivor cannot be made to pay for the forensic part of the exam or the evidence kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed for it.
rule.quote: A victim of a sexual assault may not be required to pay for: (1) the forensic portion of the forensic medical examination; or (2) the evidence collection kit.
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

rule.summary: The Attorney General reimburses the provider or examiner for the forensic portion of the exam, the evidence kit, and medical care given during the exam.
rule.quote: a health care provider that provides a forensic medical examination to a sexual assault survivor in accordance with this subchapter, or the sexual assault examiner or sexual assault nurse examiner who conducts that examination in accordance with this subchapter, as applicable, is entitled to be reimbursed in an amount set by attorney general rule for: (1) the reasonable costs of the forensic portion of that examination; (2) the evidence collection kit;
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

before.summary: Emergency Medical Care (EMC): the Attorney General pays for medical care given during a sexual assault forensic exam, and prescribed related follow-up care, at medical fee guideline rates, up to $25,000. The program's medical care page treats this as separate from the general award cap.

after.summary: Emergency Medical Care (EMC): the Attorney General pays for medical care given during a sexual assault forensic exam, at medical fee guideline rates, up to $25,000. The program's medical care page treats this as separate from the general award cap.

rule.summary: Emergency Medical Care (EMC): the Attorney General pays for medical care given during a sexual assault forensic exam, at medical fee guideline rates, up to $25,000. The program's medical care page treats this as separate from the general award cap.
rule.quote: The attorney general shall make a payment under Subsection (a) in accordance with the medical fee guidelines prescribed by Subtitle A, Title 5, Labor Code. A payment made under Subsection (a) may not exceed $25,000.
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56A (Subchapter G, forensic medical examination)

rule.summary: Awards for one victim and everyone claiming because of that victim's injury may not exceed $50,000 in total.
rule.quote: Except as otherwise provided by this article, awards payable to a victim and any other claimant sustaining pecuniary loss because of injury or death of that victim may not exceed $50,000 in the aggregate.
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

before.summary: A victim of sexual assault who was assaulted in their own home can be compensated for relocation costs and housing rent; other victims can qualify when the move is needed for health or safety.

params.scope: moving costs and rent, if the assault happened in your home

after.summary: A victim of sexual assault who was assaulted at home can be paid relocation costs and housing rent.

rule.summary: A victim of sexual assault who was assaulted at home can be paid relocation costs and housing rent.
rule.quote: A victim of stalking, family violence, or trafficking of persons, a victim of sexual assault who is assaulted in the victim's place of residence, or a child who is a victim of a murder attempt in the child's place of residence may receive compensation for the following expenses: (1) relocation expenses, including expenses for rental deposit, utility connections, expenses relating to moving belongings, motor vehicle mileage expenses, temporary or emergency lodging, and for an out-of-state move, expenses for transportation, lodging, and meals; and (2) housing rental expenses.
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

before.summary: For victims who qualify for relocation help (for sexual assault, only when the assault happened in the victim's home), emergency or temporary lodging is covered for up to 14 days.

rule.summary: Prescriptions and dental work for crime-related injuries are among the medical costs the program lists as covered.
