rule.source_title: OAG Medical Care Expenses

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, new child or dependent care costs are paid up to $300 per week for each child or dependent.
rule.quote: On or after July 15, 2016, $300 per week for each child or dependent.
rule.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, crime scene cleaning is capped at $2250 per victim.
rule.quote: for criminally injurious conduct that occurs on or after July 15, 2016, compensation may not exceed $2250 per victim.
rule.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

params.scope: replacing clothing, bedding, or property taken as evidence or ruined by the investigation

rule.summary: Clothing, bedding, or other property of the victim that police took as evidence or that the investigation made unusable can be replaced.
rule.quote: reasonable replacement costs for clothing, bedding, or property of the victim seized as evidence or rendered unusable as a result of the criminal investigation;
rule.source_title: Tex. Code Crim. Proc. Chapter 56B (Crime Victims' Compensation)

rule.summary: For crimes on or after July 15, 2016, replacement of seized or unusable clothing, bedding, or property is capped at $1000 per victim.
rule.quote: Under Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Article 56.32(a)(9)(G), the OAG may pay for the reasonable replacement costs as follows: (1) for criminally injurious conduct that occurs between September 1, 1995 and July 14, 2016, compensation may not exceed $750; and (2) for criminally injurious conduct that occurs on or after July 15, 2016, compensation may not exceed $1000 per victim.
rule.source_title: 1 Tex. Admin. Code 61.405 (Other Limits on Compensation)

before.summary: The program does not pay for property theft, damage, or loss. Replacing clothing, bedding, or property seized as evidence or made unusable by the investigation is a separate covered cost (see TX-SEIZED-1).

after.summary: The program does not pay for property theft, damage, or loss. Replacing clothing, bedding, or property seized as evidence or made unusable by the investigation is a separate covered cost.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for property theft, damage, or loss. Replacing clothing, bedding, or property seized as evidence or made unusable by the investigation is a separate covered cost.
rule.quote: The CVC Program cannot make payments for the following: Property theft, damage, or loss Identity theft costs Pain, suffering, or emotional distress Any cost not a direct result of the crime

added.summary: For the office to pay for the exam, the provider who did it must report the exam to law enforcement, and may collect evidence only with the permission of the victim or the victim's legal guardian.
added.quote: To be eligible for reimbursement of a medical forensic sexual assault examination, the medical service provider who performed the sexual assault forensic examination shall: (a) report the medical forensic sexual assault examination to law enforcement; and (b) only collect evidence with the permission of the victim or the legal guardian of the victim.
added.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

added.summary: The application can be completed through UOVC's online portal (the page's Online Application link goes to newclaim.crimevictim.utah.gov).

added.summary: The PDF application can be mailed to UOVC at its current mailing address on East South Temple in Salt Lake City.
added.quote: Mailing & Physical Address: 420 East South Temple, Suite 500, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Contact Us (mailing address, email, fax)

added.summary: The PDF application can be faxed to UOVC.
added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Contact Us (mailing address, email, fax)

added.summary: UOVC staff request the investigative report directly from law enforcement, so you list the agency and case number rather than attaching the report.
added.quote: The Utah Office for Victims of Crime staff must request the investigative report directly from the law enforcement agency.
added.pinpoint: Apply for Compensation, Victim Compensation Application Process
added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

added.summary: In sexual assault cases, a questionnaire completed by a sexual assault victim service provider can take the place of a police report.
added.quote: In cases of sexual assault, a questionnaire can be completed by a sexual assault victim service provider in place of a police report.
added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

added.summary: Fill in the insurance section of the application; leaving it blank delays processing.
added.quote: INSURANCE (Failure to provide this information will delay processing of the application)
added.source_title: Application for the Crime Victim Reparations Program (English)

added.summary: For a child victim, the application must be completed and signed by the child's parent or legal guardian.
added.quote: APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED FOR CHILD VICTIMS UNDER THE AGE OF EIGHTEEN MUST BE COMPLETED AND SIGNED BY THE CHILD'S PARENT OR LEGAL GUARDIAN

added.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

added.summary: Funeral or relocation costs can be paid directly to providers, or reimbursed to you when you submit the necessary documentation.

added.pinpoint: What Happens After a Decision, Funeral or Relocation Costs
added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, What Happens After a Decision

added.summary: Applications are reviewed in the order received, and processing takes about 60 to 90 days.
added.quote: Processing time is approximately 60-90 days.

added.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Apply for Compensation (application process and eligibility)

added.summary: Utah's Safe at Home Program is for survivors of sexual assault, abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking who live in Utah and are afraid they will be in physical danger if the perpetrator knows where they live. It gives them a substitute address and mail forwarding. You apply through a certified program assistant, not on your own.
added.quote: Utah’s Safe at Home Program is available to survivors of abuse, child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and sexual assault who are afraid that they will be in physical danger if their perpetrator knows where they live. The program will provide a substitute address and mail forwarding for survivors living in Utah.
added.pinpoint: Safe at Home homepage, program description; Utah Code 75E-11-102 and 75E-11-302 (UT-S16)
added.source_title: Utah Safe at Home, program homepage (Utah's address confidentiality program)

added.summary: Records the Utah Office for Victims of Crime keeps about a claim, including restitution records, can be shared only as this law allows, whatever the state open records law says.
added.quote: Notwithstanding Title 63G, Chapter 2, Government Records Access and Management Act, a confidential record, a public restitution record, and a nonpublic restitution record may only be disclosed as provided in this section.
added.pinpoint: Utah Code 75E-5-205(1)-(3); definition of confidential record at 75E-5-101(10)
added.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rule.summary: A survivor may not be charged for a medical forensic sexual assault exam, and does not have to take part in the criminal justice system or cooperate with police or prosecutors to get one.
rule.quote: A victim may not be: (a) charged for a medical forensic sexual assault examination; or (b) required to participate in the criminal justice system or cooperate with law enforcement or prosecuting attorneys as a condition of being provided a medical forensic sexual assault examination.
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: An exam provider that accepts payment from the Utah Office for Victims of Crime must take it as payment in full and may not try to collect more from the patient.
rule.quote: A sexual assault exam service provider who accepts payment from UOVC agrees to accept that payment as payment in full on behalf of the patient and may not attempt to collect additional payment from the patient.
rule.pinpoint: UOVC Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page, Payment in Full Requirement
rule.source_title: Utah Office for Victims of Crime, Sexual Assault Services Providers billing page

rule.summary: The Utah Office for Victims of Crime may pay the examiner up to $1,250 for a complete medical forensic sexual assault exam with photo documentation; this limit covers the examiner's fee only, and the exam room, lab tests, and medications are paid separately.
rule.quote: The office may pay a medical service provider who performs a medical forensic sexual assault examination: (a) up to $1,250 for a complete medical forensic sexual assault examination with photo documentation
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: The office may also pay the facility where the exam is done 50% of the exam room fee, up to $350, plus the PEHP rate or 50% of the fee for the history and physical, specimen collection, STD and pregnancy testing, and STD treatment.
rule.quote: 50% of the fee for the use of an examination room to perform a medical forensic sexual assault examination up to a maximum payment of $350
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

params.exception: or more in some cases

rule.summary: A compensation award may not exceed $25,000, including any award for a secondary victim, except for medical expenses from serious or substantial bodily injury.
rule.quote: Except as provided in Subsection (4)(b), a compensation award may not exceed $25,000 including any compensation award for a secondary victim.
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

before.summary: A primary victim can get up to 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, individual or group; more can be authorized with justification and extenuating circumstances.

after.summary: A primary victim can get up to 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, individual or group. The reparations officer can approve more if the counselor sends enough documentation to justify them and extenuating circumstances call for them.

rule.summary: A primary victim can get up to 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, individual or group. The reparations officer can approve more if the counselor sends enough documentation to justify them and extenuating circumstances call for them.
rule.quote: a primary victim of a crime is eligible for a total of 25 outpatient mental health counseling sessions, including either individual or group counseling session;
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: The office may pay up to $1,000 for reasonable and necessary travel to court, meetings with police or prosecutors, and medical, mental health, or other crime-related appointments.
rule.quote: the office may pay up to $1,000 for the reasonable and necessary costs for a victim to travel to and from:
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: Up to $1,500 may be allowed for other essential personal property such as burglar alarms, door locks, crime scene cleanup, and repair of walls and broken windows.
rule.quote: The reparations officer may allow up to $1,500 for other essential personal property such as burglar alarms, door locks, crime scene cleanup, repair of walls and broken windows.
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: Up to $5,000 may be allowed for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, and wheelchairs.
rule.quote: The reparations officer may allow up to $5,000 for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, hearing aids, and wheelchairs.
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

rule.summary: When there is no other payment source, the office may pay medical services at the PEHP fee schedule rate, or 50% of billed charges if PEHP has no fee schedule for that service.
rule.quote: if the victim does not have any collateral source to pay for medical services the office may pay: (1) the rate established by the PEHP fee schedule for medical services; or (2) 50% of the billed charges for medical services if PEHP does not have a fee schedule established for a medical service.
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

before.summary: Mental health counseling is covered when it is in a mental health treatment plan approved by a compensation specialist before any payment is made.

after.summary: Mental health counseling can be covered, but a compensation specialist must approve a mental health treatment plan for it before any payment is made.

rule.summary: Mental health counseling can be covered, but a compensation specialist must approve a mental health treatment plan for it before any payment is made.
rule.quote: mental health counseling that: (A) is set forth in a mental health treatment plan that is approved before any payment is made by a compensation specialist
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rule.summary: Lost past and future earnings from death or disability caused by the injury are covered at up to 66-2/3% of gross weekly wages or the state workers' compensation maximum.
rule.quote: actual loss of past earnings and anticipated loss of future earnings because of a death or disability resulting from the personal injury at a rate not to exceed 66-2/3% of the individual's weekly gross salary or wages or the maximum amount allowed under the state workers' compensation statute;
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.scope: child care so you or your spouse can keep working

rule.summary: Care of minor children so the victim or the victim's spouse (not both) can keep working is covered, at a weekly per-child rate set by rule.
rule.quote: care of minor children enabling a victim or spouse of a victim, but not both, to continue gainful employment at a rate per child per week as determined under rules established by the office
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

params.scope: personal property needed for your health or safety

rule.summary: Personal property necessary and essential to the victim's health or safety is covered, as defined by the office's rules.
rule.quote: personal property necessary and essential to the health or safety of the victim as defined by rules made by the office
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rule.summary: Prescription or over-the-counter medications used with medical treatment are considered while the victim is being treated by the physician.
rule.quote: The office shall only consider reimbursement of prescription or over-the-counter medications used in conjunction with medical treatment while the victim is being treated by the physician.
rule.source_title: Utah Admin. Code R270-1, Award and Reparation Standards (effective 12/08/2023)

before.summary: Economic loss does not include noneconomic detriment, which the chapter defines as pain, suffering, inconvenience, physical impairment, and other nonpecuniary damage.

after.summary: The program does not pay for harm that is not a money loss, such as pain and suffering.

rule.summary: The program does not pay for harm that is not a money loss, such as pain and suffering.
rule.quote: "Economic loss" does not include noneconomic detriment.
rule.source_title: Utah Code Title 75E, Chapter 5, Office for Victims of Crime (effective 7/1/2026)

rule.summary: The program lists sex crimes and child physical or sexual abuse among the crimes eligible for compensation.
rule.quote: Crimes that are eligible for compensation include: Aggravated Robbery Assault Domestic Violence Bigamy Child Physical or Sexual Abuse DUI with Injury or Death Elder Abuse Home Invasion Homicide Human Trafficking (Sex or Labor) Kidnapping and Unlawful Detention Protective Order Violations Sex Crimes Stalking

added.summary: The SAFE Payment Program pays only if the crime was in Virginia and evidence is collected.
added.quote: The crime occurred within the Commonwealth of Virginia . Collection of evidence took place as outlined in §19.2-165.1 of the Code of Virginia. Patients are not required to report the crime to law enforcement, nor cooperate with an investigation in order to request a Physical Evidence Recovery Kit (PERK) exam or for that exam to be paid per §19.2-165.1 (B). If the patient declines evidence collection, the claim is not eligible for reimbursement. The SAFE Payment Program does not reimburse for consults, only for collection of medical forensic evidence. Medical forensic examinations for non-acute (more than 120 hours after the crime) and/or chronic sexual abuse cases require authorization by law enforcement officer or prosecutor for payment per §19.2-165.1 (A).
added.pinpoint: VVF SAFE Payment Program page, Eligibility Requirements
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: SAFE Payment Program page

added.summary: If the crime leaves the victim totally unable to work, lost pay is paid weekly while that lasts. The rate is 66-2/3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages.
added.quote: An award made pursuant to this chapter for total loss of earnings that results directly from incapacity incurred by a crime victim shall be payable during total incapacity to the victim or to such other eligible person, at a weekly compensation rate equal to 66-2 /3 percent of the victim's average weekly wages
added.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.11:1 (Amount of award)

added.summary: The date of the crime decides how long you have to file, based on the law in effect at that time.
added.quote: The date of the crime will determine how long the victim has to file a claim with VVF based on the law in effect at the time.
added.pinpoint: VVF Eligibility page, Requirement #5: Filing Timeline Stipulations
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: Eligibility page

added.summary: For a crime on or after July 1, 2001, the Commission may give more time to file for good cause.
added.quote: For good cause shown, the Commission may extend the time for filing for a crime committed on or after July 1, 2001.
added.source_title: Va. Code § 19.2-368.5 (Filing of claims)

added.summary: Mail the completed application to the Virginia Victims Fund at P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261.
added.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: The application can be faxed to the Virginia Victims Fund at 804-823-6905.
added.quote: Submit application to P.O. Box 26927, Richmond, VA 23261 or (fax) 804-823-6905.

added.summary: Claims can be filed in person at the office of the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission, which runs the Fund; the contact page says in-person help is by appointment only.
added.quote: Claims shall be filed in the office of the Commission in person, by mail, or by electronic means in accordance with standards approved by the Commission.

added.summary: WebFile, the program's online claim system, is for victim advocates with special training.
added.quote: Victim advocates that have been through specialized training may file via WebFile, the Fund's online claims submission system.

added.source_title: Policies of the Virginia Victims Fund (revised September 2025)

added.summary: Attach all receipts, records and documents that support the expenses requested, and keep sending them for ongoing expenses.
added.quote: Applicants should attach all receipts, records and documents supporting requested expenses and continue doing so for ongoing expenses.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 2 (Returning the Application)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Attach copies of detailed, itemized billing statements from the medical providers who treated crime-related injuries.

added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Include bills, receipts, invoices and insurance documentation with the application.
added.quote: Please include any bills, receipts, invoices, and insurance documentation with the application.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form page, Helpful Tips
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund: VVF Claim Form page (form instructions)

added.summary: Once the application is deemed eligible, the survivor must provide proof of physical or emotional injury, such as health records.
added.quote: Eligible claimants must submit proof of physical and/or emotional injuries. Proof includes health records detailing a physical and/or emotional injury.
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (Physical/Emotional Injuries)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Include a written explanation of the victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation with the application; the form asks for this under the reporting factors for newer crimes.
added.quote: The victim's physical, mental, emotional and family situation (Claimants must include a written explanation of these factors with their application,)
added.pinpoint: VVF Claim Form (English, 08/12/2025), instructions p. 1 (The Crime)
added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: If there is a permanent protective order between the victim and offender, attach it.
added.quote: Is there a permanent protective order for the victim and offender? ☐ Yes ☐ No (Attach if yes.)

added.summary: To be reimbursed for clothing or bedding taken as evidence, send a copy of the evidence receipt from law enforcement and the receipt for the replacement items.

added.summary: Moving expenses need dated, signed contracts and a written justification.

added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: The application is not accepted unless the applicant signs it.

added.source_title: Virginia Victims Fund claim form (English, 08/12/2025)

added.summary: Virginia's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of the Attorney General, lets victims of sexual violence, domestic violence, stalking or child abduction use a designated address, and the office forwards their first-class mail to the actual address.

added.summary: As this section describes, the State covers the costs of certain medical care for victims of a crime committed in Vermont who have no health insurance or whose insurance does not pay for all of the care.
added.quote: As described in this section, the State shall cover the costs of certain medical care for victims of crime committed in this State without health insurance or whose health insurance does not pay for all of the care provided.
added.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

added.summary: Prosecution for lewd and lascivious conduct must begin within 6 years, so that is also the time limit to apply for it.
added.quote: (b) Prosecutions for lewd and lascivious conduct, sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(a) of this title, grand larceny, robbery, burglary, embezzlement, forgery, bribery offenses, false claims, fraud under 33 V.S.A. § 141(d), and felony tax offenses shall be commenced within six years after the commission of the offense, and not after.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

added.summary: For lewd and lascivious conduct against a child under 18, lewd or lascivious conduct with a child, and sexual exploitation of children, prosecution must begin within 40 years. That is also the time limit to apply.
added.quote: (c) Prosecutions for any of the following offenses shall be commenced within 40 years after the commission of the offense, and not after: (1) lewd and lascivious conduct alleged to have been committed against a child under 18 years of age; (2) maiming; (3) lewd or lascivious conduct with a child; (4) sexual exploitation of children under chapter 64 of this title; and (5) sexual abuse of a vulnerable adult under subsection 1379(b) of this title.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

added.summary: For other felonies and misdemeanors, prosecution must begin within 3 years. That is also the time limit to apply.
added.quote: (e) Prosecutions for other felonies and for misdemeanors shall be commenced within three years after the commission of the offense, and not after.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. § 4501, Limitation of prosecutions for certain crimes

added.summary: Mail the paper application (taped or stapled shut, or in an envelope) and any crime-related bills to the Victims Compensation Program address printed on the first page of the application.
added.quote:
Victims Compensation Program
58 South Main Street, Suite One
Waterbury, Vermont 05676-1599
added.pinpoint: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation, cover page; Application Instructions item 4
added.source_title: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation (English)

added.summary: The application can be filed online; the Application & Forms page's ONLINE Victims Compensation Application link goes to ccvcvt.org, where the applicant signs in or creates an account.
added.quote: The application is also available and can be downloaded in other languages, as well as in a fillable PDF version if you prefer to print and mail your application to us. ONLINE Victims Compensation Application
added.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Application & Forms

added.summary: Outstanding crime-related bills should be sent in with the application.
added.quote: If there are outstanding crime related bills, please send them with the application.
added.pinpoint: Victims Compensation FAQ, What happens when an application is received?
added.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation FAQ

added.summary: The application must be signed and dated in three places (authorization, repayment agreement, certification) to be eligible; missing signatures delay a claim.
added.quote:
You must sign and date in the three (3) places that follow to be eligible for Victims
Compensation.
added.pinpoint: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation, page 6
added.source_title: Application for Vermont Victims Compensation (English)

added.summary: For self-employed victims, lost wages are figured from net income shown on tax returns, 1099 forms, Schedule C, W-2s, or other proof of income.
added.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, item 3
added.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

added.summary: To be paid for more than two weeks of lost wages, the victim must submit a Physician's Report or a mental health provider's statement saying when they can return to work.
added.quote:
eligible for reimbursement of more than two weeks lost wages, a victim must
submit his/her Physician's Report, or a statement from his/her mental health
provider which states the nature of the disability and indicates when the victim
will be able to return to work.
added.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, item 4b
added.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

added.summary: Counseling is paid only after the treatment provider submits a current Mental Health Treatment Plan.
added.quote:
To be eligible for payment of counseling expenses, the treatment
provider must submit a current Mental Health Treatment Plan
added.pinpoint: CCVS Victims Compensation Mental Health Policy, section 2, Treatment Plans
added.source_title: CCVS Victims Compensation Mental Health Policy (amended 8/12/2024)

added.summary: A security deposit the victim already paid is reimbursed after the victim submits the landlord's receipt and a signed copy of the lease.
added.quote:
we will
reimburse the victim for the security deposit upon the victim's
submission of a landlord's receipt and a signed copy of the lease.
added.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation, Security Deposits
added.source_title: CCVS Policy for Housing and Relocation

added.summary: For the Sexual Assault Program, the signed Sexual Assault Billing Form completed at the exam serves as the application.
added.quote: The signed Sexual Assault Billing Form serves as the application to open a claim
added.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, How to access the Program?
added.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

added.summary: The Secretary of State's Safe at Home program offers an address confidentiality service and a protected records service to survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and human trafficking. You can apply online on the program page, on your own or with help from an Applicant Assistant at a local advocacy agency.
added.quote: Safe at Home provides an address confidentiality service and a protected records service. The program serves survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, providers of legally protected healthcare (reproductive and gender-affirming care), and patients of legally protected healthcare.
added.pinpoint: Vermont SOS Safe at Home page, opening paragraph; statutory basis 15 V.S.A. §§ 1150 to 1160
added.source_title: Vermont Secretary of State, Safe at Home Address Confidentiality Program page

added.summary: Every document the Victims Compensation Board reviews to decide a compensation application is confidential and cannot be disclosed without the victim's consent, except as the statute allows.
added.quote: (a) All documents reviewed by the Victims Compensation Board for purposes of approving an application for compensation shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed without the consent of the victim except as provided in this section and subsection 7043(c) of this title.
added.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rule.summary: If the survivor's health coverage leaves a co-payment, coinsurance, deductible, or other cost-sharing for the exam, the Fund pays that share directly to the provider, so the survivor does not owe it.
rule.quote: If the victim's health coverage does not cover all of the medical care provided pursuant to this section and the victim would otherwise be responsible for any co-payment, coinsurance, deductible, or other cost-sharing, the Fund shall pay the victim's share directly to the health care facility or provider.
rule.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rule.summary: Providers must bill the survivor's health plan, Medicaid, or Medicare for the exam first. If the survivor is uninsured or the plan denies the claim, the Fund pays Vermont providers 60 percent of billed charges and the provider may not bill the survivor for the balance.
rule.quote: Health care facilities and health care providers shall bill the victim's health insurance plan, Medicaid, Medicare, or another health benefit plan, as applicable, for the services described in subsection (b) of this section. If the victim does not have health coverage or if the victim's health benefit plan denies the claim, the Fund shall reimburse health care facilities and health care providers located in Vermont as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 9402 at 60 percent of the billed charges for these claims, and the health care provider or facility shall not bill any balance to the crime victim.
rule.source_title: 32 V.S.A. § 1407, Costs to be borne by the State

rule.summary: Through the CCVS Sexual Assault Program, the initial sexual assault medical exam is covered, including evidence collection, STI and HIV screening and prophylaxis, pregnancy testing, and treatment of related injuries.
rule.quote: Resources are available to pay for the initial sexual assault medical examination to include: collection of evidence STI (sexually transmitted infections) and HIV screening prophylaxis pregnancy testing treatment of related injuries
rule.pinpoint: CCVS Sexual Assault Program page, What is covered?
rule.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

rule.summary: Covered medical costs include individual or family psychological, psychiatric, or mental health counseling, and replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, or prosthetic devices taken, lost, or destroyed during the crime.
rule.quote: Medical or medically related expenses may include, but are not limited to, the costs of individual or family psychological, psychiatric, or mental health counseling and the costs of replacing or repairing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures, or any prosthetic devices that were taken, lost, or destroyed during the commission of the crime.
rule.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rule.summary: Lost wages are paid at 85% of the victim's gross wages at the time of the loss.
rule.quote: lost wages will be paid at 85% of the victim's gross wages at the time of the loss.
rule.pinpoint: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages, para. 2
rule.source_title: CCVS Policy for Reimbursement of Lost Wages (amended 9/8/2025)

rule.summary: Pecuniary loss covers medical or medically related expenses, lost wages, and other expenses the Board finds became necessary as a direct result of the crime.
rule.quote: "Pecuniary loss" means, in the case of a victim, the amount of medical or medically related expenses, loss of wages, and any other expenses that the Board feels became necessary as a direct result of the crime.
rule.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

params.scope: the separate Sexual Assault Program

rule.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Sexual Assault Program

rule.summary: The program pays only losses not covered by medical, hospitalization, or disability insurance or workers' compensation.
rule.quote: (A) that is not covered by medical, hospitalization, or disability insurance or workers' compensation
rule.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

before.summary: An application is denied if the victim broke a Vermont criminal law that caused or contributed to the victim's injuries.

after.summary: A claim must be denied if the victim broke a Vermont criminal law that caused or helped cause the victim's injuries.

rule.summary: A claim must be denied if the victim broke a Vermont criminal law that caused or helped cause the victim's injuries.
rule.quote: (2) The victim violated a criminal law of this State that caused or contributed to the victim's injuries or death.
rule.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

rule.summary: Sexual assault is listed among the crimes that may qualify for compensation.
rule.quote: Robbery Sexual Assault Stalking
rule.pinpoint: CCVS Eligibility page, Types of crimes that may qualify
rule.source_title: Vermont CCVS, Victims Compensation Eligibility

rule.summary: Injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, or emotional harm resulting from the crime.
rule.quote: "Injury" means actual bodily harm or pregnancy, or emotional harm resulting from the crime.
rule.source_title: 13 V.S.A. chapter 167 (Crime Victims), full text incl. subchapter 1, Compensation to Victims of Crime

added.source_title: RCW 7.68.140 (confidentiality of victim claim files and records)

rule.summary: To get the exam, a patient does not have to pay, use their own insurance, report to police, or file a compensation application.
rule.quote: In order to receive an examination, patients are not required to: Pay for the examination Use their own insurance Report to police File a crime victim's application.

rule.summary: Monthly wage loss payments are 60 percent of the victim's monthly wage, up to 100 percent of the state's average monthly wage.

rule.summary: A victim who was not working at the time of the crime gets no lost wage support unless they worked at least 12 weeks in the 6 months before the crime.
rule.quote: If the victim was not gainfully employed at the time of the criminal act, no financial support for lost wages will be paid to the victim or any beneficiaries, unless the victim was gainfully employed for a total of at least twelve weeks in the six months preceding the date of the criminal act.
rule.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rule.summary: If the employer keeps paying the victim's wages, no lost wage support is paid.
rule.quote: If a victim's employer continues to pay the victim's wages that he or she was earning at the time of the crime, the victim shall not receive any financial support for lost wages.
rule.source_title: RCW 7.68.070 (benefits, amounts, limitations)

rule.summary: Counseling for immediate family members is covered under the victim's sexual assault claim.

rule.quote: When the injury to any victim is so serious as to require the victim being taken from the place of injury to a place of treatment, reasonable transportation costs to and from the nearest place of proper treatment to a reasonable location of the victim's choice shall be reimbursed by the department as part of the victim's total claim under RCW 7.68.070 (1).

rule.summary: A health care provider that asks the state SAFE Fund to pay for a sexual assault forensic exam may not bill the survivor (or the survivor's guardian) for any of the exam costs.

rule.quote: The health care provider may not bill the victim or the family of the victim for the cost of a SANE exam. Should a victim receive a bill for a SANE exam, they must contact the health care provider immediately and ask them to submit the bill to the SAFE Fund.
rule.source_title: Wisconsin DOJ: Sexual Assault Forensic Exam (SAFE) Fund

before.summary: The Wisconsin Department of Justice pays exam costs directly to the health care provider through the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Fund. Exam costs cover the evidence exam plus STD testing and prevention, HIV prophylaxis and STD medication given during the exam; the fund does not cover follow-up medical treatment. The fund does not pay if the survivor both authorizes insurance billing and cooperates with police.

after.summary: For a sexual assault that happened in Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Department of Justice pays exam costs directly to the health care provider through the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Fund. Exam costs are the evidence exam plus testing, prevention and medicine for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and medicine to prevent HIV, given or prescribed during the exam. The fund pays only these exam costs, not other medical treatment or follow-up visits. It does not pay if the provider is allowed to bill insurance and the survivor (or a guardian) has reported to police or helped their investigation.

rule.summary: For a sexual assault that happened in Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Department of Justice pays exam costs directly to the health care provider through the Sexual Assault Forensic Examination (SAFE) Fund. Exam costs are the evidence exam plus testing, prevention and medicine for sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) and medicine to prevent HIV, given or prescribed during the exam. The fund pays only these exam costs, not other medical treatment or follow-up visits. It does not pay if the provider is allowed to bill insurance and the survivor (or a guardian) has reported to police or helped their investigation.
rule.quote: the department shall make an award under this section to a health care provider who conducts an examination to gather evidence regarding a sex offense to reimburse the health care provider only for the examination costs
rule.source_title: Wis. Stat. ch. 949, Awards for the Victims of Crimes (subch. I crime victim compensation; subch. II sexual assault forensic examination compensation)

rule.summary: For the forensic exam, no police report is needed: the SAFE Fund may not refuse payment because the survivor does not cooperate with law enforcement or because there is no investigation or prosecution.
rule.quote: The department may not refuse to make an award under this section because the victim or the guardian of the victim does not cooperate with a law enforcement agency regarding the sex offense, or due to lack of an investigation or prosecution of the sex offense.

added.summary: The Secretary of State's Address Confidentiality Program is designed to help victims of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking and human trafficking deal with government agencies without risking that their home address gets out. rule.quote: The commissioner may not approve an award of compensation if the criminally injurious conduct upon which the claim is based was not reported to a law-enforcement officer or agency or, in the case of sexual offense, the victim did not undergo a forensic medical examination, within 96 hours after the occurrence of the conduct, unless it is determined that good cause existed for the failure to report the conduct or undergo a forensic medical examination within the 96-hour period: Provided , That reporting to a law-enforcement officer or agency or a forensic medical examination is not required if the victim is a juvenile in order for a commissioner to approve an award of compensation

params.scope: filing of a criminal charge, not just a report; exceptions for unknown offender, juvenile claimant, or adult claimant who did not block charges where law enforcement confirms a crime occurred

before.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown, when the claimant was a juvenile, or when an adult claimant did not cause the lack of charges and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.

params.scope: filing of a criminal charge, not just a report; exceptions for unknown offender, juvenile claimant, or adult claimant who did not block charges where law enforcement confirms a crime occurred

after.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown or the claimant was a juvenile. It is also not required for an adult claimant when no charges were filed for reasons other than the claimant's own wish and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.

rule.summary: Beyond the police report, a criminal charge generally has to be filed. It is not required when the offender is unknown or the claimant was a juvenile. It is also not required for an adult claimant when no charges were filed for reasons other than the claimant's own wish and law enforcement confirms the evidence supports that a crime occurred. A conviction is not required.
rule.quote: The filing of a criminal charge shall be a prerequisite for receipt of compensation unless it is determined that no charges were filed due to the identity of the perpetrator being unknown: Provided, That no criminal charges need be filed if: (1) The claimant is an adult at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred and no criminal charges were filed for reasons other than the desire of the claimant and a law-enforcement agency confirms that the available evidence supports a finding that a crime occurred; or (2) the claimant was a juvenile at the time the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-18 (Effect of no criminal charges)

before.summary: An award may be denied or reduced if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or the claim investigator.

after.summary: A commissioner may deny a claim, reduce an award, or reconsider an approved claim if the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement or the claim investigator.

rule.summary: A commissioner may deny a claim, reduce an award, or reconsider an approved claim if the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with law enforcement or the claim investigator.
rule.quote: A commissioner, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law-enforcement agencies or the claim investigator, may deny a claim, reduce an award of compensation, or reconsider a claim already approved.
rule.source_title: W. Va. Code 14-2A-14 (Denial, reduction, maximum award)

rule.quote: Murder Other Violent Crimes Robbery Sexual Assault Kidnapping Human Trafficking
rule.pinpoint: Eligibility page, Crimes Resulting in Personal Injury

added.summary: For a catastrophic injury, the division may award up to $10,000 more than the maximum award, to cover future lost wages, special medical needs, and other special help the injury requires.
added.quote: In addition to the maximum award authorized in subsection (d) of this section, in the case of catastrophic injury the division may award an additional amount not to exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) to the victim to cover future lost wages, special medical needs and any other special assistance needed as a result of the injury.
added.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

added.summary: Losses that happen more than 24 months after the injury or the discovery of the crime are not paid.
added.quote: Compensation shall only be awarded for economic losses occurring within a twenty-four (24) month period from the date of the injury or discovery of the crime.
added.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

added.quote: Return to: Division of Victim Services, 320 W. 25th Street, 2nd Floor, Cheyenne, WY 82002.

added.summary: Attach itemized copies of the bills being claimed.
added.quote: Attach itemized copies of any bills

added.summary: Attach copies of bills, estimates, and receipts for the expenses claimed.
added.quote: Attach copies of bills, estimates, and receipts

added.summary: By statute, information in victims' compensation claim files and records that is covered by a confidentiality privilege under Wyoming law stays confidential and is not open to public inspection. It is also shielded from legal process and cannot be used as evidence in any proceeding without the consent of the person who gave it.
added.quote: Information contained in the claim files and records of victims, which are subject to any privilege of confidentiality under Wyoming law, shall remain confidential and shall not be open to public inspection. The information shall be immune from legal process and shall not, without the consent of the person furnishing the information, be admitted as evidence or used for any purpose in any action, suit or other judicial, legislative or administrative proceeding.
added.source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, W.S. 1-40-101 to 1-40-119 (copy posted by DVS)

before.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000. A separate catastrophic injury award can add more (see notes).

after.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000.

rule.summary: The maximum award to any victim or dependent is $15,000.
rule.quote: the maximum individual award of compensation paid to any victim or dependent shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000.00).
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

rule.summary: Counseling and other losses for an associated victim (such as a family or household member) are limited to $1,500 per year and $4,500 for the life of the claim, and count toward the primary victim's $15,000 award.
rule.quote: Associated victims may be eligible for compensation with regard to counseling and other economic losses in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00 per year for a maximum of $4,500.00 for the life of the claim (effective July 1, 2019). The compensation paid to an associated victim is included in the primary victim's award of $15,000.00.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Payment Threshold on Associated Victim Claims
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Losses are paid only if they happen within 24 months of the injury or discovery of the crime. The division can extend this by 12 months for mental health counseling, for a total of 36 months.

after.summary: The division can extend the 24-month limit by 12 more months for mental health counseling, for 36 months in all.

rule.summary: The division can extend the 24-month limit by 12 more months for mental health counseling, for 36 months in all.
rule.quote: However, the division may extend the twenty-four (24) month period to allow compensation for mental health counseling and care occurring within an additional twelve (12) month period for a total of thirty-six (36) months.
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-109, Standards for compensation (2025, via Justia)

rule.summary: For counseling to be covered, the first session must be within 1 year of the crime; for juvenile victims reported after the filing period, within 1 year of the report.
rule.quote: The first counseling session must be within one (1) year of the date of the crime. The first counseling session for juvenile victims (crimes reported past the one year filing requirement) must be within one year of reporting date of the crime.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Mental Health Expenses
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage, for up to 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months total. The victim must have been employed at the time of the crime, and sick and vacation leave count as other sources.

after.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage. The limit is 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months in all.

rule.summary: Lost wages are paid at no more than the federal minimum wage. The limit is 8 hours a day, 40 hours a week, or 173 hours a month, for up to 3 months in all.
rule.quote: Maximum amount must not exceed the federal minimum hourly wage for eight (8) hours per day, or forty (40) hours per week, or one hundred seventy-three (173) hours per month up to three (3) months total.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Loss of Earnings, Financial Limits
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

params.scope: trips of at least 10 miles outside your home community

rule.summary: Travel is covered when a victim has to go at least 10 miles outside their home community for counseling, medical treatment not available locally, or to give a victim impact statement at sentencing. Mileage is paid at the state rate, with no separate cap beyond the total award.
rule.quote: Expenses incurred when required to travel at least ten (10) miles outside the home community to receive the following services.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Travel Expenses
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground (see the relocation caps).

after.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground.

rule.summary: Relocation can be covered when the crime happened in the victim's home and returning would do greater harm, and the policy lists sexual assaults as an example. A lower cap applies to this ground.
rule.quote: Victim may need to relocate if the crime scene was the home of the victim and returning would do greater harm to the victim.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Relocation, Requirements
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.

after.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other elective electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.

rule.summary: Phones, laptops, tablets, and other elective electronic devices are not covered, unless good cause is shown.
rule.quote: Cell phones, laptops, tablets, and any other elective electronic devices are not covered under the CVCP, unless good cause is shown for reimbursement.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Replacement of Personal Property Seized as Evidence, Exemptions
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible for replacement.

after.summary: The benefit that replaces things police took as evidence does not cover things that were damaged or ruined in the crime.

rule.summary: The benefit that replaces things police took as evidence does not cover things that were damaged or ruined in the crime.
rule.quote: Items destroyed or damaged during the crime are not eligible.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Replacement of Personal Property Seized as Evidence
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

params.extension: The division may extend the time for good cause shown.
or later if the division allows more time for good cause

rule.summary: Apply within 1 year of the injury. The division can allow more time for good cause.
rule.quote: The application for compensation is filed with the division within one (1) year after the date of the injury to or death of the victim, or within any extension of time the division allows for good cause shown
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-106, Eligibility for compensation (2025, via Justia)

before.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical, and the claimant must cooperate with law enforcement. The statute sets no fixed number of days and lists no alternative to a police report.

after.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical. The claimant must also cooperate with law enforcement.

rule.summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement as soon as practical. The claimant must also cooperate with law enforcement.
rule.quote: The appropriate law enforcement authorities were notified of the criminal act allegedly causing the injury to or death of the victim as soon as practical under the circumstance after perpetration of the offense and the claimant cooperates with appropriate law enforcement authorities with respect to the crime for which compensation is sought
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-106, Eligibility for compensation (2025, via Justia)

params.applies_to: mental health counseling only

params.scope: mental health counseling only

rule.summary: Program policy also accepts a valid order of protection instead of a police report, but only for mental health counseling claims. An ex parte (temporary) order is not enough.
rule.quote: A valid Order of Protection (Mental Health Counseling Only). A claim cannot be approved based on an Ex Parte Order of Protection.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation Guidelines and Policy (eff. Jan 1, 2025), Primary Victim Eligibility
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Guidelines and Policy (effective January 1, 2025)

before.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed. The crime only has to be reported to law enforcement.

after.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed to be eligible.

rule.summary: No arrest, prosecution, or conviction is needed to be eligible.
rule.quote: No arrest, prosecution, nor conviction is necessary to be eligible.
rule.pinpoint: WY DVS Compensation FAQ, Does There Have To Be An Arrest Or Conviction
rule.source_title: Wyoming DVS Crime Victim Compensation Frequently Asked Questions

before.summary: The division can make an emergency award of up to $1,000 before a hearing if waiting would cause undue hardship. It is subtracted from the final award.

after.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.

rule.summary: An emergency award can be no more than $1,000.
rule.quote: The amount of an emergency award to an applicant shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
rule.source_title: W.S. 1-40-111, Emergency awards; limitation (2025, via Justia)
